articles.title: Geometric points detect elements when the generic fiber is reduced
articles.statement:
An element of a torsion-free algebra that vanishes under every algebra
homomorphism into an algebraically closed field is zero, provided the
tensor product with the fraction field is reduced and finite.

This is the Nullstellensatz-style statement that points detect functions:
it is used to show maps of schemes are determined by their values on
geometric points, to pass from vanishing on fibers to vanishing globally,
and to prove reducedness from pointwise vanishing.

articles.title: A tensor vanishing at all pairs of algebraic points is zero
articles.statement:
If the scalar-extended evaluation map is injective, a tensor vanishing at
all pairs of selected algebraic points is zero. The algebra and the point
index may be infinite; no closedness or perfection assumption is needed.

articles.title: Algebra maps from relation-preserving generator assignments
articles.statement:
A unital, multiplicatively consistent assignment on generators extends to
an algebra homomorphism when it preserves every finite linear relation.

The index family need not be injective or finite; the target may have zero
divisors. This preserves the full statement of the source theorem
`exists_algHom_adjoin_range_apply_eq_of_forall_sum_smul_eq_zero_of_algebra`.

articles.title: Extending a ring character via prime-subfield-valued linear forms
articles.statement:
A ring character extends to the algebra generated by another ring image
when its kernel contains the first kernel and a separating family of linear
forms takes prime-subfield values on that image.

The ambient algebra may be noncommutative, and the separating family may be
infinite. The prime subfield is `⊥ : Subfield κ`, in any characteristic.
This is the source theorem
`exists_algHom_adjoin_range_apply_eq_of_forall_apply_mem_bot`.

articles.title: Lifting maps to algebraically closed fields along integral extensions
articles.statement:
A homomorphism from `R` to an algebraically closed field extends to an
integral extension `S` with any prescribed prime kernel lying over `ker χ`.

This is the key step for extending points of a scheme along integral
morphisms, for going-up arguments, and for lifting maps through integral
closures: the kernel control `RingHom.ker χ' = Q` says the lifted map has
exactly the prescribed residue behavior.

articles.title: Counting algebra homomorphisms from an étale algebra
articles.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field, the number of algebra homomorphisms
from an étale algebra to the base field equals its rank.

articles.title: Counting algebra homomorphisms of a finite reduced algebra
articles.statement:
A finite reduced algebra over an algebraically closed field has
`finrank` many algebra homomorphisms to the field.

articles.title: Universal-property criterion for a pushout square of algebras
articles.statement:
A square of algebras is a pushout when it satisfies the universal
property for algebra homomorphisms: for every `R'`-algebra `T` and every
`g : S →+* T` compatible with the maps from `R`, there is a unique
`R'`-algebra map `S' →ₐ[R'] T` extending `g`. The rings may lie in
independent universes; it suffices to quantify `T` in the maximum of the
universes of `S`, `R'`, and `S'`.

This is the hands-on criterion for recognizing pushouts (tensor products)
without computing the tensor product: it is used to identify fiber
products of schemes, base changes, and tensor-product decompositions from
their mapping properties.

articles.title: Iterated derivation of a power when $D\varepsilon = r\varepsilon^2$
articles.statement:
If `D epsilon = r • epsilon²`, then the `n`th iterate of `D` on `epsilon^m` has
coefficient `r^n` times the ascending factorial of `m`. The coefficient is not cancelled,
so the formula remains valid in positive characteristic.

articles.title: Factorial-normalized iterated Leibniz rule
articles.statement: The factorial-normalized iterated Leibniz rule for a rational derivation.

articles.title: Leibniz rule for iterated derivations
articles.statement:
Leibniz's rule for an iterated derivation. The natural weights are not cancelled, so the
identity remains valid in positive characteristic.

articles.title: Differential of a transcendental element is nonzero
articles.statement: The differential of a transcendental separable element is nonzero.

articles.title: Kähler differentials are unique multiples of dt for transcendental t
articles.statement:
Every Kähler differential is uniquely a scalar multiple of the
differential of a transcendental separable element.

articles.title: Differential of a transcendental element spans the differentials
articles.statement:
The differential of a transcendental separable element spans the Kähler
differentials.

articles.title: Smooth curves have discrete valuation rings as local rings
articles.statement:
The localization at a maximal ideal of a standard smooth algebra of
relative dimension `1` over a field is a discrete valuation ring.

articles.title: Localizations of smooth algebras are integrally closed domains
articles.statement:
The localization of a smooth algebra at a prime is a domain and
integrally closed.

articles.title: Localizations of étale algebras are integrally closed domains
articles.statement:
The localization of an étale algebra at a prime is a domain and
integrally closed.

articles.title: Local rings with principal regular maximal ideal are domains
articles.statement:
A Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by a single
regular element is a domain.

articles.title: The norm commutes with base change
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $A'$ and $B$ be commutative rings, where
$A'$ and $B$ are $A$-algebras and $B$ is a free $A$-module of finite rank. Then for every
$b \in B$, the image of the norm $N_{B/A}(b)$ under the structure map $A \to A'$ equals the norm
$N_{(A' \otimes_A B)/A'}(1 \otimes b)$ of $1 \otimes b$ in the $A'$-algebra $A' \otimes_A B$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`, Lemma 4.49 (norm clause).

articles.title: Norm on a subsingleton algebra is one
articles.statement:
The norm on a subsingleton algebra is `1`: left multiplication by any
element is the identity map on a subsingleton module, hence has determinant
`1`.

articles.title: Norm in a product algebra is the product of norms
articles.statement:
The norm of a product algebra is the product of the norms of the
components: left multiplication by `(x₁, x₂)` is the product map of the
left multiplications, and the determinant of a product map is the product
of the determinants.

articles.title: The trace commutes with base change
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $A'$ and $B$ be commutative rings, where
$A'$ and $B$ are $A$-algebras and $B$ is a free $A$-module of finite rank. Then for every
$b \in B$, the image of the trace $T_{B/A}(b)$ under the structure map $A \to A'$ equals the trace
$T_{(A' \otimes_A B)/A'}(1 \otimes b)$ of $1 \otimes b$ in the $A'$-algebra $A' \otimes_A B$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`, Lemma 4.49 (trace clause).

articles.title: Functoriality of point derivations in the coefficient module
articles.statement: Functoriality of point derivations in the coefficient module.

articles.title: Point derivations of an algebra
articles.statement:
Point derivations at a `k`-point `ev` of a `k`-algebra `A` with values
in a `k`-module `M`.

articles.title: Étale algebras are detected by the discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a
field $K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. Then the discriminant of $b$
over $K$ is nonzero if and only if $R$ is étale over $K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Lemma 12.18.

articles.title: Discriminant and nondegeneracy of the trace form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a
field $K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. For $z \in R$ write
$\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$.
Then the discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero if and only if the trace form
$(x, y) \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$ of $R$ over $K$ is nondegenerate.

articles.title: Étale algebras have nonzero discriminant
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field
$K$ that is étale over $K$. Then for every $K$-basis $b$ of $R$ indexed by a finite set, the
discriminant of $b$ over $K$ is nonzero.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Lemma 12.18, one direction.

articles.title: A nonzero discriminant forces étaleness
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative algebra over a field
$K$ and let $b$ be a $K$-basis of $R$ indexed by a finite set. If the discriminant of $b$ over
$K$ is nonzero, then $R$ is étale over $K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Lemma 12.18, one direction.

articles.title: A nondegenerate trace form forces the algebra to be reduced
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative
algebra over a field $K$. For $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the
$K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$, taken to be $0$ when $R$ is infinite-dimensional
over $K$. If the trace form $(x, y) \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$ of $R$ over $K$ is
nondegenerate, then $R$ is reduced, that is, its only nilpotent element is $0$.

Every nilpotent element lies in the kernel of the trace form, hence is zero.

articles.title: Étale criterion via semisimple base change
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $\Omega$ an
algebraically closed field extension of $K$, and $A$ a commutative $K$-algebra that is
finite-dimensional over $K$. If the ring $\Omega \otimes_K A$ is semisimple, then $A$ is étale
over $K$.

articles.title: Nilpotent elements pair to zero under the trace form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative algebra
over a field $K$, and for $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of the
$K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$, taken to be $0$ when $R$ is infinite-dimensional
over $K$. If $x, y \in R$ and $x$ is nilpotent, then the trace form of $R$ over $K$ vanishes at
$(x, y)$, that is, $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy) = 0$.

Multiplication by a nilpotent element is a nilpotent endomorphism, whose trace vanishes.

articles.title: The trace form is invariant under algebra isomorphisms
articles.statement:
For a commutative algebra $A$
over a field $K$ and $z \in A$, write $\operatorname{Tr}_{A/K}(z)$ for the trace of the $K$-linear
map given by multiplication by $z$, taken to be $0$ when $A$ is infinite-dimensional over $K$. Let
$R$ and $S$ be commutative algebras over $K$ and let $e : R \to S$ be an isomorphism of
$K$-algebras. Then for all $x, y \in R$ we have
$\operatorname{Tr}_{S/K}(e(x)\,e(y)) = \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$, that is, $e$ carries the
trace form of $R$ over $K$ to the trace form of $S$ over $K$.

articles.title: Trace form criterion for étale algebras
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a finite-dimensional commutative
algebra over a field $K$, and for $z \in R$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(z)$ for the trace of
the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$. Then the trace form
$(x, y) \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{R/K}(xy)$ of $R$ over $K$ is nondegenerate if and only if $R$
is étale over $K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Theorem 5.20.

articles.title: Trace form of a finite product of algebras
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, and for a
finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebra $A$ and $z \in A$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{A/K}(z)$
for the trace of the $K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$. Let $(A_i)_{i \in I}$ be a
family of finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebras indexed by a finite set $I$, and let
$P = \prod_{i \in I} A_i$. Then for all $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ and $y = (y_i)_{i \in I}$ in $P$,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{P/K}(xy) = \sum_{i \in I} \operatorname{Tr}_{A_i/K}(x_i y_i)$, that is, the
trace form of $P$ over $K$ is the sum of the trace forms of the factors.

articles.title: Trace on a finite product of algebras
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, and for a finite-dimensional
commutative $K$-algebra $A$ and $z \in A$ write $\operatorname{Tr}_{A/K}(z)$ for the trace of the
$K$-linear map given by multiplication by $z$. Let $(A_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of
finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebras indexed by a finite set $I$, and let
$P = \prod_{i \in I} A_i$. Then for every $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ in $P$,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{P/K}(x) = \sum_{i \in I} \operatorname{Tr}_{A_i/K}(x_i)$.

articles.title: Field-with-domain tensor products over an algebraically closed field
articles.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field, the tensor product of a field with a
domain is a domain.

articles.title: Tensor products of domains over an algebraically closed field
articles.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field, the tensor product of a finite-type
domain with a domain is a domain.

articles.title: Reduced algebras stay reduced under base change over a perfect field
articles.statement:
Tensoring a reduced algebra with a field extension over a perfect field
preserves reducedness.

articles.title: A set with a p-ordering is infinite
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a
nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $S \subseteq R$. If some sequence in $R$ is a
$\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, then $S$ is infinite.

articles.title: Building a p-ordering
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime
ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the
stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. If $S$ is
infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every
$x \in S$, then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$.

articles.title: Each term of a p-ordering attains the least valuation
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain,
$\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a
$\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with
respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then for every $n$, $v_n(a_n)$ is the least element of
$\{v_n(x) : x \in S\}$.

articles.title: The stage-zero condition of a p-ordering is automatic
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain,
$\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in
$R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$
and $(a_n)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite,
$a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n \ge 1$ and every $x \in S$.

Since every stage-zero valuation is $0$, the term $a_0$ may be any element of $S$.

articles.title: Unfolding the definition of a p-ordering
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$
a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and
write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and
$(a_n)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite,
$a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.

articles.title: Bhargava p-ordering
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal
of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. Write $v_n(x)$ for the stage-$n$
prefix-product valuation of $x \in R$ with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$, the multiplicity
of $\mathfrak p$ in the ideal generated by $\prod_{k < n} (x - a_k)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a
$\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ when $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and
$v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.

## Sources

- Takeda, Introduction, lines 52-60.

articles.title: Terms of a p-ordering lie in the set
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a
nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of
$S$. Then $a_n \in S$ for every $n$.

articles.title: Minimality of a p-ordering
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime
ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, and write
$v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$.
Then $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.

articles.title: The stage-zero valuation vanishes
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a
nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. For every $x \in R$, the
stage-$0$ prefix-product valuation of $x$ with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$ is $0$: the
product is empty, so the ideal is all of $R$.

articles.title: Prefix-product valuation
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime
ideal of $R$ and $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. For $n \in \mathbb N$ and $x \in R$, the
stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation of $x$ is the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in the principal
ideal generated by $\prod_{k < n} (x - a_k)$: the largest $m \in \mathbb N$ such that
$\mathfrak p^m$ divides this ideal, or $\infty$ if every power of $\mathfrak p$ divides it.

## Sources

- Takeda, Introduction, lines 52-60.

articles.title: Dedekind domains are the integrally closed Noetherian domains of dimension at most one
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension
at most one if and only if $A$ is a Dedekind domain.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Definition 2.10, characterization form.

articles.title: Dedekind domains as the Noetherian domains where to contain is to divide
articles.statement:
An integral
domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and
$J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Theorem 3.23, conditions (1) and (5).

articles.title: Dedekind domains via principal products
articles.statement:
An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if
and only if for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a
nonzero principal ideal.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Theorem 3.23(6), corrected: the recorded condition omits both nonzero qualifiers, which makes it vacuous (take $J = 0$).

articles.title: Dedekind domains from two generators with one prescribed
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$ with
$I = (a, b)$. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.

## Sources

- converse of ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Theorem 3.22, derived independently.

articles.title: Dedekind domains from principal quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for
every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a
Dedekind domain.

## Sources

- converse of ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 3.18, derived independently.

articles.title: Equivalent characterizations of Dedekind domains
articles.statement:
For an integral domain $A$, the
following are equivalent: (1) $A$ is a Dedekind domain; (2) $A$ is Noetherian and, for all
ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$; (3) for every
nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal
ideal.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Theorem 3.23, conditions (1), (5) and (6), with (6) corrected by the two nonzero qualifiers.

articles.title: Principal quotients give discrete valuation rings at nonzero primes
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an
integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a
principal ideal ring. Then for every nonzero prime ideal $P$ of $A$, the localization $A_P$ is a
discrete valuation ring.

The image of $P$ in $A/P^2$ is principal, generated by the image of some $\pi \in P$, so
$P \subseteq (\pi) + P^2$. Hence the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A_P$ satisfies
$\mathfrak{m} \subseteq (\pi) + \mathfrak{m}^2$, and Nakayama's lemma gives
$\mathfrak{m} = (\pi)$.

articles.title: DVR localizations in a Noetherian domain
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then
the localizations $A_P$ at all nonzero prime ideals $P$ of $A$ are discrete valuation rings if
and only if $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Proposition 2.9.

articles.title: Domains with principal quotients are Noetherian
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain such that
for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is
a Noetherian ring.

For a nonzero ideal $I$, pick a nonzero $a \in I$; the image of $I$ in the principal ideal ring
$A/(a)$ is principal, and lifting a generator to some $b \in I$ shows $I = (a, b)$, so $I$ is
finitely generated.

articles.title: Two generators with one prescribed give principal quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral
domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$
with $I = (a, b)$. Then for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$, the quotient ring $A/I$ is a
principal ideal ring.

For a nonzero ideal $I$, an ideal $J$ of $A/I$ has preimage $J'$ in $A$ containing $I$; pick a
nonzero $a \in I$, write $J' = (a, b)$, and the image of $b$ generates $J$ since the image of $a$
is zero.

articles.title: Quotients of Dedekind domains by nonzero ideals are principal ideal rings
articles.statement:
Every quotient
of a Dedekind domain by a nonzero ideal is a principal ideal ring.

articles.title: Residue field of the completion
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let
$\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ be the valuation
ring of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of $K$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$.
This is the ring isomorphism
$\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p} \cong A/\mathfrak{p}$ that sends the residue
class of the image of each $a \in A$ to the class of $a$ modulo $\mathfrak{p}$. It is induced by
the residue map $A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$ (the canonical map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ followed by the quotient map), which is surjective with kernel
$\mathfrak{p}$.

articles.title: Residue map to the completed residue field
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ be
the valuation ring of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of $K$, with maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$. The residue map is the ring homomorphism
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$ obtained by composing the canonical map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ with the quotient map
$\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p} \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$.

articles.title: Finite residue field of adic completion integers
articles.statement:
The residue field of the adic completion integers at a place with finite
residue field is finite.

articles.title: Kernel of the completed residue map
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$,
let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ be the
valuation ring of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of $K$, with maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$. The kernel of the residue map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$, the canonical map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ followed by the quotient map, is $\mathfrak{p}$.

articles.title: Extension of a prime to the completed valuation ring
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$, let $v$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the valuation
ring of the $v$-adic completion of $K$. Then the ideal of $\mathcal{O}_v$ generated by the image of
$v$ under the canonical map $A \to \mathcal{O}_v$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal{O}_v$.

articles.title: Surjectivity of the completed residue map
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ be
the valuation ring of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of $K$, with maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$. The residue map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}$, the canonical map
$A \to \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ followed by the quotient map, is surjective.

articles.title: Localization at a prime as a preimage of the completed valuation ring
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $v$ be a height-one prime of $R$, and let
$\mathcal{O}_v$ be the valuation ring of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then the
localization $R_v$ of $R$ at $v$, viewed as a subring of $K$, is the preimage of $\mathcal{O}_v$
under the canonical embedding $K \to K_v$.

articles.title: Conductor of a monogenic subalgebra
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative
$R$-algebra and $x \in S$. The conductor ideal of the subalgebra $R[x]$ of $S$ generated by $x$
equals the conductor of $x$, the ideal of all $a \in S$ such that $ab \in R[x]$ for every
$b \in S$.

articles.title: Finiteness of an overring via its conductor
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral domain with
fraction field $K$, and let $T$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $K$. Then the conductor ideal of the
image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is nonzero if and only if $T$ is
finitely generated as an $R$-module.

articles.title: Equal ideal indices away from a denominator-clearing ideal
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be an algebra over
$O$, where $O$ and $B$ are commutative rings, with structure map $\varphi : O \to B$. Let
$\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $B$ with
$\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$
there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. Then the index of $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ in $O$
equals the index of $\mathfrak q$ in $B$, where the index of an ideal is the number of elements of
the quotient, taken to be $0$ when the quotient is infinite.

articles.title: Contraction after extension fixes primes away from the conductor
articles.statement: Contraction after extension is the identity on primes not containing `𝔠`.

articles.title: Contraction of a nonzero ideal is nonzero
articles.statement:
Contraction of a nonzero ideal is nonzero when `𝔠` is nonzero: a
nonzero element of `𝔠` clears a nonzero element of `𝔮` back to a nonzero
element of the contraction.

articles.title: A finite overring has nonzero conductor
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be an integral domain with fraction
field $K$, and let $T$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $K$ that is finitely generated as an $R$-module.
Then the conductor ideal of the image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is
nonzero.

articles.title: Preimage of a conductor ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ and $T$ commutative
$R$-algebras, $f \colon S \to T$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $B$ an $R$-subalgebra of
$T$. Then the preimage under $f$ of the conductor ideal of $B$ is contained in the conductor
ideal of the subalgebra $f^{-1}(B)$ of $S$.

articles.title: The conductor ideal is the unit ideal only for the whole algebra
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. The
conductor ideal of $A$ is all of $S$ if and only if $A = S$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of the conductor ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative
$R$-algebra and $A \subseteq B$ two $R$-subalgebras of $S$. Then the conductor ideal of $A$ is
contained in the conductor ideal of $B$.

articles.title: The conductor ideal lies in the subalgebra
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a
commutative $R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. Then the conductor ideal of $A$ is
contained in $A$.

articles.title: Conductor ideal of the whole algebra
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and $S$ a
commutative $R$-algebra. The conductor ideal of $S$, viewed as an $R$-subalgebra of itself, is
the unit ideal $S$.

articles.title: Conductor ideal of a subalgebra
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative
$R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. The conductor ideal of $A$ is the ideal of $S$
consisting of all $s \in S$ such that $st \in A$ for every $t \in S$; it is the largest ideal of
$S$ contained in $A$.

articles.title: A subalgebra of a field with nonzero conductor is finite
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian
commutative ring, $K$ a field that is an $R$-algebra, and $T$ an $R$-subalgebra of $K$. If the
conductor ideal of the image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is nonzero, then
$T$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.

articles.title: Finiteness of the integral closure via the conductor
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral
domain with fraction field $K$, and let $\overline{R}$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $K$,
viewed as an $R$-algebra. The conductor ideal of the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $\overline{R}$
(the image of $R$) is a nonzero ideal of $\overline{R}$ if and only if $\overline{R}$ is finitely
generated as an $R$-module.

articles.title: Maximal ideals stay maximal under denominator clearing
articles.statement:
Let $O$ and $B$ be commutative
rings, let $B$ be an $O$-algebra whose structure map $f \colon O \to B$ is injective, let
$\mathfrak p$ be a maximal ideal of $O$, and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $O$ with
$\mathfrak c + \mathfrak p = O$ such that $f(x)\,b$ lies in the image of $f$ for every
$x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$. Then the ideal $\mathfrak p B$ of $B$ generated by
$f(\mathfrak p)$ is maximal.

The proof shows that the canonical map $O/\mathfrak p \to B/\mathfrak p B$ is a ring isomorphism
and transfers the field property across it.

articles.title: In dimension at most one, nonzero primes extend to maximal ideals under denominator clearing
articles.statement:
**In dimension at most one, nonzero primes extend to maximal ideals under denominator
clearing.** Let $O$ and $B$ be commutative rings such that every nonzero prime ideal of $O$ is
maximal, let $B$ be an $O$-algebra whose structure map $f \colon O \to B$ is injective, let
$\mathfrak p$ be a nonzero prime ideal of $O$, and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $O$ with
$\mathfrak c + \mathfrak p = O$ such that $f(x)\,b$ lies in the image of $f$ for every
$x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$. Then the ideal of $B$ generated by $f(\mathfrak p)$ is
maximal.

Here dimension at most one means that every nonzero prime ideal of $O$ is maximal; for an
integral domain $O$ this is the condition that $O$ has Krull dimension at most one.

articles.title: Prime ideals stay prime under denominator clearing
articles.statement:
Let $O$ and $B$ be commutative rings,
let $B$ be an $O$-algebra whose structure map $f \colon O \to B$ is injective, let $\mathfrak p$
be a prime ideal of $O$, and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $O$ with
$\mathfrak c + \mathfrak p = O$ such that $f(x)\,b$ lies in the image of $f$ for every
$x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$. Then the ideal $\mathfrak p B$ of $B$ generated by
$f(\mathfrak p)$ is prime.

The proof shows that the canonical map $O/\mathfrak p \to B/\mathfrak p B$ is a ring isomorphism
and transfers the integral-domain property across it.

articles.title: Universal property of the conductor ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative semirings with
$S$ an $R$-algebra, let $A$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $S$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $S$. Then $I$
is contained in the conductor ideal of $A$ if and only if $I$ is contained in $A$.

articles.title: Extension after contraction fixes primes away from the conductor
articles.statement:
Extension after contraction is the identity on primes of `B` not
containing `𝔠.map f`, using that `B` has Krull dimension at most one.

articles.title: Membership in the conductor ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative semirings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, and let $A$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. An element $s \in S$ lies in the conductor
ideal of $A$ if and only if $st \in A$ for every $t \in S$.

articles.title: Equal cardinality of residue rings away from a denominator-clearing ideal
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be an
algebra over $O$, where $O$ and $B$ are commutative rings, with structure map
$\varphi : O \to B$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an
ideal of $B$ with $\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$
and every $b \in B$ there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. Then
$O / \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $B / \mathfrak q$ have the same cardinality, where the
cardinality of an infinite set is taken to be $0$.

articles.title: Bijection of nonzero primes away from the conductor
articles.statement:
Contraction and extension give an equivalence between the nonzero primes
of `B` not containing `𝔠.map (algebraMap O B)` and the nonzero primes of `O`
not containing `𝔠`. This is the restriction of
`Ideal.primeEquivOfNotLeConductor` to nonzero prime ideals.

articles.title: Bijection of primes away from the conductor
articles.statement:
Contraction and extension give an equivalence between all primes of `B`
not containing `𝔠.map (algebraMap O B)` and all primes of `O` not containing
`𝔠`, including the zero prime on both sides. This restores the full spectra
in ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 6.27.

articles.title: The residue-ring isomorphism on residue classes
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be an algebra over $O$, where
$O$ and $B$ are commutative rings, with structure map $\varphi : O \to B$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a
maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $B$ with
$\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$
there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. Then for every $o \in O$, the residue-ring isomorphism
$O / \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q) \cong B / \mathfrak q$ sends the class of $o$ to the class of
$\varphi(o)$.

articles.title: Residue-ring isomorphism away from a denominator-clearing ideal
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be an algebra
over $O$, where $O$ and $B$ are commutative rings, with structure map $\varphi : O \to B$. Let
$\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $B$ with
$\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$
there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. This is the ring isomorphism
$O / \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q) \to B / \mathfrak q$ induced by $\varphi$, which sends the class of
$o \in O$ to the class of $\varphi(o)$.

articles.title: Inverses of invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If an invertible fractional ideal $I$ of
$A$ in $K$ is prime to $J$, then its inverse $I^{-1}$ is prime to $J$.

articles.title: The unit fractional ideal is prime to every ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the unit fractional ideal $A$ of $A$ in $K$ is
prime to $J$.

articles.title: Fractional ideals prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field
$K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. Then $I$ is prime
to $J$ if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ with $J \subseteq \mathfrak p$, the extension
$I A_{\mathfrak p}$ of $I$ to the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$, a fractional ideal of
$A_{\mathfrak p}$ in $K$, is the unit fractional ideal $A_{\mathfrak p}$.

articles.title: Membership in the subgroup of units prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. An invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in
$K$ lies in the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals prime to $J$ if and only if $I$ is prime
to $J$.

articles.title: Prime to an ideal implies prime to every larger ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals
of $A$. If $I$ is prime to $J$, then $I$ is prime to $J'$.

articles.title: Products of fractional ideals prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If fractional ideals $I$ and $I'$ of $A$ in $K$
are both prime to $J$, then their product $I I'$ is prime to $J$.

articles.title: Non-zero-divisors stay non-zero-divisors in a localization at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal of $A$. Every non-zero-divisor of $A$ maps to a
non-zero-divisor of the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of the subgroups of units prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
with fraction field $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. Then the subgroup of invertible
fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J$ is contained in the subgroup of invertible fractional
ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J'$.

articles.title: Every invertible fractional ideal is prime to the unit ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
with fraction field $K$. The subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to the
unit ideal $A$ is the whole group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.

articles.title: Invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction
field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. The invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ that are
prime to $J$ form a subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.

articles.title: Making an ideal principal with a factor coprime to a given ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Dedekind domain and let $I$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ be nonzero ideals of $A$. Then there is an
ideal $J$ of $A$ with $J + \mathfrak{a} = A$ such that the product $IJ$ is a principal
ideal.

articles.title: Ideal classes have representatives coprime to a given ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Dedekind domain and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a nonzero ideal of $A$. Then every class $c$ in the
ideal class group of $A$ is the class of some nonzero ideal $K$ of $A$ with
$K + \mathfrak{a} = A$.

articles.title: Similar ideals
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain. Two nonzero ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$ are
similar when their classes in the ideal class group of $R$ are equal.

articles.title: Dedekind domains: PID iff trivial class group
articles.statement:
A Dedekind domain $R$ is a principal ideal
domain if and only if its ideal class group is trivial.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 3.2, Corollary 3.15 (second equivalence).

articles.title: Dedekind domains: UFD iff PID
articles.statement:
A Dedekind domain $R$ is a unique factorization domain if
and only if it is a principal ideal domain.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 3.2, Corollary 3.15 (first equivalence).

articles.title: Dedekind domains: UFD iff trivial class group
articles.statement:
A Dedekind domain $R$ is a unique
factorization domain if and only if its ideal class group is trivial.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 3.2, Corollary 3.15 (combined).

articles.title: Extension to a localization is localization
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be integral domains with $B$
a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $K$ be a field that is a fraction field of both $A$ and $B$,
compatibly with $A \to B \to K$. Let $S$ be a submonoid of $A$ such that $B$ is the localization
of $A$ at $S$ and the identity map of $K$ is a localization of the $A$-module $K$ at $S$. Then for
every fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$, the $B$-submodule of $K$ underlying the extension of $I$
to a fractional ideal of $B$ (the $B$-submodule generated by $I$) equals the localization
$S^{-1}I = \{x/s : x \in I,\ s \in S\}$ of $I$, viewed as a $B$-submodule of $K$.

articles.title: The inverse of a nonzero fractional ideal is its multiplication dual
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an
integral domain with fraction field $K$, and let $I$ be a nonzero fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$.
Then $I^{-1}$, viewed as an $A$-submodule of $K$, equals the dual submodule of $I$ with respect
to the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$, namely the set
$\{x \in K : xy \in A \text{ for all } y \in I\}$, where $A$ is identified with its image in $K$.

articles.title: Double dual of an invertible fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction
field $K$ and let $I$ be an invertible fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$. This is the $A$-linear
isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(I, A), A) \to I$ inverse to the canonical
evaluation map $I \to \operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(I, A), A)$,
$x \mapsto (f \mapsto f(x))$.

articles.title: Dual of a nonzero fractional ideal is its inverse
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$ and let $I$ be a nonzero fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$. This is the $A$-linear
isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_A(I, A) \to I^{-1}$, with $I^{-1}$ viewed as an $A$-submodule of
$K$, sending $f$ to the unique $x \in I^{-1}$ such that $f(y) = xy$ in $K$ for all $y \in I$
(where $A$ is identified with its image in $K$).

articles.title: Formula for the isomorphism onto the multiplication dual
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
with fraction field $K$, let $M$ be a nonzero $A$-submodule of $K$, and let
$\varphi \colon \operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A) \to M^\vee$ be the isomorphism onto the dual submodule
$M^\vee$ of $M$ for the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$. Then for every
$f \in \operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A)$ and every $m \in M$, the image of $f(m)$ in $K$ equals
$\varphi(f) \, m$.

articles.title: Dual of a nonzero submodule of the fraction field
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$, identify $A$ with its image in $K$, and let $M$ be a nonzero $A$-submodule of
$K$. Let $M^\vee = \{x \in K : xy \in A \text{ for all } y \in M\}$ be the dual submodule of $M$
for the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$. This is the $A$-linear isomorphism
$\operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A) \to M^\vee$ inverse to the map sending $x \in M^\vee$ to the
functional $y \mapsto xy$ on $M$; it sends $f$ to the unique $x \in M^\vee$ with $f(y) = xy$ for
all $y \in M$.

articles.title: The multiplication dual is a colon quotient
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a field
that is an $A$-algebra, and write $1$ for the $A$-submodule $A \cdot 1$ of $K$. For every
$A$-submodule $M$ of $K$, the dual submodule of $M$ with respect to the multiplication form
$(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$ equals the quotient $1 / M$, the set of $x \in K$ with $xy \in A \cdot 1$
for all $y \in M$.

articles.title: Functionals on a submodule of the fraction field are multiplications
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an
integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $M$ be a nonzero $A$-submodule of $K$. For every
$A$-linear map $f \colon M \to A$ there is $x \in K$ such that the image of $f(m)$ in $K$ equals
$xm$ for every $m \in M$.

articles.title: Extension to a localization commutes with division by a finitely generated ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$
and $B$ be integral domains with $B$ a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $K$ be a field that is a
fraction field of both $A$ and $B$, compatibly with $A \to B \to K$. Let $S$ be a submonoid of $A$
such that $B$ is the localization of $A$ at $S$. Let $I$ and $J$ be fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$
with $J \ne 0$ and $J$ finitely generated as an $A$-module, and write $IB$ for the extension of $I$
to a fractional ideal of $B$. Then $(I/J)B = IB/JB$, where for a nonzero denominator the quotient
of fractional ideals is $I/J = \{x \in K : xJ \subseteq I\}$.

articles.title: Over a Noetherian domain, extension to a localization commutes with division
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be
a Noetherian integral domain, $B$ an integral domain that is a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and $K$ a
field that is a fraction field of both $A$ and $B$, compatibly with $A \to B \to K$. Let $S$ be a
submonoid of $A$ such that $B$ is the localization of $A$ at $S$. Let $I$ and $J$ be fractional
ideals of $A$ in $K$ with $J \ne 0$, and write $IB$ for the extension of $I$ to a fractional ideal
of $B$. Then $(I/J)B = IB/JB$, where for a nonzero denominator the quotient of fractional ideals
is $I/J = \{x \in K : xJ \subseteq I\}$.

articles.title: Invertible fractional ideals of a Noetherian local domain are principal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Noetherian local integral domain with fraction field $K$, and let $I$ be a nonzero fractional ideal
of $A$ in $K$. Then $I$ is invertible if and only if $I$ is principal.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 3.1, Lemma 3.4.

articles.title: Inverse of a localized fractional ideal is bounded by localization
articles.statement: The inverse/localization inequality follows from equality.

articles.title: Locally principal fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$.
For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, write $A_{\mathfrak m}$ for the localization of $A$ at
$\mathfrak m$ and $I_{\mathfrak m}$ for the localization of a fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$,
the $A_{\mathfrak m}$-submodule of $K$ generated by $I$. A fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$ is
locally principal if for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ the localization
$I_{\mathfrak m}$, as an $A_{\mathfrak m}$-submodule of $K$, is principal.

articles.title: Corollary 3.5
articles.statement:
A nonzero fractional ideal of a Noetherian domain is invertible iff it is
locally principal.

articles.title: Theorem 3.2
articles.statement:
**Theorem 3.2** (prime-ideal form). A fractional ideal of a Noetherian domain is invertible iff
its localization at every prime ideal is invertible.

articles.title: Theorem 3.2
articles.statement:
**Theorem 3.2** (maximal-ideal form). A fractional ideal of a Noetherian domain is invertible
iff its localization at every maximal ideal is invertible.

articles.title: Localization commutes with inverting fractional ideals
articles.statement: Localization commutes with inversion of fractional ideals.

articles.title: Localization of a fractional ideal at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction
field $K$, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $A$, and write $A_{\mathfrak p}$ for the
localization of $A$ at $\mathfrak p$. The localization $I_{\mathfrak p}$ of a fractional ideal $I$
of $A$ in $K$ is the fractional ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ in $K$ obtained by extending $I$ along
$A \to A_{\mathfrak p}$, that is, the $A_{\mathfrak p}$-submodule of $K$ generated by $I$.

articles.title: Localization commutes with division by a finitely generated submodule
articles.statement:
Let $R$, $S$ and $K$
be commutative rings with algebra maps $R \to S \to K$ forming a scalar tower, let $p$ be a
submonoid of $R$ such that $S$ is the localization of $R$ at $p$, and suppose the identity map of
$K$ is a localization of the $R$-module $K$ at $p$. For an $R$-submodule $M$ of $K$ write
$M_p = \{x/s : x \in M,\ s \in p\}$ for its localization, an $S$-submodule of $K$, where $x/s$ is
the element $y \in K$ with $s y = x$. For submodules write $M/N = \{x \in K : xN \subseteq M\}$.
Then for $R$-submodules $I$ and $J$ of $K$ with $J$ finitely generated, $(I/J)_p = I_p/J_p$.

articles.title: Every functional comes from the multiplication dual
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain with
fraction field $K$, identify $A$ with its image in $K$, and let $M$ be a nonzero $A$-submodule of
$K$. Let $M^\vee = \{x \in K : xy \in A \text{ for all } y \in M\}$ be the dual submodule of $M$
for the multiplication form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$. Then the $A$-linear map
$M^\vee \to \operatorname{Hom}_A(M, A)$ sending $x$ to the functional $y \mapsto xy$ on $M$ is
surjective.

articles.title: Multiplication is a nondegenerate bilinear form
articles.statement:
For every field $K$, the $K$-bilinear
form $(x, y) \mapsto xy$ on $K$ is nondegenerate: if $xy = 0$ for all $y \in K$ then $x = 0$, and
if $xy = 0$ for all $x \in K$ then $y = 0$.

articles.title: A nonzero submodule spans the field
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a field that is
an $A$-algebra. Then every nonzero $A$-submodule $M$ of $K$ spans $K$ as a $K$-vector space.

articles.title: Fractional ideals have finite support
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with field of
fractions $K$, and let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$. For a nonzero prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $A$, let $v_{\mathfrak p}(I) \in \mathbb Z$ be the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in
the factorization of $I$ into prime ideals, with $v_{\mathfrak p}(0) = 0$. Then
$v_{\mathfrak p}(I) \neq 0$ for only finitely many nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $A$.

In particular, for $x \in K^\times$ the valuations $v_{\mathfrak p}(xA)$ vanish for all but
finitely many $\mathfrak p$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 3.10. The book's hypothesis $I \neq 0$ is dropped, since every valuation of the zero ideal is zero.

articles.title: Valuations of a product of prime powers
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$. For every finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to
$\mathbb{Z}$ and every height-one prime $v$ of $R$, the $v$-adic valuation of the fractional
ideal $\prod_w w^{e(w)}$, the product over the primes $w$ with $e(w) \neq 0$, equals $e(v)$.

articles.title: Vanishing multiplicity of a prime factor
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain, let $\mathfrak p$
be a prime ideal of $A$ and let $I$ be a nonzero ideal of $A$. Then the multiplicity of
$\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of $I$ into prime ideals is zero if and only if
$I \not\subseteq \mathfrak p$.

In particular, if $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ are distinct nonzero prime ideals of $A$, then
the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of $\mathfrak q$ is zero.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Lemma 3.9.

articles.title: Ideal multiplicity is unchanged by localization at a maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a maximal ideal of $R$, and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a local ring that
is a localization of $R$ at $\mathfrak p$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Then for every
ideal $I$ of $R$, the multiplicity of $\mathfrak m$ in the extended ideal $I R_{\mathfrak p}$
equals the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in $I$. Here the multiplicity of an ideal $J$ in an
ideal $K$ is the largest $n$ with $J^n \mid K$, or $\infty$ if $J^n \mid K$ for every $n$.

articles.title: Exponent function of a prime ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field
$K$ and let $w$ be a height-one prime of $R$. The factorization isomorphism sends the fractional
ideal $w$, as a unit fractional ideal of $R$ in $K$, to the function on height-one primes of $R$
that is $1$ at $w$ and $0$ elsewhere.

articles.title: Prime factorization isomorphism for fractional ideals
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$, and for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime $v$
of $R$ write $\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. The factorization
isomorphism is the group isomorphism from the unit group of the fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$
to the additive group of finitely supported functions from the height-one primes of $R$ to
$\mathbb{Z}$ (written multiplicatively) that sends $I$ to the function
$v \mapsto \operatorname{val}_v(I)$. Its inverse sends $e$ to $\prod_v v^{e(v)}$, the product
over the primes $v$ with $e(v) \neq 0$.

articles.title: Finitely many primes contain a nonzero ideal
articles.statement:
In a Dedekind domain $A$, every nonzero
ideal $I$ is contained in only finitely many prime ideals of $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 3.7.

articles.title: Finitely many primes contain a nonzero element
articles.statement:
In a Dedekind domain $A$, every nonzero
element $a$ lies in only finitely many prime ideals of $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Lemma 3.6.

articles.title: Products of prime powers are nonzero
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field
$K$. For every finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$,
the fractional ideal $\prod_v v^{e(v)}$ of $R$ in $K$, the product over the primes $v$ with
$e(v) \neq 0$, is nonzero.

articles.title: Fractional ideal with prescribed prime exponents
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$. For a finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to
$\mathbb{Z}$, this is the fractional ideal $\prod_v v^{e(v)}$ of $R$ in $K$, the product over the
primes $v$ with $e(v) \neq 0$, regarded as a unit of the monoid of fractional ideals (it is
nonzero, hence invertible).

articles.title: Inverse factorization of a single prime power
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $w$ be a height-one prime of $R$ and let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The inverse of the
factorization isomorphism sends the function on height-one primes of $R$ that is $n$ at $w$ and
$0$ elsewhere to the fractional ideal $w^n$.

articles.title: Reconstructing a fractional ideal from its prime exponents
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain
with fraction field $K$, and for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime
$v$ of $R$ write $\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. Every unit
fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ equals $\prod_v v^{\operatorname{val}_v(I)}$, the product over
the height-one primes $v$ of $R$ with $\operatorname{val}_v(I) \neq 0$.

articles.title: Recovering prime exponents from a product of prime powers
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain
with fraction field $K$, and let $e$ be a finitely supported function from the height-one primes
of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$. The prime-exponent function of the fractional ideal $\prod_w w^{e(w)}$,
the product over the primes $w$ with $e(w) \neq 0$, is $e$: its $v$-adic valuation is $e(v)$
for every height-one prime $v$ of $R$.

articles.title: Support of the prime exponents of a fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$. For a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$, this is the finite set of
height-one primes $v$ of $R$ at which the $v$-adic valuation of $I$ is nonzero.

articles.title: Prime exponents are additive
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and
for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write
$\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. For all unit fractional ideals $I$
and $J$ of $R$ in $K$ and every height-one prime $v$ of $R$,
$\operatorname{val}_v(IJ) = \operatorname{val}_v(I) + \operatorname{val}_v(J)$.

articles.title: Prime exponents of an invertible fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$, and let $I$ be a unit of the monoid of fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$.
The prime exponents of $I$ form the finitely supported function from the height-one primes of
$R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ that sends each height-one prime $v$ to the exponent $\operatorname{ord}_v(I)$
of $v$ in the factorization $I = \prod_v v^{\operatorname{ord}_v(I)}$; its support is the finite
set of $v$ with $\operatorname{ord}_v(I) \neq 0$.

articles.title: Elements of a translated fractional ideal are images
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a
commutative domain $R$ by ring automorphisms, let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$, and let $G$
act on fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$ by $g \cdot I = \tilde\sigma_g(I)$, where $\tilde\sigma_g$
is the automorphism of $K$ extending $r \mapsto g \cdot r$. For every $g \in G$, every fractional
ideal $I$ and every $x \in K$, we have $x \in g \cdot I$ if and only if $\tilde\sigma_g(y) = x$
for some $y \in I$.

articles.title: Membership in a translated fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative domain
$R$ by ring automorphisms, let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$, and let $G$ act on fractional
ideals of $R$ in $K$ by $g \cdot I = \tilde\sigma_g(I)$, where $\tilde\sigma_g$ is the
automorphism of $K$ extending $r \mapsto g \cdot r$. For every $g \in G$, every fractional ideal
$I$ and every $x \in K$, we have $x \in g \cdot I$ if and only if
$\tilde\sigma_g^{-1}(x) \in I$.

articles.title: Ring automorphisms act on fractional ideals
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative domain
and $K$ a field of fractions of $R$. For a ring automorphism $\sigma$ of $R$, let $\tilde\sigma$
be the automorphism of $K$ extending $\sigma$. Sending $\sigma$ to the map
$I \mapsto \tilde\sigma(I)$ on fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$ defines a group homomorphism from
the group of ring automorphisms of $R$ to the group of ring automorphisms of the semiring of
fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$.

articles.title: Viewing prime ideals as fractional ideals commutes with the group action
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$
act on an integral domain $R$ by ring automorphisms, let $K$ be a fraction field of $R$, and let
$G$ act on the fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$ through the extension of each automorphism of $R$
to $K$. For $g \in G$ and a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, write
$g \cdot \mathfrak p = \{g \cdot x : x \in \mathfrak p\}$ for the image of $\mathfrak p$ under
$g$, again a prime ideal of $R$. Then for every $g \in G$ and every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of
$R$, the ideal $g \cdot \mathfrak p$ viewed as a fractional ideal in $K$ equals $g$ applied to
$\mathfrak p$ viewed as a fractional ideal in $K$.

articles.title: Translating a prime ideal by a group element
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative
semiring $R$ by semiring automorphisms, and let $G$ act on the prime spectrum of $R$ by the
induced action. For every $g \in G$ and every point $\mathfrak p$ of the prime spectrum of $R$,
the prime ideal underlying the translated point $g \cdot \mathfrak p$ is the image of the ideal
$\mathfrak p$ under the automorphism of $R$ given by $g$.

articles.title: Translating an integral ideal
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative domain $R$ by ring
automorphisms, let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$, and let $G$ act on fractional ideals of
$R$ in $K$ by $g \cdot J = \tilde\sigma_g(J)$, where $\tilde\sigma_g$ is the automorphism of $K$
extending $r \mapsto g \cdot r$. For every $g \in G$ and every ideal $I$ of $R$, the translate
$g \cdot I$ of $I$ viewed as a fractional ideal is the ideal $\{g \cdot a : a \in I\}$ of $R$
viewed as a fractional ideal.

articles.title: The action on fractional ideals is by images
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative domain
$R$ by ring automorphisms and let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$. For $g \in G$ let
$\tilde\sigma_g$ be the automorphism of $K$ extending the automorphism $r \mapsto g \cdot r$ of
$R$. Then for every $g \in G$ and every fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$, the induced action
satisfies $g \cdot I = \tilde\sigma_g(I)$, the image of $I$ under $\tilde\sigma_g$.

articles.title: Action on invertible fractional ideals
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative domain $R$
by ring automorphisms, let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$, and let $G$ act on fractional
ideals of $R$ in $K$ by $g \cdot I = \tilde\sigma_g(I)$, where $\tilde\sigma_g$ is the
automorphism of $K$ extending $r \mapsto g \cdot r$. This induces an action of $G$ on the group
of invertible fractional ideals: $g$ sends an invertible fractional ideal $I$ to $g \cdot I$,
whose inverse is $g \cdot I^{-1}$. This action respects products and fixes the unit fractional
ideal $R$.

articles.title: Translating an invertible fractional ideal
articles.statement:
Let a group $G$ act on a commutative domain
$R$ by ring automorphisms, let $K$ be a field of fractions of $R$, and let $G$ act on fractional
ideals of $R$ in $K$ by $g \cdot I = \tilde\sigma_g(I)$, where $\tilde\sigma_g$ is the
automorphism of $K$ extending $r \mapsto g \cdot r$. For every $g \in G$ and every invertible
fractional ideal $I$, the translate of $I$ under the induced action on invertible fractional
ideals has underlying fractional ideal $g \cdot I$.

articles.title: Coefficient of the exponential in a given degree
articles.statement: In particular, the coefficient of degree `d.degree` uses exactly the terms `n ≤ d.degree`.

articles.title: Weighted coefficient relation passes to formal exponentials
articles.statement:
If `w` has the coefficients of `q` scaled by an additive weight, then the
same coefficient relation holds for their lawful formal exponentials. The
coefficient hypothesis and `q`'s zero constant imply the required premise for
`w`; no separate zero-constant assumption on `w` is needed.

articles.title: Coefficients of the exponential via truncation
articles.statement:
A coefficient of the exponential is computed by any truncation extending past its degree.
This is the exact finite-sum formula used by the source's degreewise constructor.

articles.title: Coefficients of weighted rescaling of truncated exponentials
articles.statement:
The coefficient form of weighted finite exponential commutation. It
preserves the source's degreewise expression for arbitrary input series.

articles.title: Coefficients of a weighted rescaling of a rational power series
articles.statement:
Mapping rational coefficients and rescaling variable `i` by
`ε ^ wt (Finsupp.single i 1)` multiplies coefficient `d` by `ε ^ wt d`.

articles.title: Weighted coefficient equality transfers zero constant coefficient
articles.statement:
Weighted coefficient equality transfers a zero constant coefficient from
the rational source series to the target series.

articles.title: Constant coefficient of the formal exponential is one
articles.statement: The constant coefficient of the formal exponential is one.

articles.title: Characterization of weighted rescalings of a power series
articles.statement:
A series has the weighted coefficients of `q` exactly when it is the
canonical coefficient map of `q` followed by the corresponding rescaling.

articles.title: Formal exponential turns sums into products
articles.statement: The formal exponential carries sums of series with zero constant coefficient to products.

articles.title: Multivariate exponential as substitution into exp
articles.statement: The exponential API is the canonical univariate exponential substituted at `w`.

articles.title: Weighted rescaling commutes with the formal exponential
articles.statement:
On the zero-constant domain, weighted coefficient mapping and rescaling
commutes with the lawful full formal exponential.

articles.title: Exponential of a variable
articles.statement: Substituting a variable recovers the canonical exponential in that variable.

articles.title: Exponential of the zero series is one
articles.statement: The exponential of the zero series is one.

articles.title: Exponential of a power series with zero constant coefficient
articles.statement:
The formal exponential of a series with zero constant coefficient, obtained
by substituting it into Mathlib's canonical exponential power series.

articles.title: Weighted rescaling commutes with truncated exponentials
articles.statement:
Weighted coefficient mapping and rescaling commutes with every finite
exponential truncation, without a constant coefficient restriction.

articles.title: Truncated exponential of a multivariate power series
articles.statement: The finite sum `∑ n < N, wⁿ/n!`, defined without a constant coefficient restriction.

articles.title: Filtration-preserving endomorphisms commute with the formal exponential
articles.statement:
A ring endomorphism preserving the total-degree coefficient filtration
commutes with the formal exponential. The filtration premise itself implies
that the image of a zero-constant series again has zero constant coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficient ring maps commute with the formal exponential
articles.statement: Applying a coefficient ring homomorphism commutes with the formal exponential.

articles.title: Ring maps commute with truncated exponentials
articles.statement:
A ring homomorphism between multivariate power-series rings commutes with
finite exponential truncations.

articles.title: Partial derivative of the formal exponential
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of the canonical exponential is the derivative of its exponent times
the exponential.

articles.title: Partial derivative of the truncated exponential
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of the finite exponential sum containing the terms `w ^ n / n!` for
`n ≤ N` is the derivative of its exponent times the sum containing those terms for `n < N`.

articles.title: Iterated coefficient operators raise the order
articles.statement: Iteration raises every natural lower bound on order by the number of steps.

articles.title: Coefficient operators raise the order by one
articles.statement: A coefficient operator raises every natural lower bound on order by one.

articles.title: Coefficient of a coefficient operator over any finite superset
articles.statement: At any exponent, sum over any finite set containing its support.

articles.title: Coefficient formula for a coefficient operator
articles.statement: The coefficient of the formal operator is a sum over the exponent support.

articles.title: Operator exponential coefficients depend only on lower-degree inputs
articles.statement:
A coefficient of the operator exponential depends only on input coefficients of no
greater total degree.

articles.title: Defining coefficient formula of the operator exponential
articles.statement: The defining iteration bound is exactly the source constructor's bound.

articles.title: Coefficients of the operator exponential via partial sums
articles.statement: For `d.degree < N`, the first `N` operator iterates determine coefficient `d`.

articles.title: Low-degree coefficients of an iterated coefficient operator vanish
articles.statement: The `n`th iterate has no coefficient in total degree less than `n`.

articles.title: Product rule for coefficient operators
articles.statement: A family of coefficient derivations gives the source product rule, without commutation.

articles.title: Coefficient operator on multivariate power series
articles.statement: The operator `∑ i, X i * O i`, defined by finite coefficient sums.

articles.title: Lifted coefficient maps commute with the coefficient operator
articles.statement: Lifted coefficient maps commute with the operator under the source pairwise premise.

articles.title: Lifted coefficient maps commute with coefficient-operator iterates
articles.statement:
A lifted coefficient map commutes with every coefficient-operator iterate when the
coefficient maps commute pairwise.

articles.title: The operator exponential preserves the constant coefficient
articles.statement: The formal exponential preserves every constant coefficient, including nonzero ones.

articles.title: The operator exponential commutes with the formal exponential
articles.statement: The operator exponential commutes with the lawful ordinary formal exponential.

articles.title: Evaluation of the operator-exponential ring homomorphism
articles.statement:
Applying the operator-exponential ring homomorphism is the existing formal operator
exponential.

articles.title: Exponential of coefficient derivations as a ring endomorphism
articles.statement: The formal exponential of coefficient derivations as a ring endomorphism.

articles.title: The exponential of coefficient derivations is multiplicative
articles.statement:
The formal exponential of a family of coefficient derivations preserves products.
No pairwise commutation or finiteness hypothesis on the family is needed.

articles.title: Operator exponential when the square of the operator vanishes
articles.statement: If the second operator iterate vanishes on `f`, its exponential is `f + 𝒪 f`.

articles.title: The operator exponential fixes series annihilated by the operator
articles.statement: The exponential fixes an input annihilated by the coefficient operator.

articles.title: The exponential of coefficient derivations preserves one
articles.statement: The formal exponential of a family of coefficient derivations preserves one.

articles.title: Partial operator exponential as a sum of function iterates
articles.statement: The finite exponential sum agrees with the source's function-iterate formula.

articles.title: Partial sums of the exponential of a coefficient operator
articles.statement: The first `N` operator iterates, `∑ n < N, 𝒪ⁿ / n!`, acting on the full input series.

articles.title: Exponential of the zero coefficient-operator family is the identity
articles.statement: The exponential of the zero coefficient-map family is the identity linear map.

articles.title: Formal exponential of a coefficient operator
articles.statement: The formal exponential: coefficient `d` uses operator iterates `n ≤ d.degree`.

articles.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient operator
articles.statement: The operator derivative is the operator of the derivative plus the lifted `O i`.

articles.title: Partial derivatives commute with coefficient lifting
articles.statement: Partial differentiation commutes with canonical coefficient lifting.

articles.title: Gradient law for the exponential of commuting coefficient derivations
articles.statement:
The exponential gradient law specialized to a pairwise commuting family of coefficient
derivations, using their canonical rational linear maps.

articles.title: Partial derivative of partial sums of the operator exponential
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of the first `N + 1` exponential terms is the corresponding
partial sum on the derivative plus the first `N` terms on the lifted coefficient map.

articles.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient-operator exponential
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of a formal coefficient-operator exponential is the exponential
of the input derivative plus the exponential of the lifted coefficient map.

articles.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient-operator iterate
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of the `(n + 1)`st coefficient-operator iterate is the
iterate of the partial derivative plus `(n + 1)` copies of the lifted coefficient map.

articles.title: Coefficients of the coefficientwise derivation
articles.statement: The coefficient of the lifted derivation is the derivative of that coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficient formula for the coefficientwise linear operator
articles.statement: The coefficient formula for the linear operator underlying the lifted derivation.

articles.title: Coefficientwise derivation of a constant series
articles.statement: On a constant series, the lift acts on its constant coefficient.

articles.title: Commuting derivations lift to commuting coefficientwise derivations
articles.statement: Commuting coefficient derivations lift to commuting derivations of Hahn series.

articles.title: Coefficientwise derivation of a single-term series
articles.statement: A one-term series keeps its exponent and differentiates its coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficientwise lift of the zero derivation
articles.statement: The lift of the zero derivation is zero.

articles.title: Coefficientwise derivation of Hahn series
articles.statement: Extend a derivation of the coefficient algebra by applying it to each coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficientwise linear operator on Hahn series
articles.statement: Apply a coefficient derivation to a Hahn series as an `R`-linear operator.

articles.title: Coefficientwise linear operator does not enlarge the support
articles.statement: Acting on coefficients cannot introduce new exponents into the support.

articles.title: Powers of the inverse variable difference have binomial coefficients
articles.statement:
The `(N + 1)`-st power of the inverse variable difference has negative-binomial
coefficients on one diagonal.

articles.title: Inverse of the variable difference as a diagonal series
articles.statement: The inverse of the formal variable difference is its infinite diagonal Laurent series.

articles.title: Value of the variable difference unit
articles.statement: The value of `variableDifferenceUnit` is the difference of the two formal variables.

articles.title: Double coefficients of a diagonal Laurent series
articles.statement: Both coefficients of a diagonal Laurent series, exposing its cutoff and diagonal equation.

articles.title: Multiplying by the variable difference on diagonal coefficients
articles.statement:
Multiplication by the difference of the two variables takes a difference of adjacent
diagonal coefficients.

articles.title: Outer coefficient of a diagonal Laurent series
articles.statement: The outer coefficient of a diagonal Laurent series.

articles.title: Diagonal Laurent-coefficient Hahn series
articles.statement:
The Hahn series with coefficient `c y` at inner exponent `d - y` and outer exponent `y`
for every `y ≥ j₀`.

articles.title: Variable difference as a unit of Hahn series
articles.statement:
The formal difference of the inner and outer variables, bundled with its diagonal-series
inverse.

articles.title: Coefficient formula for an exponent-indexed coefficient map
articles.statement: The coefficient formula for an exponent-indexed coefficient map.

articles.title: Exponent-indexed coefficient map on a constant series
articles.statement: On a constant series, the map indexed by zero acts on the constant coefficient.

articles.title: Product rule for graded Leibniz coefficient maps
articles.statement:
An exponent-indexed coefficient map satisfying the graded Leibniz identity obeys the product
rule on Hahn series.

articles.title: Exponent-indexed coefficient map on a single-term series
articles.statement: A one-term series keeps its exponent and applies the map indexed by that exponent.

articles.title: Exponent-indexed coefficient map of the zero family
articles.statement: The family consisting of zero maps induces the zero additive map.

articles.title: Exponent-indexed coefficient map on Hahn series
articles.statement: Apply the map indexed by each exponent to the coefficient at that exponent.

articles.title: Exponent-indexed coefficient maps do not enlarge the support
articles.statement: Acting coefficientwise cannot introduce new exponents into the support.

articles.title: Coefficients of the bivariate monoid algebra embedding
articles.statement: The two coefficient projections of the bivariate embedding recover the original coefficient.

articles.title: Monoid algebra embedding into Hahn series preserves coefficients
articles.statement: The finite Hahn embedding preserves every coefficient.

articles.title: Monoid algebra embedding into Hahn series as a ring map
articles.statement: The finite Hahn embedding is Mathlib's `ofFinsupp`, bundled as a ring homomorphism.

articles.title: Injectivity of the monoid algebra embedding into Hahn series
articles.statement: The finite Hahn embedding is injective.

articles.title: Embedding of a finite additive monoid algebra into Hahn series
articles.statement: Embed a finite additive monoid algebra into Hahn series.

articles.title: Injectivity of the bivariate monoid algebra embedding
articles.statement: The bivariate finite Hahn embedding is injective.

articles.title: Embedding of a bivariate monoid algebra into Hahn series
articles.statement: Embed a bivariate finite monoid algebra into Hahn series, with the second coordinate outer.

articles.title: Membership in the span of a constant and initial variables
articles.statement:
A power series lies in the span of `C ϖ` and the first `k` variables
exactly when every coefficient of a monomial supported on the last `n - k`
variables is divisible by `ϖ`.

articles.title: The variables span the kernel of the constant coefficient map
articles.statement:
The kernel of the constant coefficient map on multivariate power series
is the span of the variables.

articles.title: Coefficients of a positive log-convex series are positive
articles.statement:
If a real formal power series
$f$ has positive log-convex coefficients, then the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$ is strictly
positive for every natural number $n$.

articles.title: Positive log-convex coefficients
articles.statement:
A real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ has
positive log-convex coefficients if $a_n > 0$ for every natural number $n$ and
$a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural number $n$. This is the hypothesis of Kaluza's
bounds for the coefficients of the reciprocal series.

## Sources

- László Tóth, *Alternating Sums Concerning Multiplicative Arithmetic Functions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 20, the lemma at lines 553–562 of <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL20/Toth/toth25.tex>.

articles.title: Kaluza's bounds for the coefficients of a reciprocal power series
articles.statement:
Let
$f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ be a real formal power series with positive log-convex coefficients, and
let $f^{-1} = \sum_n b_n X^n$ be its reciprocal in the ring of formal power series. Then
$b_0 = a_0^{-1}$, $b_0 > 0$, and $-a_n / a_0^2 \le b_n \le 0$ for every $n \ge 1$.

The reciprocal is formal; no convergence is assumed.

## Sources

- László Tóth, *Alternating Sums Concerning Multiplicative Arithmetic Functions*, Journal of Integer Sequences 20, the lemma at lines 553–562 of <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL20/Toth/toth25.tex>. Tóth attributes the nonpositivity of `bₙ` to T. Kaluza, Satz 3.

articles.title: Log-convexity of the coefficients
articles.statement:
If a real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$
has positive log-convex coefficients, then $a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural
number $n$.

articles.title: Hermite's diagonal form of Lagrange inversion without side conditions
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative ring, let $F$, $\varphi$, $w$ and $G$ be formal power series over $R$, and write
$[X^n]H$ for the coefficient of $X^n$ in a power series $H$. Write $\varphi'$ for the formal
derivative of $\varphi$, and $\varphi(w)$, $\varphi'(w)$, $F(w)$ for the substitution of $w$ into
$\varphi$, $\varphi'$, $F$. If $w = X\,\varphi(w)$ and $(1 - X\,\varphi'(w))\,G = F(w)$, then
$[X^n](F\varphi^n) = [X^n]G$ for every natural number $n$.

The constant term of $w$ vanishes automatically, and $\varphi$ may have zero constant term.

articles.title: Lagrange–Bürmann formula, coefficient form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$,
$\varphi$ and $g$ be formal power series over $R$ such that the constant term of $A$ is
nilpotent, $\varphi$ has nonzero constant term, and $A = X\,\varphi(A)$, where $\varphi(A)$ and
