$g(A)$ denote the substitution of $A$ into $\varphi$ and $g$. Write $[X^m]H$ for the coefficient
of $X^m$ in a power series $H$ and $g'$ for the formal derivative of $g$. Then for every
natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$n\, [X^n]\, g(A) = [X^{n-1}]\left(g' \varphi^n\right).$$

This is the division-free form over a commutative ring: no division by $n$ is required.

## Sources

- Alexander M. Haupt, "Enumeration of S-omino Towers and Row-Convex k-omino Towers," JIS 24 (2021), proposition at lines 400–407, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL24/Haupt/haupt4.tex. Corroborating power specialization: Dmitry Kruchinin and Vladimir Kruchinin, "A Method for Obtaining Generating Functions for Central Coefficients of Triangles," JIS 15 (2012), lines 199–210, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL15/Kruchinin/kruchinin5.tex.

articles.title: Lagrange–Bürmann formula from the fixed-point equation alone
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative
ring and let $A$, $\varphi$ and $g$ be formal power series over $R$ with $A = X\,\varphi(A)$,
where $\varphi(A)$ and $g(A)$ denote the substitution of $A$ into $\varphi$ and $g$. Write
$[X^m]H$ for the coefficient of $X^m$ in a power series $H$ and $g'$ for the formal derivative
of $g$. Then for every natural number $n \ge 1$,

$$n\, [X^n]\, g(A) = [X^{n-1}]\left(g' \varphi^n\right).$$

No condition on the constant term of $\varphi$ is needed.

articles.title: Hermite's diagonal form of Lagrange inversion
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $F$,
$\varphi$, $w$ and $G$ be formal power series over $R$, and write $[X^n]H$ for the coefficient
of $X^n$ in a power series $H$. Write $\varphi'$ for the formal derivative of $\varphi$, and
$\varphi(w)$, $\varphi'(w)$, $F(w)$ for the substitution of $w$ into $\varphi$, $\varphi'$, $F$.
Suppose that $w$ has constant term $0$, that $\varphi$ has nonzero constant term, that
$w = X\,\varphi(w)$, and that $(1 - X\,\varphi'(w))\,G = F(w)$. Then
$[X^n](F\varphi^n) = [X^n]G$ for every natural number $n$.

In contrast to the derivative-coefficient form of the Lagrange–Bürmann formula, the derivative
here is absorbed into the defining equation for $G$.

Reference: Bakir Farhi, "Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula
for the k-Fibonacci Numbers", Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024),
Hermite corollary and derivation lines 205-240.

## Sources

- https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Farhi/farhi35.tex, statement lines 205-210; lines 205-240.

articles.title: Hermite's form of Lagrange inversion as a series identity
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$, $g$, $F$ and $\psi$
be formal power series over $\mathbb{C}$, write $F'$ for the formal derivative of $F$, and write
$h(k)$ for the substitution of a power series $k$ into a power series $h$. Suppose that $\varphi$
has nonzero constant term, that $F\varphi = X$, and that $\psi$ is a two-sided compositional
inverse of $F$, that is, $F(\psi) = X$ and $\psi(F) = X$. Let $H = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n X^n$,
where $c_n$ is the coefficient of $X^n$ in $g\varphi^n$. Then

$$X\, g(\psi) = H\, \psi\, F'(\psi).$$

The source states this, with $F = X/\varphi$, as $X\, g(\psi) / (\psi\, F'(\psi)) = H$; the
form here is cleared of denominators.

## Sources

- Bakir Farhi, "Some Applications of the Lagrange Inversion Formula for the k-Fibonacci Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.1, Corollary (Hermite, label t-her), lines 205–210, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Farhi/farhi35.tex

articles.title: Coefficient of a single variable in a formal linear form
articles.statement: The coefficient of variable `i` is the prescribed coefficient `b i`.

articles.title: Coefficient formula for a formal linear form

articles.statement: A formal linear form has zero constant coefficient.

articles.title: Rational factorial coefficient as a constant term of an iterated derivative
articles.statement: The source rational-factorial constant coefficient equation.

articles.title: Factorial times a coefficient is a constant term of an iterated derivative
articles.statement:
A monomial's factorial times its coefficient is the constant coefficient of the
corresponding iterated partial derivative.

articles.title: Rational factorial-weighted coefficient of an iterated derivative
articles.statement:

articles.title: Factorial-weighted coefficient of an iterated partial derivative
articles.statement:

cancelled, so this identity also holds in positive characteristic.

articles.title: Iterated partial derivatives along concatenated lists compose

articles.title: Formal linear form in multivariate power series
articles.statement:
The formal linear form with variable coefficient family `b : σ → R`.

Its coefficient at `d` is the sum of `b i` over the support of `d` when `d`
has total degree one, and zero otherwise.

articles.title: Coefficient ring maps commute with formal linear forms

articles.title: Partial derivative of a formal linear form
articles.statement:
The partial derivative of a formal linear form is its corresponding

articles.title: Variable multiplicities of a list as a sum of singleton multi-indices
articles.statement: List variable multiplicities equal the sum of singleton multi-indices.

articles.title: Taylor's formula for formal power series
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra
and $f$ a formal power series over $R$, with $j$-th formal derivative $f^{(j)}$, and write
$[X^i]h$ for the coefficient of $X^i$ in a power series $h$. In the ring of formal power series
over $R$ in two variables $t$ and $u$,

$$\sum_{i, j \ge 0} \frac{1}{j!}\, [X^i] f^{(j)}\; t^i u^j = f(t + u),$$

where $f(t + u)$ is the substitution of $t + u$ into $f$. In other words, the exponential
generating series $\sum_j f^{(j)}(t)\, u^j / j!$ of the successive derivatives of $f$ is
$f(t + u)$.

## Sources

- Emanuele Munarini, *Combinatorial Identities for the Tricomi Polynomials*, Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), Article 20.9.4, equation (5.32).

articles.title: Chinese remainder theorem as an algebra isomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative semiring,
let $R$ be a commutative ring that is a $K$-algebra, and let $(I_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family
of ideals of $R$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$ that are pairwise coprime, that is,
$I_i + I_j = R$ for $i \ne j$. Then the map sending the class of $r \in R$ to
$(r \bmod I_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras from $R / \bigcap_i I_i$ to
$\prod_i R / I_i$.

articles.title: Base change of $K(X)/(f)$ along a factorization of $f$ over $K'$
articles.statement:
Let $K$ and $K'$
be fields with $K'$ a $K$-algebra, let $f \in K[X]$, and let $(g_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family
of irreducible polynomials in $K'[X]$, indexed by a finite type $\iota$, that are pairwise
non-associated and whose product $\prod_i g_i$ is associated (equal up to a unit) to the image
of $f$ in $K'[X]$. Then there is an isomorphism of $K'$-algebras

$$(K[X]/(f)) \otimes_K K' \cong \prod_{i \in \iota} K'[X]/(g_i),$$

where the tensor product is a $K'$-algebra through its right factor. For $p \in K[X]$ with
class $[p]$ in $K[X]/(f)$ and for $c \in K'$, it sends $[p] \otimes c$ to the family of the
classes of $c\,p$ modulo the $g_i$, with $p$ read in $K'[X]$.

## Sources

- This is the algebraic decomposition in ATLAS N86, Corollary 4.39 of [MIT 18.785 *Number Theory I*](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-785-number-theory-i-fall-2021/). The corresponding upstream declaration is [`TensorSplitting.adjoinRoot_tensor_algEquiv_prod`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean/blob/e8b31c5cb0bec89b487ce33fe525a2c0b0f8b9c6/v1/Atlas/NumberTheoryI/code/Chapter4/TensorSplitting.lean#L146-L160). There, `L` is presented as `K[X] / (f)`, the extension `K' / K` is arbitrary, and the distinct irreducible factors of `f` over `K'` are represented here by `g`, `hirr`, `hne`, and `hprod`. The source assumes that `f` is irreducible and separable in order to say that `L / K` is a finite separable field extension. Those assumptions are not needed for this CRT decomposition of the explicitly presented algebra `AdjoinRoot f`; accordingly, this theorem makes no stronger field or finite-etale claim about its factors.

articles.title: Weak Nullstellensatz, kernel form
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number. An ideal $I$ of the
polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ is maximal if and only if there is a point
$a \in \mathbb{C}^n$ such that $I$ is the kernel of the evaluation homomorphism
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to \mathbb{C}$, $f \mapsto f(a)$.

articles.title: Weak Nullstellensatz, quotient form
articles.statement:
Let $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ be polynomials in
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ and let $A = \mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(P_1, \ldots, P_m)$.
An ideal $J$ of $A$ is maximal if and only if there is a common zero $a \in \mathbb{C}^n$ of
$P_1, \ldots, P_m$ such that $J$ is the image in $A$ of the ideal of polynomials vanishing at
$a$.

articles.title: Vanishing ideal of a point
articles.statement:
For a point $a \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the ideal of polynomials in
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ that vanish on $\{a\}$ equals the kernel of the evaluation
homomorphism $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to \mathbb{C}$, $f \mapsto f(a)$.

articles.title: An ideal is the intersection of its contracted localizations at maximal ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$
be a commutative ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A$, let
$\varphi_{\mathfrak{m}} \colon A \to A_{\mathfrak{m}}$ be the canonical map to the localization
of $A$ at $\mathfrak{m}$. Then
$I = \bigcap_{\mathfrak{m}} \varphi_{\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}(I A_{\mathfrak{m}})$, the intersection
over all maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A$: an ideal is the intersection of the contractions
to $A$ of its extensions to the localizations at the maximal ideals.

articles.title: An ideal is the intersection of its contracted localizations at prime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$
be a commutative ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ of $A$, let
$\varphi_{\mathfrak{p}} \colon A \to A_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the canonical map to the localization
of $A$ at $\mathfrak{p}$. Then
$I = \bigcap_{\mathfrak{p}} \varphi_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-1}(I A_{\mathfrak{p}})$, the intersection
over all prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}$ of $A$: an ideal is the intersection of the contractions
to $A$ of its extensions to the localizations at the prime ideals.

articles.title: A submodule is the intersection of its saturations at the maximal ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring, $V$ an $A$-module and $M$ a submodule of $V$. For a maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m$ of $A$, let $M_{\mathfrak m}$ be the saturation of $M$ at $A \setminus \mathfrak m$,
that is, the set of $v \in V$ with $s v \in M$ for some $s \in A \setminus \mathfrak m$. Then $M$
is the intersection of the submodules $M_{\mathfrak m}$ over all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$
of $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 2.3, Proposition 2.6, maximal-ideal form.

articles.title: Intersections of saturations over maximal and over prime ideals agree
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring, $V$ an $A$-module and $M$ a submodule of $V$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$
of $A$, let $M_{\mathfrak p}$ be the saturation of $M$ at $A \setminus \mathfrak p$, that is,
the set of $v \in V$ with $s v \in M$ for some $s \in A \setminus \mathfrak p$. Then the
intersection of the $M_{\mathfrak m}$ over all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ equals the
intersection of the $M_{\mathfrak p}$ over all prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $A$.

articles.title: The image of an ideal in the fraction field is the intersection of its localizations at maximal ideals
articles.statement:
**The image of an ideal in the fraction field is the intersection of its localizations at
maximal ideals.** Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be an ideal of
$A$, and let $M \subseteq K$ be the image of $I$ under the canonical map $A \to K$, an
$A$-submodule of $K$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A$, let $M_{\mathfrak{m}}$ be the
localization of $M$ at $\mathfrak{m}$: the set of $x \in K$ such that $s x \in M$ for some
$s \in A \setminus \mathfrak{m}$. Then $M = \bigcap_{\mathfrak{m}} M_{\mathfrak{m}}$, the
intersection over all maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A$, taken inside $K$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 2.3, Corollary 2.7, maximal-ideal form.

articles.title: A submodule is the intersection of its saturations at the prime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring, $V$ an $A$-module and $M$ a submodule of $V$. For a prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $A$, let $M_{\mathfrak p}$ be the saturation of $M$ at $A \setminus \mathfrak p$,

is the intersection of the submodules $M_{\mathfrak p}$ over all prime ideals $\mathfrak p$
of $A$.

articles.title: The image of an ideal in the fraction field is the intersection of its localizations at prime ideals
articles.statement:

prime ideals.** Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be an ideal of

articles.title: Contracted localizations of an ideal: the maximal and prime intersections agree
articles.statement:
Let $A$
be a commutative ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ of $A$, let
$\varphi_{\mathfrak{p}} \colon A \to A_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the canonical map to the localization
of $A$ at $\mathfrak{p}$. Then
$\bigcap_{\mathfrak{m}} \varphi_{\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}(I A_{\mathfrak{m}}) =
\bigcap_{\mathfrak{p}} \varphi_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-1}(I A_{\mathfrak{p}})$, where the left
intersection runs over all maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}$ of $A$ and the right one over all
prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}$ of $A$.

articles.title: Saturation of a submodule at a submonoid
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $V$ an
$A$-module, $M$ a submodule of $V$ and $S$ a submonoid of $A$. The saturation of $M$ at $S$ is the
submodule of $V$ consisting of the elements $v \in V$ such that $s v \in M$ for some $s \in S$.

Writing $S^{-1}V$ for the localization of $V$ at $S$ and $S^{-1}M \subseteq S^{-1}V$ for that of
$M$, it is the preimage of $S^{-1}M$ under the localization map $V \to S^{-1}V$, that is, the
contraction to $V$ of the extension of $M$ to the localization at $S$.

articles.title: Membership in the saturation
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $V$ an $A$-module, $M$ a
submodule of $V$ and $S$ a submonoid of $A$. An element $v \in V$ lies in the saturation of $M$ at
$S$ if and only if $s v \in M$ for some $s \in S$.

articles.title: Membership is detected at the maximal ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $V$ an
$A$-module, $M$ a submodule of $V$ and $v \in V$. Suppose that for every maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m$ of $A$, $v$ lies in the saturation of $M$ at $A \setminus \mathfrak m$, that is,
$s v \in M$ for some $s \in A \setminus \mathfrak m$. Then $v \in M$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 2.3, Proposition 2.6, element form.

articles.title: Membership is detected at the prime ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $V$ an
$A$-module, $M$ a submodule of $V$ and $v \in V$. Suppose that for every prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ of $A$, $v$ lies in the saturation of $M$ at $A \setminus \mathfrak p$, that is,
$s v \in M$ for some $s \in A \setminus \mathfrak p$. Then $v \in M$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 2.3, Proposition 2.6, element form.

articles.title: Denominator of the top coefficient on a circuit
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and
for a finite set $Y \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $f_Y \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ for the interpolation
polynomial of $f$ on $Y$. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be a finite circuit for $f$: $f_X$ does not
have integer coefficients, but $f_{X \setminus \{a\}}$ has integer coefficients for every
$a \in X$. Let $c$ be the coefficient of $x^{|X|-1}$ in $f_X$ and let $q \ge 1$ be the denominator
of $c$ in lowest terms. Then $q \ne 1$, so $c$ is not an integer, and $q$ divides $a - b$ for all
$a, b \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 7, with the circuit definition preceding it.

articles.title: Degree bound for the interpolation polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and
$f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$
has degree less than $|X|$, where the zero polynomial has degree $-\infty$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Section 1.

articles.title: The interpolation polynomial agrees with the function on its nodes
articles.statement:
Let
$X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial
$f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$ satisfies $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Section 1.

articles.title: Integer polynomials take a large value at a small nonnegative integer
articles.statement:
Let
$f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ have degree $d$. Then there is an integer $x$ with $0 \le x \le d$ such that
$|f(x)| \ge d!/2^d$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 5.

articles.title: Non-polynomial LIP functions on the integers that are small on an infinite set
articles.statement:
Let
$\tau : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\tau(n) \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Write
$\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial functions on $\mathbb{Z}$:
the functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose restriction to every finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}$
agrees with a polynomial with integer coefficients. Then there is $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$
that is not of the form $x \mapsto p(x)$ for any $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$, together with an infinite
set $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ such that $|f(x)| < |x|^{\tau(|x|)}$ for every $x \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Infinite ascending chains of principal ideals in LIP rings
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be
infinite, and write $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$:
the functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose restriction to every finite subset of $U$ agrees with a
polynomial with integer coefficients. Then there are $g_0, g_1, g_2, \ldots \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$
such that the principal ideals of $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ they generate form a strictly increasing chain
$(g_0) \subsetneq (g_1) \subsetneq (g_2) \subsetneq \cdots$.

In particular $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ is not Noetherian.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Exchange formula for interpolation polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for
a finite set $Y \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $f_Y \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ for the interpolation polynomial
of $f$ on $Y$. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and $a, b \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus X$, and let
$c$ be the coefficient of $x^{|X|+1}$ in $f_{X \cup \{a, b\}}$. Then

$$f_{X \cup \{a\}} = f_{X \cup \{b\}} + c\,(a - b) \prod_{z \in X} (x - z).$$

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 6.

articles.title: Interpolation polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite and
$f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. The interpolation polynomial $f_X \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ of $f$ on $X$
is the Lagrange interpolation polynomial: the unique polynomial with rational coefficients of
degree less than $|X|$ such that $f_X(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Section 1 and Definition 3.

articles.title: LIP functions with infinitely many prime values are irreducible
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, and write $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial
functions on $U$: the functions $U \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose restriction to every finite subset of $U$
agrees with a polynomial with integer coefficients. Let $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$. If $|f(x)|$ is a
prime number for infinitely many $x \in U$, then $f$ is irreducible in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 2.

articles.title: LIP continuation at two points
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for a finite set
$Y \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $f_Y \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ for the interpolation polynomial of $f$ on
$Y$. For $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer
polynomial functions on $S$: the functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose restriction to every finite
subset of $S$ agrees with a polynomial with integer coefficients. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be
finite and $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $f_{X \cup \{a, b\}}$ does not have integer
coefficients, while $f_{X \cup \{a\}}$ and $f_{X \cup \{b\}}$ both do (this forces $a \ne b$ and
$a, b \notin X$). Put $V = \{x \in \mathbb{Z} : \gcd(x - a, a - b) = 1\}$. Then $|a - b| \ge 2$,
and there is a function $g : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $g(x) = f(x)$ for all
$x \in X \cup \{a, b\}$ whose restriction to $X \cup V \cup \{a\}$ lies in
$\mathrm{LIP}(X \cup V \cup \{a\})$ and whose restriction to $X \cup V \cup \{b\}$ lies in
$\mathrm{LIP}(X \cup V \cup \{b\})$.

This is the form of Theorem 8 established in its proof in the source.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 8.

articles.title: A locally integer polynomial function with infinitely many zeros is zero
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and let $f : U \to \mathbb{Z}$ lie in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of
locally integer polynomial functions on $U$. If $f(x) = 0$ for infinitely many $x \in U$, then
$f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on a union of sets
articles.statement:
For $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, write
$\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Let
$(V_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of subsets of $\mathbb{Z}$ with union $U = \bigcup_{i \in I} V_i$.
Suppose that for all $i, j \in I$, not necessarily distinct, and all $a_1 \in V_i$ and
$a_2 \in V_j$ with $a_1 \ne a_2$, the set $V_i \cap V_j$ contains infinitely many elements of
$\{a_1 + (a_2 - a_1) n : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$. Then for every $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the
restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if, for every $i \in I$, the
restriction of $f$ to $V_i$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(V_i)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 9.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions agreeing on an infinite subset are equal
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq V \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $U$ infinite, and let $f, g : V \to \mathbb{Z}$ lie in
the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(V)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $V$. If $f(x) = g(x)$ for
every $x \in U$, then $f = g$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on cofinite subsets of the integers
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ have finite complement, let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for
$S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial (LIP)
functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and
only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$ with finite complement in $\mathbb{Z}$ such
that the restriction of $f$ to $W$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(W)$.

In the cofinite topology on $\mathbb{Z}$ the nonempty open sets are the sets with finite
complement, so this says that a function which is LIP on an open neighbourhood of each point of
a nonempty open set $U$ is LIP on $U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on cofinite sets of positive integers
articles.statement:
Let
$\mathbb{N}^+ = \{n \in \mathbb{Z} : n > 0\}$, let $U \subseteq \mathbb{N}^+$ with
$\mathbb{N}^+ \setminus U$ finite, let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for
$S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer polynomial (LIP)
functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and
only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$ with $\mathbb{N}^+ \setminus W$ finite such
that the restriction of $f$ to $W$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(W)$.

In the cofinite topology on $\mathbb{N}^+$ the nonempty open sets are the subsets with finite
complement, so this says that a function which is LIP on an open neighbourhood of each point of
a nonempty open set $U$ is LIP on $U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on cofinite sets of primes
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be the set of
positive prime numbers in $\mathbb{Z}$, let $U \subseteq P$ with $P \setminus U$ finite, let
$f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and for $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the
ring of locally integer polynomial (LIP) functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of
$f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$
with $P \setminus W$ finite such that the restriction of $f$ to $W$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(W)$.

In the cofinite topology on $P$ the nonempty open sets are the subsets with finite complement,
so this says that a function which is LIP on an open neighbourhood of each point of a nonempty
open set $U$ is LIP on $U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 5.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on density one subsets of the integers
articles.statement:
Say that
$S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ has density one if $\#(S \cap [-x, x]) / (2x + 1) \to 1$ as the natural
number $x$ tends to infinity, and write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally integer
polynomial (LIP) functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ have density one and
let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
if and only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$ of density one such that the
restriction of $f$ to $W$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(W)$.

In the density one topology on $\mathbb{Z}$ the nonempty open sets are the sets of density one,
so this says that a function which is LIP on an open neighbourhood of each point of a nonempty
open set $U$ is LIP on $U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on density one sets of positive integers
articles.statement:
Say that
a set $S$ of positive integers has natural density one if $\#(S \cap [1, x]) / x \to 1$ as the
natural number $x$ tends to infinity, and write $\mathrm{LIP}(S)$ for the ring of locally
integer polynomial (LIP) functions $S \to \mathbb{Z}$. Let $U$ be a set of positive integers of
natural density one and let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then the restriction of $f$ to $U$
lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if every $a \in U$ lies in some $W \subseteq U$ of natural
density one such that the restriction of $f$ to $W$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(W)$.

In the density one topology on the positive integers the nonempty open sets are the sets of
natural density one, so this says that a function which is LIP on an open neighbourhood of each
point of a nonempty open set $U$ is LIP on $U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Locally integer polynomial functions on an infinite set form a domain
articles.statement:
For every infinite
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions
$U \to \mathbb{Z}$ is an integral domain.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Newton series of locally integer polynomial functions
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, let
$\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to U$ be a bijection. For a
sequence of integers $a = (a_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ define $f_a : U \to \mathbb{Z}$ by

$$f_a(u) = \sum_{k=0}^{\sigma^{-1}(u)} a_k \prod_{i=0}^{k-1} (u - \sigma(i)).$$

Then $f_a$ lies in the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ for
every sequence $a$, and every $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$ equals $f_a$ for exactly one sequence $a$.

For $u = \sigma(m)$ every product with $k > m$ contains the factor $u - \sigma(m) = 0$, so $f_a$
is the formal series $\sum_{k \ge 0} a_k \prod_{i < k} (x - \sigma(i))$ evaluated at $x = u$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 1, reindexed from `σ(1), σ(2), …`.

articles.title: Units of $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
articles.statement:
For every infinite set $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the only
units of the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ are the
constant functions $1$ and $-1$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 4.

articles.title: The ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of locally integer polynomial functions
articles.statement:
For
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ is the subring of the ring of all functions
$U \to \mathbb{Z}$ (with pointwise operations) consisting of the functions $f$ such that for
every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$
for all $x \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Definitions 1 and 2.

articles.title: Gluing LIP functions on two intersecting progressions
articles.statement:
Let $a_1, a_2 \ge 0$ and
$d_1, d_2 \ge 1$ be integers, let $U_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{Z}, n \ge 0\}$ for
$i = 1, 2$, and suppose $U_1 \cap U_2$ is nonempty. If $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ restricts
to an element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U_1)$ on $U_1$ and to an element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U_2)$ on $U_2$,
then the restriction of $f$ to $U_1 \cup U_2$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U_1 \cup U_2)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 6.

articles.title: $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$ is closed under composition
articles.statement:
If $f$ and $g$ lie in
$\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions
$\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, then so does the composite $x \mapsto f(g(x))$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 5.

articles.title: $\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$ is closed under the discrete derivative
articles.statement:
If $f$ lies in
$\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions
$\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, then so does the function $x \mapsto f(x) - f(x - 1)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Integrality of low-degree interpolants
articles.statement:
Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be finite, let
$q \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ have degree less than $|X|$, and let $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfy
$q(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in X$. Then $q$ has integer coefficients, that is, $q$ is the image in
$\mathbb{Q}[x]$ of a polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Membership in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
articles.statement:
For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and $f : U \to \mathbb{Z}$,
$f$ lies in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ if and only if for every finite subset $X \subseteq U$ there is a
polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $p(x) = f(x)$ for all $x \in X$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Definition 1.

articles.title: A LIP function bounded by $C|x|^d$ infinitely often is a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, let $C$ be a real number and $d \ge 0$ an integer, and let
$f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$. If $|f(x)| \le C|x|^d$ for infinitely many $x \in U$, then there is a
polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(x) = p(x)$ for all $x \in U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 3.

articles.title: LIP functions on $\mathbb{Z}$ below the factorial bound are polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $f$ lie in
$\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$, the ring of locally integer polynomial functions
$\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. If $|f(x)| < (2|x| - 1)!/2^{2|x| - 1}$ for all but finitely many
$x \in \mathbb{Z}$, then there is a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(x) = p(x)$ for all
$x \in \mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Theorem 7.

articles.title: $\mathbb{Z}(x)$ is algebraically closed in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$
be infinite, and map each $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ to the function $u \mapsto p(u)$ in
$\mathrm{LIP}(U)$. Let $f \in \mathrm{LIP}(U)$ and let $Q$ be a nonzero polynomial with
coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $Q(f) = 0$ in $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$, where the
coefficients of $Q$ are mapped into $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ in this way. Then there is
$p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(u) = p(u)$ for all $u \in U$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 3.

articles.title: Two intersecting progressions share infinitely many terms with a third
articles.statement:
Let
$a_1, a_2, d_1, d_2, a, b$ be natural numbers with $d_1, d_2 > 0$, where
$\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let $P_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for
$i = 1, 2$. If $a \in P_1$, $b \in P_2$, $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty and $a \neq b$, then
$P_1 \cap P_2$ contains infinitely many elements of the progression
$\{\min(a, b) + |a - b|\, n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 9.

articles.title: Intersection of two arithmetic progressions of natural numbers
articles.statement:
Let $a_1, a_2, d_1, d_2$
be natural numbers with $d_1, d_2 > 0$, where $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$, and let
$P_i = \{a_i + d_i n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for $i = 1, 2$. Then $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty if
and only if $\gcd(d_1, d_2)$ divides the integer $a_1 - a_2$, and if $P_1 \cap P_2$ is nonempty,
then $P_1 \cap P_2 = \{a_3 + \operatorname{lcm}(d_1, d_2)\, n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ for some
$a_3 \in \mathbb{N}$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 8.

articles.title: Values of the evaluation map into LIP(U)
articles.statement:
For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, an integer
polynomial $p \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $u \in U$, the image of $p$ under the evaluation map
$\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$ takes the value $p(u)$ at $u$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Integer polynomials embed in LIP(U)
articles.statement:
For every infinite set $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the
evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$, sending $p$ to the function $u \mapsto p(u)$,
is injective: distinct integer polynomials give distinct functions on $U$.

The other part of Lemma 1, that $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ is a subring of the ring of all functions
$U \to \mathbb{Z}$, holds by construction.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 1.

articles.title: The evaluation map from $\mathbb{Z}(x)$ to $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$
articles.statement:
For $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$,
the evaluation map is the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ to the ring $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$ of
locally integer polynomial functions on $U$ that sends each integer polynomial $p$ to the function
$U \to \mathbb{Z}$, $u \mapsto p(u)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Prime integer polynomials stay prime in LIP(U)
articles.statement:
Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be infinite
and let $p$ be a prime element of $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ (a prime of $\mathbb{Z}$, or an irreducible
integer polynomial of content $1$). Then the function $u \mapsto p(u)$, the image of $p$ under
the evaluation map $\mathbb{Z}[x] \to \mathrm{LIP}(U)$, is a prime element of $\mathrm{LIP}(U)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Corollary 2.

articles.title: The triangular-number function is not LIP on the integers
articles.statement:
The function
$x \mapsto x(x+1)/2$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ (an integer, since $x(x+1)$ is even) does not belong to
$\mathrm{LIP}(\mathbb{Z})$: no integer polynomial $p$ takes the values $0, 0, 1$ at $-1, 0, 1$,
since $1 - (-1)$ must divide $p(1) - p(-1)$.

## Sources

- Alexander Borisov, *Locally Integer Polynomial Functions*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A41, Section 1 and Example 2.

articles.title: Surjections from a finite product of fields are coordinate restrictions up to isomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite type, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are
$K$-algebras, and $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra. For every surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism
$\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ there are a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$ and a
$K$-algebra isomorphism $e : B \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ such that $e \circ \varphi$ is the
coordinate restriction $(x_i)_{i \in \iota} \mapsto (x_i)_{i \in S}$.

articles.title: A surjective image of a finite product of fields is isomorphic to a subproduct
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be
a field, $\iota$ a finite type, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, and
$B$ a commutative $K$-algebra. If $\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ is a surjective
$K$-algebra homomorphism, then there is a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$ such that $B$ is
isomorphic as a $K$-algebra to $\prod_{i \in S} F_i$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of a finite product of fields up to permutation
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, and let
$(F_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(G_j)_{j \in J}$ be families of fields that are $K$-algebras, indexed by
finite types $I$ and $J$. If $e : \prod_{i \in I} F_i \to \prod_{j \in J} G_j$ is an isomorphism
of $K$-algebras, then there is a bijection $\sigma : I \to J$ such that $F_i$ is isomorphic to
$G_{\sigma(i)}$ as a $K$-algebra for every $i \in I$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N83, Corollary 4.33.

articles.title: Kernel membership in a finite product of fields is componentwise
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field,
$\iota$ a finite type, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, $B$ a
commutative $K$-algebra and $\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ a $K$-algebra
homomorphism. For $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$, $\varphi(x) = 0$ if and only if for every
$i \in \iota$ the coordinate $x_i$ lies in the ideal of $F_i$ generated by the image of
$\ker \varphi$ under the $i$-th projection $\prod_{j \in \iota} F_j \to F_i$.

articles.title: Kernel of coordinate restriction
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of
fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a finite subset.
An element $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$ is sent to $0$ by the coordinate restriction
$\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ if and only if $x_i = 0$ for every $i \in S$.

articles.title: Membership in the selected indices
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite type,
$(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra and
$\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ a $K$-algebra homomorphism. An index $i \in \iota$
belongs to the selected indices of $\varphi$ if and only if the ideal of $F_i$ generated by the
image of $\ker \varphi$ under the $i$-th projection $\prod_{j \in \iota} F_j \to F_i$ is zero.

articles.title: Coordinates of a restriction
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of
fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a finite subset.
For $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i$ and $s \in S$, the $s$-th coordinate of the coordinate
restriction of $x$ to $S$ is $x_s$.

articles.title: Coordinate restriction is surjective
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a
family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$, and $S \subseteq \iota$ a
finite subset. The coordinate restriction $\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ is
surjective.

A preimage is obtained by extending by zero outside $S$.

articles.title: Coordinate restriction
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields
that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$. For a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$, the
coordinate restriction is the $K$-algebra homomorphism
$\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ sending $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ to
$(x_i)_{i \in S}$.

articles.title: Product decompositions and idempotents
articles.statement:
A commutative ring $Q$ is isomorphic to a product
$R \times S$ of two nontrivial rings $R$ and $S$ if and only if $Q$ contains an idempotent $e$
with $e \neq 0$ and $e \neq 1$.

In the reverse direction the two factors are the quotients $Q/(e)$ and $Q/(1 - e)$.

articles.title: Selected indices of a homomorphism
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite type,
$(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra and
$\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ a $K$-algebra homomorphism. The selected indices of
$\varphi$ form the finite set of those $i \in \iota$ for which the ideal of $F_i$ generated by the
image of $\ker \varphi$ under the $i$-th projection $\prod_{j \in \iota} F_j \to F_i$ is zero.

articles.title: Ghost components determine Witt vector coefficients
articles.statement:
Ghost components determine Witt vector coefficients when `p` is a
non-zero-divisor.

articles.title: Divisibility of Witt coefficients from divisible ghost components
articles.statement:
If a ghost component of a Witt vector is highly `p`-divisible and the
reduction mod `p` is reduced, all lower coefficients lie in `(p)`.

articles.title: Ghost data compatible with a Frobenius lift come from a Witt vector
articles.statement:
Compatible ghost data with a Frobenius lift is realized by a Witt
vector.

articles.title: Homomorphisms from Witt vectors over finite fields commute with Frobenius
articles.statement:
Ring homomorphisms out of Witt vectors over a finite field commute with
Frobenius.

articles.title: Adjacency in the zero-divisor graph
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Two vertices $v$
and $w$ of the zero-divisor graph of $R$ are adjacent if and only if $v \neq w$ and $vw = 0$.

articles.title: Vertices are the nonzero zero divisors
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. An element
$r \in R$ is a vertex of the zero-divisor graph of $R$ if and only if $r \neq 0$ and $r$ is a
zero divisor, that is, $sr = 0$ for some nonzero $s \in R$.

articles.title: Nonzero zero divisors
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, this is the set of elements
$r \in R$ with $r \neq 0$ such that $sr = 0$ for some nonzero $s \in R$, that is, the nonzero
zero divisors of $R$. They are the vertices of the zero-divisor graph of $R$.

articles.title: The zero-divisor graph
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, the zero-divisor graph of $R$ is
the simple graph whose vertices are the nonzero zero divisors of $R$, in which two distinct
vertices $v$ and $w$ are adjacent exactly when $vw = 0$.

articles.title: Finiteness over a subring containing the invariants
articles.statement:
Over a Noetherian ring `R`, suppose `B` is finite type over `R` and
the faithful image of `A` in `B` contains every fixed element of a finite
group acting on `B` by semiring automorphisms. Then `B` is finite over `A`
and `A` is finite type over `R`.

articles.title: Hyperplane sum
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$ and a subgroup $G$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$, the hyperplane sum of $G$ is the rational number
$r = \sum_W ((p - 1) \alpha_W + s_W - 1)$, where $W$ runs over the maximal proper submodules
of $V = (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ (the hyperplanes of $V$ when $p$ is prime) and
$(p - 1) \alpha_W + s_W - 1$ is the hyperplane term of $W$: here $N_W$ is the number of elements
of the pointwise stabilizer $G_W$ of $W$ in $G$ (taken to be $0$ if $G_W$ is infinite),
$\alpha_W$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $N_W$ (which is $0$ unless $p$
is prime and $N_W \ne 0$), and $s_W = N_W / p^{\alpha_W}$, so that $N_W = p^{\alpha_W} s_W$.
The sum is defined to be $0$ if infinitely many of its terms are nonzero, which can happen only
for $p = 0$.

articles.title: Hyperplane term
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, a subgroup $G$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ and a submodule $W$ of $V = (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$, let
$N$ be the number of elements of the pointwise stabilizer $G_W$ of $W$ in $G$ (taken to be $0$
if $G_W$ is infinite), let $\alpha_W$ be the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $N$
(which is $0$ unless $p$ is prime and $N \ne 0$), and let $s_W = N / p^{\alpha_W}$, so that
$N = p^{\alpha_W} s_W$ and $p \nmid s_W$ when $p$ is prime and $N \ne 0$. The hyperplane term of
$W$ is the rational number $(p - 1) \alpha_W + s_W - 1$.

articles.title: Homogeneous component of the invariant ring
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, a subgroup
$G$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the degree-$m$ component
$T_m$ of the invariant ring $T$ of $G$ is the $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-submodule of the polynomial
ring $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})[x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}]$ consisting of the homogeneous polynomials $f$
of degree $m$ that are fixed by the linear substitution $x_i \mapsto \sum_j g_{ij} x_j$ of every
$g \in G$, that is, with $f(gx) = f(x)$ as polynomials for all $g \in G$, where
$x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ is the column vector of variables.

articles.title: Linear substitution by a matrix
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$ and an $n \times n$ matrix
$g$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, the linear substitution by $g$ is the
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-algebra endomorphism of the polynomial ring
$(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})[x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}]$ that sends each variable $x_i$ to
$\sum_j g_{ij} x_j$. Viewing polynomials as functions on $V = (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$, it sends
$f$ to the function $x \mapsto f(gx)$.

articles.title: Benson–Crawley-Boevey hyperplane formula (Kourovka 12.36)
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$, every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$, with $P(t)$ the
Poincaré series of the invariant ring of $G$ and $r$ the hyperplane sum of $G$, there are
polynomials $A, B \in \mathbb{Q}[t]$ with $B(1) \ne 0$ and $B(t) (1 - t)^n P(t) = A(t)$ in
$\mathbb{Q}[[t]]$ such that

$$\frac{A(1) B'(1) - A'(1) B(1)}{B(1)^2} = \frac{r}{2 |G|}.$$

That is, the Carlisle–Kropholler conjecture on the second Laurent coefficient holds: the
coefficient $a_{-n+1}$ in the expansion $P(t) = \sum_{i \ge -n} a_i (1 - t)^i$ equals
$r / (2 |G|)$.

Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive records the conjecture as proved by Benson and Crawley-Boevey
(Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995)), with a second proof by Neeman (Comment. Math. Helv. 70 (1995))
based on the Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem. Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.),
Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026),
Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.36 (D. Carlisle, P. H. Kropholler); resolution: D. J. Benson
and W. W. Crawley-Boevey, Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995), no. 5, 435-440; A. Neeman, Comment.
Math. Helv. 70 (1995), no. 3, 339-349, Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.36: the conjecture is proved.

articles.title: Carlisle–Kropholler conjecture on the second Laurent coefficient (Kourovka 12.36)
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every prime $p$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subgroup $G$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$, with $P(t)$ the Poincaré series of the invariant ring of $G$ and
$r$ the hyperplane sum of $G$, there are polynomials $A, B \in \mathbb{Q}[t]$ with $B(1) \ne 0$
and $B(t) (1 - t)^n P(t) = A(t)$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[t]]$ such that

$$\frac{A(1) B'(1) - A'(1) B(1)}{B(1)^2} = \frac{r}{2 |G|}.$$

Here $(1 - t)^n P(t) = A(t) / B(t) = a_{-n} + a_{-n+1} (1 - t) + \cdots$, where
$P(t) = \sum_{i \ge -n} a_i (1 - t)^i$ is the Laurent expansion of $P$ at $t = 1$, so the left
side is $a_{-n+1} = -(A / B)'(1)$, and the conjecture says $a_{-n+1} = r / (2 |G|)$.

articles.title: Poincaré series of the invariant ring
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$ and a subgroup $G$
of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$, the Poincaré series of the invariant ring $T$ of $G$
is the formal power series $P(t) = \sum_{m \ge 0} b_m t^m$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, where $b_m$ is the
rank over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ (the dimension, when $p$ is prime) of the degree-$m$
homogeneous component $T_m$ of $T$.

articles.title: Pointwise stabilizer
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $n$, a subgroup $G$ of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ and a submodule $W$ of $V = (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$,
the pointwise stabilizer $G_W$ of $W$ in $G$ is the set of all $g \in G$ with $g w = w$ for every
$w \in W$, where $g$ acts on column vectors by matrix multiplication.

articles.title: Ring equivalences of local rings induce equivalent completions
articles.statement:
A ring equivalence between local rings induces an equivalence of their
maximal-ideal adic completions.

articles.title: Ring equivalences induce equivalences of adic completions
articles.statement: A ring equivalence induces an equivalence of adic completions.

articles.title: Lifting compatible ring maps to adic completions
articles.statement:
A ring homomorphism compatible with the adic topologies lifts to a map
from the adic completion into an adically complete target.

articles.title: Adic completeness of multivariate power series
articles.statement:
If `R` is adically complete at its maximal ideal, then `MvPowerSeries σ R`
is adically complete at its maximal ideal.

articles.title: Finite local extensions of adically complete rings are complete
articles.statement:
A finite local extension of an adically complete local ring is adically
complete at its maximal ideal.

articles.title: Adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian
articles.statement: The adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.

articles.title: Ideals contract to themselves along local adic completion
articles.statement:
Ideals contract back to themselves along the adic completion map of a
Noetherian local ring.

articles.title: Completion of a Noetherian local ring is faithfully flat
articles.statement:
The adic completion of a Noetherian local ring at its maximal ideal is
faithfully flat.

articles.title: Maximal ideal power quotients transported along an isomorphism
articles.statement:
The finite quotients of `B` by powers of its maximal ideal agree with
those of `A`, transported along an algebra isomorphism with the completion
of `A`.

articles.title: Isomorphism of maximal ideal power quotients of a ring and its completion
articles.statement:
The finite quotient of the completion by a power of its maximal ideal
identifies with the corresponding quotient of the ring.

articles.title: Algebra map between maximal ideal power quotients of a ring and its completion
articles.statement:
The finite quotient of the completion by a power of its maximal ideal
identifies with the corresponding quotient of the ring.

articles.title: Adic completeness at a nilpotent ideal
articles.statement: A ring is adically complete at a nilpotent ideal.

articles.title: Finite free modules over adically complete rings are complete
articles.statement:
If `𝓞` is adically complete at `(p)` and `R` is finite free over `𝓞`,
then `R` is adically complete at `(p)`.

articles.title: Adic completion preserves Krull dimension at least two
articles.statement:
A Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension at least two has an adic
completion of Krull dimension at least two.

articles.title: Flat local maps reflect integrally closed domains
articles.statement:
A flat local homomorphism from a local ring to a domain and integrally
closed local ring forces the source to be a domain and integrally closed.
The flatness is stated with the `Flat` class of Mathlib 4.35, where the
FLT source used the older `RingHom.Flat` spelling.

articles.title: Short prime chains when the completion has dimension at most two
articles.statement:
In a Noetherian local domain whose adic completion has Krull dimension
at most `2`, any prime strictly below a non-maximal prime is `⊥`.

articles.title: Prime chains lift along injective integral maps
articles.statement: Every finite chain of prime ideals lifts along an injective integral algebra map.

articles.title: Injective integral maps preserve Krull dimension
articles.statement: An injective integral algebra map preserves Krull dimension.

articles.title: Krull dimension does not decrease along injective integral maps
articles.statement: Krull dimension cannot decrease along an injective integral algebra map.

articles.title: Krull dimension does not increase along integral algebras
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative
rings and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is integral over $A$. Then the Krull dimension of $B$ is
at most the Krull dimension of $A$.

The structure map $A \to B$ need not be injective. The inequality comes from incomparability:
contracting prime ideals of $B$ to $A$ is strictly monotone, so it gives a strictly monotone map
from the prime spectrum of $B$ to the prime spectrum of $A$.

articles.title: Length bound for a quotient containing a kernel
articles.statement: If `ker f ≤ K`, the length of `M ⧸ K` is at most the length of `N`.

articles.title: Characteristic of the residue field of a local ring
articles.statement:
If `(p : A)` lies in the maximal ideal of a local ring `A`, the residue
field has characteristic `p`: `p` maps to zero in the residue field.

articles.title: Quotient of a local ring by a proper ideal is local
articles.statement:
A quotient of a local ring by a proper ideal is local. Mathlib uses this
fact inline (via `IsLocalRing.of_surjective'`), but does not package it as a
standalone lemma.

articles.title: Kernel of reducing polynomial coefficients modulo an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$. The kernel of the ring homomorphism $A[X] \to (A/I)[X]$ that
reduces every coefficient modulo $I$ is the ideal of $A[X]$ generated by the constant
polynomials $a$ with $a \in I$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring come from residual irreducible factors
articles.statement:
**Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring come from residual irreducible
factors.** Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and for
$f \in A[X]$ write $\bar{f}$ for its image in $(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$. Let $g \in A[X]$ and suppose
that $A[X]/(g)$ is integral over $A$. Then for every maximal ideal $M$ of $A[X]/(g)$ there is a
polynomial $q \in A[X]$ such that $\bar{q}$ is irreducible in $(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$, $\bar{q}$
divides $\bar{g}$, and $M$ is the ideal of $A[X]/(g)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$
and the class of $q$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring, monic case
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and for $f \in A[X]$ write $\bar{f}$ for
its image in $(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$. Let $g \in A[X]$ be monic. Then an ideal $M$ of $A[X]/(g)$ is
maximal if and only if there is a polynomial $q \in A[X]$ such that $\bar{q}$ is irreducible in
$(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$, $\bar{q}$ divides $\bar{g}$, and $M$ is the ideal of $A[X]/(g)$ generated
by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$ and the class of $q$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative local
ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and for $f \in A[X]$ write $\bar{f}$ for its image in
$(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$. Let $g \in A[X]$ and suppose that $A[X]/(g)$ is integral over $A$. Then an
ideal $M$ of $A[X]/(g)$ is maximal if and only if there is a polynomial $q \in A[X]$ such that
$\bar{q}$ is irreducible in $(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$, $\bar{q}$ divides $\bar{g}$, and $M$ is the
ideal of $A[X]/(g)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$ and the class of $q$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring contain the base maximal ideal, monic case
articles.statement:
**Maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra over a local ring contain the base maximal ideal,
monic case.** Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and let
$g \in A[X]$ be monic. Then every maximal ideal $M$ of $A[X]/(g)$ contains the ideal of
$A[X]/(g)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of an integral monogenic algebra over a local ring contain the base maximal ideal
articles.statement:
**Maximal ideals of an integral monogenic algebra over a local ring contain the base maximal
ideal.** Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, let $g \in A[X]$,
and suppose that $A[X]/(g)$ is integral over $A$. Then every maximal ideal $M$ of $A[X]/(g)$
contains the ideal of $A[X]/(g)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$.

articles.title: Residual irreducible factors give maximal ideals of a monogenic algebra
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and for $f \in A[X]$ write $\bar{f}$ for
its image in $(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$. Let $g, q \in A[X]$ be such that $\bar{q}$ is irreducible in
$(A/\mathfrak{m})[X]$ and $\bar{q}$ divides $\bar{g}$. Then the ideal of $A[X]/(g)$ generated by
the image of $\mathfrak{m}$ and the class of $q$ is maximal.

No integrality assumption on $A[X]/(g)$ over $A$ is needed.

articles.title: Maximal ideals of an integral algebra over a local ring contain the base maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and let $B$ be a
commutative $A$-algebra that is integral over $A$. Then every maximal ideal $M$ of $B$ contains
the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak{m}$.

articles.title: The complete local ring reconstruction conjecture is false
articles.statement:
There exist commutative
Noetherian local rings $A$ and $B$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, that
are complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic and $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topologies, such
that $A/\mathfrak m_A^r$ and $B/\mathfrak m_B^r$ are isomorphic as rings for every natural number
$r$, but $A$ and $B$ are not isomorphic as rings.

Van den Dries proves that such rings are isomorphic when the residue field is algebraic over its
prime field, and reports examples by Gabber showing that the answer is no in general.

## Sources

- Lou van den Dries, Isomorphism of complete local noetherian rings and strong approximation, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 136 (2008), 3435-3448, https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-08-09401-X.

articles.title: Complete local ring reconstruction conjecture
articles.statement:
The statement that any two commutative
Noetherian local rings $A$ and $B$, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, that
are complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak m_A$-adic and $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topologies are
isomorphic as rings whenever $A/\mathfrak m_A^r$ and $B/\mathfrak m_B^r$ are isomorphic as rings
for every natural number $r$.

## Sources

- OWR-1453-004.

articles.title: Adjoining a root of an Eisenstein-like polynomial preserves regularity
articles.statement:
Adjoining a root of a monic polynomial whose non-leading coefficients lie
in the maximal ideal and whose constant coefficient lies outside the square
of the maximal ideal preserves regularity and Krull dimension.

articles.title: Regular local rings of dimension at most one are normal domains
articles.statement:
A regular local ring of Krull dimension at most one is a domain and
integrally closed.

articles.title: Multivariable power series over a regular local ring are regular local
articles.statement:
Multivariable power series over a regular local ring form a
regular local ring. The discrete-valuation-ring case follows by typeclass
inference, since a DVR is a regular local ring.

articles.title: Power series over a regular local ring are regular local
articles.statement: Power series over a regular local ring are regular local.

articles.title: $X$ is a regular element of the power series ring
articles.statement: `X` is a regular element of the power series ring.

articles.title: Kernel of the constant coefficient map of power series
articles.statement: The kernel of the constant coefficient map is the span of `X`.

articles.title: Generators of the maximal ideal of a power series ring
articles.statement:
The maximal ideal of `R⟦X⟧` is generated by the image of a generating set
of the maximal ideal of `R` together with `X`.

articles.title: Power series modulo $X$ recover the coefficient ring
articles.statement: Quotienting `R⟦X⟧` by the span of `X` recovers `R`.

articles.title: Krull dimension of a power series ring
articles.statement: The Krull dimension of `R⟦X⟧` is one more than that of `R`.

articles.title: Embedding dimension of a power series ring
articles.statement: The embedding dimension of `R⟦X⟧` is at most one more than that of `R`.

articles.title: Quotient of a regular local ring by a regular parameter is regular
articles.statement:
Quotienting a regular local ring by a parameter outside the square of the
maximal ideal and outside every minimal prime stays regular, with the
embedding dimension dropping by exactly one.

articles.title: Existence of a parameter avoiding minimal primes and the square
articles.statement:
In a Noetherian local ring of positive Krull dimension, there is a
parameter in the maximal ideal, outside its square and outside every
minimal prime.

articles.title: Regular local rings are domains
articles.statement: Every regular local ring is a domain.

articles.title: Unique factorization from a principal ideal ring quotient
articles.statement:
A Noetherian local domain is a unique factorization monoid when
quotienting by a principal prime ideal gives a principal ideal ring.

articles.title: Regular local rings of dimension at most two are UFDs
articles.statement:
A regular local ring of Krull dimension at most two is a unique
factorization monoid.

articles.title: Faithfully flat algebras inside a localization equal the base ring
articles.statement:
A faithfully flat `R`-algebra `S` which embeds compatibly in a localization
`K` of `R` has bijective structure map. No restriction on the denominators
or domain assumptions on the rings are required.

articles.title: Derived direct summand theorem
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a regular commutative ring, let $X$ be a
scheme and let $f \colon X \to \operatorname{Spec} A$ be a proper morphism that is surjective on
underlying points. Let $\varphi \colon A \to \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be the ring map
corresponding to $f$, and let $R\Gamma$ be the right derived functor, between bounded-below
derived categories, of global sections of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules followed by
restriction of scalars along $\varphi$. If the category of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules
has enough injectives, then the composite of $\varphi$, placed in degree $0$, with the canonical
map from $\Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ in degree $0$ to $R\Gamma(\mathcal{O}_X)$ is a split
monomorphism $A \to R\Gamma(\mathcal{O}_X)$ in the bounded-below derived category of
$A$-modules.

## Sources

-. Problem `direct_summand` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Direct summand theorem
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a regular commutative ring and let $B$ be a commutative
$A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $A$-module and on which $A$ acts faithfully
(equivalently, the structure map $A \to B$ is injective). Then there is an $A$-linear map
$\pi \colon B \to A$ with $\pi(a \cdot 1) = a$ for every $a \in A$; that is, $A$ is a direct
summand of $B$ as an $A$-module.

## Sources

-. Problem `direct_summand` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Single complexes in the bounded-below derived category
articles.statement:
For an abelian category $C$ with
a derived category and an integer $n$, the functor sending an object of $C$ to the complex
concentrated in degree $n$, viewed in the bounded-below derived category $D^+(C)$, is naturally
isomorphic to the corresponding single-complex functor into the bounded-below homotopy category
$K^+(C)$ followed by the localization functor $K^+(C) \to D^+(C)$.

articles.title: Eakin–Nagata theorem
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra
that is finitely generated as an $A$-module. If the structure map $A \to B$ is injective and $B$
is Noetherian, then $A$ is Noetherian.

## Sources

- P. M. Eakin Jr., 'The converse to a well known theorem on Noetherian rings', Mathematische Annalen 177 (1968), 278-282, DOI 10.1007/BF01350720.

articles.title: Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules over local rings
articles.statement:
Every projective module over a
commutative local ring is free.

## Sources

- I. Kaplansky, Projective Modules, Ann. Math. 68 (1958), 372-377, DOI 10.2307/1970252.

articles.title: Finite projective modules of fiberwise rank one are invertible
articles.statement:
A finite projective module whose base change to every field has rank
one is invertible.

This is the standard criterion for a module to define a line bundle: it
is used to show that projective modules of constant rank one are
invertible, to construct Picard group elements, and to recognize
invertible sheaves from their fibers.

articles.title: Quillen–Suslin theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $n$ be a natural number. Every finitely
generated projective module over the polynomial ring $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ variables is
free.

Proof: The argument follows Quillen's induction and patching route, using Roberts'
idempotent-matrix proof of local Horrocks; see Quillen (1976), Lam, Lang, and Dicks.

## Sources

- Serre's conjecture proved by D. Quillen, Invent. Math. 36 (1976) and A. A. Suslin, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 229 (1976); Lam, Serre's Problem; Lean states field case over `MvPolynomial (Fin n) k` with PID generalization existing.

articles.title: Tower formula for inertia groups
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. For a subgroup $S \le G$ write
$I_S(\mathfrak P)$ for the inertia group of $\mathfrak P$ in $S$, the set of $\sigma \in S$ with
$\sigma(x) - x \in \mathfrak P$ for all $x \in B$. Then
$e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p) \cdot |I_H(\mathfrak P)| = |I_G(\mathfrak P)|$, where
$e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p)$ is the ramification index of $\mathfrak P_E$ over
$\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: Equal cardinality of an intersection forces containment
articles.statement:
Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of
a group $G$ with $H$ finite. If $H \cap K$ has as many elements as $H$, then $H \le K$.

articles.title: Ramification index one and the inertia group
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $I(\mathfrak P)$ be the
inertia group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) - x \in \mathfrak P$
for all $x \in B$. Then the ramification index $e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p)$ of
$\mathfrak P_E$ over $\mathfrak p$ equals $1$ if and only if $I(\mathfrak P) \le H$.

articles.title: Ramification index one and the inertia field
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $I(\mathfrak P)$ be the
inertia group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) - x \in \mathfrak P$
for all $x \in B$, and let $L^{I(\mathfrak P)}$ be its fixed field in $L$. Then the ramification
index $e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p)$ of $\mathfrak P_E$ over $\mathfrak p$ equals $1$ if and
only if $E \subseteq L^{I(\mathfrak P)}$.

articles.title: Ramification index and inertia degree one and the decomposition field
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $D(\mathfrak P)$ be the
decomposition group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(\mathfrak P) = \mathfrak P$, and let $L^{D(\mathfrak P)}$ be its fixed field in $L$. Let
$e$ and $f$ be the ramification index and the inertia degree of $\mathfrak P_E$ over
$\mathfrak p$. Then $e = 1$ and $f = 1$ if and only if $E \subseteq L^{D(\mathfrak P)}$.

articles.title: Fields below the inertia and decomposition fields
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $I(\mathfrak P)$ be the
inertia group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) - x \in \mathfrak P$
for all $x \in B$, and $D(\mathfrak P)$ its decomposition group, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(\mathfrak P) = \mathfrak P$; let $L^{I(\mathfrak P)}$ and $L^{D(\mathfrak P)}$ be their
fixed fields in $L$, and let $e$ and $f$ be the ramification index and the inertia degree of
$\mathfrak P_E$ over $\mathfrak p$. Then $e = 1$ if and only if $E \subseteq L^{I(\mathfrak P)}$,
and $e = f = 1$ if and only if $E \subseteq L^{D(\mathfrak P)}$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 7.14.

articles.title: Ramification index and inertia degree one and the decomposition group
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $D(\mathfrak P)$ be the
decomposition group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(\mathfrak P) = \mathfrak P$, and let $e$ and $f$ be the ramification index and the
inertia degree of $\mathfrak P_E$ over $\mathfrak p$. Then $e = 1$ and $f = 1$ if and only if
$D(\mathfrak P) \le H$.

articles.title: Tower formula for inertia groups, intersected with the fixing group
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
