over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $I(\mathfrak P)$ be the
inertia group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) - x \in \mathfrak P$
for all $x \in B$. Then
$e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p) \cdot |I(\mathfrak P) \cap H| = |I(\mathfrak P)|$, where
$e(\mathfrak P_E \mid \mathfrak p)$ is the ramification index of $\mathfrak P_E$ over
$\mathfrak p$.

articles.title: Tower formula for decomposition groups
articles.statement:
Let $L/K$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$. Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains
with $B$ a finite torsion-free $A$-algebra, and let $G$ act on $B$ by ring automorphisms as a
Galois group of $B$ over $A$: faithfully, fixing the image of $A$, and with every element of $B$
fixed by $G$ in the image of $A$. Let $E$ be an intermediate field of $L/K$ and $H \le G$ the
subgroup fixing $E$ pointwise. Let $C$ be a Dedekind domain and a torsion-free $A$-algebra, and
give $E$ an $A$-algebra structure and an injective ring map $C \to E$ whose image is the set of
elements of $E$ integral over $A$ (the composite $A \to C \to E$ need not be the given map
$A \to E$). Suppose $B$ is also a finite torsion-free $C$-algebra, with $A \to C \to B$ equal to
$A \to B$, and that $H$, acting on $B$ by restriction, is a Galois group of $B$ over $C$. Let
$\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P$ be maximal ideals of $A$, $C$ and $B$ such that
$\mathfrak P$ lies over $\mathfrak p$ and over $\mathfrak P_E$ and $\mathfrak P_E$ lies over
$\mathfrak p$, and suppose that every prime of $B$ over $\mathfrak p$, and every prime of $B$
over $\mathfrak P_E$, has a separable residue field extension. Let $D(\mathfrak P)$ be the
decomposition group of $\mathfrak P$, the set of $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(\mathfrak P) = \mathfrak P$, and let $e$ and $f$ be the ramification index and the
inertia degree of $\mathfrak P_E$ over $\mathfrak p$. Then
$e f \cdot |D(\mathfrak P) \cap H| = |D(\mathfrak P)|$.

articles.title: The different of a monogenic extension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain with fraction
field $K$, let $L$ be a finite separable extension of $K$, and let $B$ be the integral closure of
$A$ in $L$, assumed to be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ that is torsion-free as an
$A$-module, with compatible algebra maps $A \to K \to L$ and $A \to B \to L$. If $\alpha \in B$
generates $B$ as an $A$-algebra, that is $B = A[\alpha]$, and $f$ is the minimal polynomial of
$\alpha$ over $A$, then the different ideal $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ is the principal ideal
$(f'(\alpha))$ of $B$.

## Sources

- Andrew V. Sutherland, 18.785 Number Theory I, Lecture 12, Proposition 12.24.

articles.title: The discriminant ideal is the norm of the different
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind
domains, with $B$ an $A$-algebra that is finite and torsion-free as an $A$-module. Then the
discriminant ideal $\mathfrak{d}_{B/A}$ is the ideal of $A$ generated by the norms
$N_{B/A}(x)$ of the elements $x$ of the different ideal $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ of $B$ over $A$;
this holds by definition.

articles.title: Tower formula for discriminant ideals
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be Dedekind domains with
algebra maps $A \to B \to C$ whose composite is the algebra map $A \to C$, such that $B$ is
finite and torsion-free over $A$, $C$ is finite and torsion-free over $A$ and over $B$, and the
fraction field of $C$ is separable over the fraction field of $A$. Write $\mathfrak{d}_{B/A}$,
$\mathfrak{d}_{C/A}$ and $\mathfrak{d}_{C/B}$ for the discriminant ideals of $B$ over $A$, of
$C$ over $A$ and of $C$ over $B$, let $n = [\operatorname{Frac} C : \operatorname{Frac} B]$,
and for an ideal $I$ of $B$ let $N_{B/A}(I)$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by the norms of the
elements of $I$. Then
$\mathfrak{d}_{C/A} = \mathfrak{d}_{B/A}^{\,n} \, N_{B/A}(\mathfrak{d}_{C/B})$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Proposition 12.28, second half.

articles.title: Discriminant ideal of a Dedekind extension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains, with
$B$ an $A$-algebra that is finite and torsion-free as an $A$-module. The discriminant ideal
$\mathfrak{d}_{B/A}$ is the ideal of $A$ generated by the norms $N_{B/A}(x)$ of the elements $x$
of the different ideal $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ of $B$ over $A$.

articles.title: Vanishing of the element different
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a commutative
$A$-algebra, $L$ a field that is a $B$-algebra, and $K$ a field with $L$ a $K$-algebra. Let
$\alpha \in B$ and let $f$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$ (taken to be $0$ when
$\alpha$ is not integral over $A$). Then the element different $\delta_{B/A}(\alpha)$ is $0$ if
and only if the image of $\alpha$ in $L$ does not generate $L$ as a $K$-algebra or
$f'(\alpha) = 0$.

articles.title: The element different lies in the different
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain with
fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a finite separable extension of $K$, and let $B$ be the integral
closure of $A$ in $L$, assumed to be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ that is
torsion-free as an $A$-module, with compatible algebra maps $A \to K \to L$ and
$A \to B \to L$. If $\alpha \in B$ and the image of $\alpha$ in $L$ generates $L$ as a
$K$-algebra, then the element different $\delta_{B/A}(\alpha)$ lies in the different ideal
$\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ of $B$ over $A$.

articles.title: Element different of a generator
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a commutative
$A$-algebra, $L$ a field that is a $B$-algebra, and $K$ a field with $L$ a $K$-algebra. Let
$\alpha \in B$ and let $f$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$ (taken to be $0$ when
$\alpha$ is not integral over $A$). If the image of $\alpha$ in $L$ generates $L$ as a
$K$-algebra, then the element different $\delta_{B/A}(\alpha)$ equals $f'(\alpha)$.

articles.title: Element different of a non-generator
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a commutative
$A$-algebra, $L$ a field that is a $B$-algebra, and $K$ a field with $L$ a $K$-algebra. If
$\alpha \in B$ and the image of $\alpha$ in $L$ does not generate $L$ as a $K$-algebra, then the
element different $\delta_{B/A}(\alpha)$ is $0$.

articles.title: Element different
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a commutative $A$-algebra, $L$ a
field that is a $B$-algebra, and $K$ a field with $L$ a $K$-algebra. For $\alpha \in B$, let
$f \in A[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$ (taken to be $0$ when $\alpha$ is not
integral over $A$). The element different $\delta_{B/A}(\alpha) \in B$ is $f'(\alpha)$ when the
image of $\alpha$ in $L$ generates $L$ as a $K$-algebra, and $0$ otherwise.

articles.title: The trace dual commutes with localization
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $L/K$ be a finite separable extension, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$
in $L$, a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicative set of
nonzerodivisors, let $A_S \subseteq K$ be the localization of $A$ at $S$ inside $K$, and let
$B_S$ be a localization of $B$ at the image of $S$ that is also an $A_S$-algebra, with a map
$B_S \to L$ such that all composite maps from $A$, $A_S$, $B$, $B_S$ and $K$ into $L$ agree.
Assume that $B_S$ is a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, torsion-free over $B$, and the
integral closure of $A_S$ in $L$. Write
$B^\vee = \{x \in L : \operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(xB) \subseteq A\}$ and
$B_S^\vee = \{x \in L : \operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(xB_S) \subseteq A_S\}$ for the trace duals. Then
the fractional ideal of $B_S$ generated by $B^\vee$ is $B_S^\vee$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N241, canonical-localization scope; transport to an arbitrary base localization is deferred.

articles.title: Only finitely many primes of the base ramify
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains, where
$B$ is an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $A$-module and the field of
fractions of $B$ is separable over the field of fractions of $A$. Then only finitely many nonzero
prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ are ramified in $B$. Here $\mathfrak p$ is unramified in $B$ when
every prime ideal $\mathfrak P$ of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ is unramified over $A$, that is, the
localization $B_{\mathfrak P}$ is formally unramified over $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 12.20, the statement for primes of $A$.

articles.title: Only finitely many primes of the extension ramify
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains,
where $B$ is an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $A$-module and the
field of fractions of $B$ is separable over the field of fractions of $A$. Then only finitely many
nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak P$ of $B$ are ramified over $A$. Here $\mathfrak P$ is unramified
over $A$ when the localization $B_{\mathfrak P}$ is formally unramified over $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS `NumberTheoryI` Corollary 12.20, the statement for primes of $B$.

articles.title: Height-one form of the discriminant ramification criterion
articles.statement: The original height-one formulation, derived from the standard primary criterion.

articles.title: Not dividing the discriminant implies unramified at a prime
articles.statement:
Height-one compatibility: evaluate the standard unramified-in conclusion
at the particular height-one prime supplied by an original client.

articles.title: Unramified primes are those not dividing the discriminant
articles.statement:
Theorem 12.19, discriminant half, in Mathlib's standard predicate:
`𝔭` is unramified in `B` exactly when it does not divide the discriminant ideal.

articles.title: Ideals below the different
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integrally closed domain with fraction field
$K$, let $L/K$ be a finite separable extension, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$;
assume that $B$ is a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ and is torsion-free as an
$A$-module. Write $B^\vee = \{x \in L : \operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(xB) \subseteq A\}$ for the trace
dual of $B$ and $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ for the different ideal of $B$ over $A$. Then an ideal $I$
of $B$ satisfies $I \subseteq \mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$ if and only if $I B^\vee \subseteq B$, where
the product is taken in the fractional ideals of $B$ in $L$.

articles.title: The different commutes with localization
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $L/K$ be a finite separable extension, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$
in $L$, a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ that is torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let
$S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors, let $A_S \subseteq K$ be the
localization of $A$ at $S$ inside $K$, and let $B_S$ be a localization of $B$ at the image of
$S$ that is also an $A_S$-algebra, with a map $B_S \to L$ such that all composite maps from
$A$, $A_S$, $B$, $B_S$ and $K$ into $L$ agree. Assume that $B_S$ is a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $L$, torsion-free over $A_S$ and over $B$, and the integral closure of $A_S$ in
$L$. Then the ideal of $B_S$ generated by the image of the different ideal $\mathfrak{D}_{B/A}$
is the different ideal $\mathfrak{D}_{B_S/A_S}$.

## Sources

- ATLAS N241, canonical-localization scope; transport to an arbitrary base localization is deferred.

articles.title: The discriminant commutes with localization
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with
fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be a finite separable extension, and let $B$ be the integral
closure of $A$ in $L$, a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ that is finite and
torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors,
let $A_S \subseteq K$ be the localization of $A$ at $S$ inside $K$, and let $B_S$ be a
localization of $B$ at the image of $S$ that is also an $A$-algebra and an $A_S$-algebra, with
a map $B_S \to L$, such that all composite maps among $A$, $A_S$, $B$, $B_S$, $K$ and $L$
agree. Assume that $B_S$ is a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, finite and torsion-free
over $A_S$, torsion-free over $B$, and the integral closure of $A_S$ in $L$. Write
$\mathfrak{d}_{B/A}$ and $\mathfrak{d}_{B_S/A_S}$ for the discriminant ideals of $B$ over $A$
and of $B_S$ over $A_S$. Then the ideal of $A_S$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak{d}_{B/A}$ is $\mathfrak{d}_{B_S/A_S}$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Proposition 12.15, canonical-localization scope; transport to an arbitrary base localization is deferred.

articles.title: The norm of the different commutes with localization
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain
with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be a finite separable extension, and let $B$ be the
integral closure of $A$ in $L$, a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$ that is finite and
torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors,
let $A_S \subseteq K$ be the localization of $A$ at $S$ inside $K$, and let $B_S$ be a
localization of $B$ at the image of $S$ that is also an $A$-algebra and an $A_S$-algebra, with
a map $B_S \to L$, such that all composite maps among $A$, $A_S$, $B$, $B_S$, $K$ and $L$
agree. Assume that $B_S$ is a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, finite and torsion-free
over $A_S$, torsion-free over $B$, and the integral closure of $A_S$ in $L$. For an extension
$R \to T$ of Dedekind domains, write $\mathfrak{D}_{T/R}$ for its different ideal and, for an
ideal $I$ of $T$, write $N_{T/R}(I)$ for the ideal of $R$ generated by the norms of the
elements of $I$. Then the ideal of $A_S$ generated by the image of
$N_{B/A}(\mathfrak{D}_{B/A})$ is $N_{B_S/A_S}(\mathfrak{D}_{B_S/A_S})$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI Proposition 12.15 (norm-of-the-different form), canonical-localization scope; transport to an arbitrary base localization is deferred.

articles.title: Unramified at a height-one prime implies not dividing discriminant
articles.statement:
Height-one compatibility: derive nondivisibility from the standard
unramified-in criterion after converting the original height-one premise.

articles.title: A valuation centered at a height-one prime is equivalent to its adic valuation
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be
a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, let $\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$, and let
$w$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined.
Suppose that $w(b) \le 1$ for every $b \in B$, and that for every $b \in B$ we have
$b \in \mathfrak{q}$ if and only if $w(b) < 1$. Then the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ is
equivalent to $w$.

articles.title: Each extension of a prime-adic valuation comes from exactly one prime above
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a finite separable extension of $K$, and let
$B$ be a Dedekind domain that is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ and has fraction field $L$.
Let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and consider valuations on $L$ with values in the
multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined. Then (1) if $\mathfrak{q}_1$ and
$\mathfrak{q}_2$ are height-one primes of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ whose adic valuations on
$L$ are equivalent, then $\mathfrak{q}_1 = \mathfrak{q}_2$; and (2) every such valuation $w$ on $L$
whose restriction to $K$ is equivalent to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$ is equivalent
to the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ for some height-one prime $\mathfrak{q}$ of $B$ lying
over $\mathfrak{p}$.

Valuations are compared only up to equivalence; no normalization or ramification index is
asserted.

articles.title: Valuations extending a prime-adic valuation
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction
field $K$, let $L$ be a field extension of $K$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$.
A valuation $w$ on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined
extends the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$ when its restriction to $K$ is equivalent to the
$\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$.

This relation does not record an extension index or a normalization.

articles.title: Membership in a prime is detected by a prime lying over it
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind
domains with $B$ an $A$-algebra, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let
$\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$. Then for every $a \in A$,
$a \in \mathfrak{p}$ if and only if the image of $a$ in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak{q}$.

articles.title: Height-one primes above a prime
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains with $B$ an
$A$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$. The primes above $\mathfrak{p}$
form the set of height-one primes $\mathfrak{q}$ of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, that is, whose
preimage in $A$ is $\mathfrak{p}$.

articles.title: The adic valuation of a prime lying over extends the adic valuation below
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a finite separable extension of $K$, and let
$B$ be a Dedekind domain that is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ and has fraction field $L$.
If $\mathfrak{q}$ is a height-one prime of $B$ lying over a height-one prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of
$A$, then the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ extends the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of
$K$: its restriction to $K$ is equivalent to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$.

articles.title: Each extension of a prime-adic valuation comes from some prime above
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a finite separable extension of $K$, and let
$B$ be a Dedekind domain that is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ and has fraction field $L$.
Let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $w$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in
the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined whose restriction to $K$ is equivalent
to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$. Then there is a height-one prime $\mathfrak{q}$ of $B$
lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ such that the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ is equivalent
to $w$.

articles.title: In an abelian group the Frobenius element depends only on the prime below
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be
a commutative algebra over a commutative ring $R$, and let a finite commutative group $G$ act on
$S$ by $R$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of $S$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an
element of $R$. For a prime $Q$ of $S$ with $S/Q$ finite, let $\mathrm{Frob}_Q \in G$ be the
chosen arithmetic Frobenius element at $Q$: an element $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod Q$ for all $x \in S$, where $q$ is the number of elements of $R$
modulo the preimage of $Q$ in $R$, chosen so that the elements chosen at primes with the same
preimage in $R$ are conjugate. If $Q$ and $Q'$ are primes of $S$ with $S/Q$ and $S/Q'$ finite
that have the same preimage in $R$, then $\mathrm{Frob}_Q = \mathrm{Frob}_{Q'}$.

articles.title: Restriction of a Frobenius element along a compatible pair
articles.statement:
A Frobenius congruence restricts along a compatible pair: if
`ι : C →ₐ[R] B` and `ρ : G →* H` satisfy `ι (ρ g • c) = g • ι c`, and `σ`
is a Frobenius at `Q`, then `ρ σ` is a Frobenius at `Q.comap ι`.

articles.title: Restriction of Frobenius equals Frobenius with trivial inertia
articles.statement:
If `σ` is a Frobenius at `Q` and `τ` satisfies the Frobenius congruence
at `Q.comap ι`, then `ρ σ = τ` when the inertia subgroup of `Q.comap ι` is
trivial. This is the equality form of the restriction statement of
Proposition 7.22 under its unramified hypothesis.

articles.title: Elements with the same powered congruence differ by inertia
articles.statement:
Two elements satisfying the same powered congruence differ by an
element of the inertia subgroup of `Q`.

articles.title: Intermediate residue cardinality as a power of the base residue cardinality
articles.statement:
In a finite ring tower `R → T → B`, the intermediate prime residue quotient
has cardinality equal to the base residue cardinality raised to its canonical
inertia degree. The cardinality theorem is Mathlib's `cardQuot_pow_inertiaDeg`.

articles.title: Powers of a Frobenius map satisfy the powered congruence
articles.statement:
Powers of an arithmetic Frobenius map satisfy the powered congruence:
if `φ x - x ^ q ∈ Q` for all `x`, then `(φ ^ f) x - x ^ q ^ f ∈ Q`.

articles.title: Uniqueness of Frobenius powers with trivial inertia
articles.statement:
If `σ` is a Frobenius at `Q` and `τ` satisfies the powered congruence
with exponent `q ^ f`, then `σ ^ f = τ` when the inertia subgroup of `Q` is
trivial. This is a uniqueness helper for an already supplied powered
congruence. The actual tower theorem below derives that congruence from the
Frobenius premise over the intermediate ring and its residue cardinality.

articles.title: Powers of a Frobenius element satisfy the powered congruence
articles.statement:
Powers of an arithmetic Frobenius element satisfy the powered
congruence: if `σ • x - x ^ q ∈ Q` for all `x`, with
`q = Nat.card (R ⧸ Q.under R)`, then
`(σ ^ f) • x - x ^ q ^ f ∈ Q`.

articles.title: Frobenius tower equality for algebra automorphisms
articles.statement:
For algebra automorphisms in a finite ring tower, the inclusion of the
intermediate Frobenius is the canonical `AlgEquiv.restrictScalars`.

articles.title: Frobenius tower equality for an intermediate field
articles.statement:
The tower equality for the source's intermediate field `E ⊂ L`.
Here `K` is the fraction field of the base ring `R`, `T` is the integral
closure of `R` in `E`, and `B` is its integral closure in `L`. In the
number-field application these are the three rings of integers. The
intermediate action is `E.fixingSubgroup`; the whole `Gal(L/K)` need not fix `T`.

articles.title: Frobenius in a tower is a power of the base Frobenius
articles.statement:
In a finite ring tower `R → T → B`, the Frobenius over `T`, embedded into
an action over `R`, equals the Frobenius over `R` raised to the intermediate
residue degree when the inertia subgroup is trivial. Only `H` must fix `T`.

articles.title: The Frobenius conjugacy class depends only on the prime below
articles.statement:
Let a finite group $G$
act on a commutative algebra $S$ over a commutative ring $R$ by $R$-algebra automorphisms such
that every element of $S$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an element of $R$. Let $Q$ and $Q'$ be
primes of $S$ with $S/Q$ and $S/Q'$ finite at which $S$ is unramified over $R$. If $Q$ and $Q'$
have the same preimage in $R$, then the Frobenius conjugacy classes at $Q$ and $Q'$ are
equal.

articles.title: The Frobenius element lies in the Frobenius conjugacy class
articles.statement:
Let a finite group $G$ act
on a commutative algebra $S$ over a commutative ring $R$ by $R$-algebra automorphisms such that
every element of $S$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an element of $R$. For every prime $Q$ of $S$
with $S/Q$ finite at which $S$ is unramified over $R$, the chosen arithmetic Frobenius element
$\mathrm{Frob}_Q$ at $Q$ belongs to the Frobenius conjugacy class at $Q$.

articles.title: Frobenius conjugacy class
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative algebra over a commutative ring $R$,
and let a finite group $G$ act on $S$ by $R$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of
$S$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an element of $R$. Let $Q$ be a prime of $S$ with $S/Q$ finite
at which $S$ is unramified over $R$ (the localization $S_Q$ is formally unramified over $R$).
The Frobenius conjugacy class at $Q$ is the conjugacy class in $G$ of the chosen arithmetic
Frobenius element $\mathrm{Frob}_Q$ at $Q$: an element $\sigma \in G$ with
$\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod Q$ for all $x \in S$, where $q$ is the number of elements of $R$
modulo the preimage of $Q$ in $R$, chosen so that the elements chosen at primes with the same
preimage in $R$ are conjugate.

articles.title: The Frobenius element is trivial iff the prime splits completely
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
integral domains with $B$ a finite flat $A$-algebra, and let $G$ be a finite group acting
faithfully on $B$ by $A$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of $B$ fixed by $G$ is
the image of an element of $A$. Let $p$ be a prime of $A$ and $P$ a prime of $B$ lying over $p$,
with $B/P$ finite and $B$ unramified over $A$ at $P$ (the localization $B_P$ is formally
unramified over $A$). Let $\mathrm{Frob}_P \in G$ be the chosen arithmetic Frobenius element at
$P$, an element $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod P$ for all $x \in B$, where $q$
is the number of elements of $A/p$. Then $\mathrm{Frob}_P = 1$ if and only if the number of
primes of $B$ lying over $p$ equals the order of $G$.

articles.title: Trivial Frobenius and the number of primes above, assuming the Frobenius generates
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative algebra over a commutative ring $A$, and let a finite group $G$ act on
$B$ by $A$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of $B$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an
element of $A$. Let $p$ be an ideal of $A$ and $P$ a prime of $B$ lying over $p$ with $B/P$
finite, and let $\mathrm{Frob}_P \in G$ be the chosen arithmetic Frobenius element at $P$, an
element $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod P$ for all $x \in B$, where $q$ is the
number of elements of $A/p$. Suppose every element of the stabilizer of $P$ in $G$ equals
$\mathrm{Frob}_P^n$ for some natural number $n$. Then $\mathrm{Frob}_P = 1$ if and only if the
number of primes of $B$ lying over $p$ equals the order of $G$.

articles.title: The Frobenius element generates the decomposition group at an unramified prime
articles.statement:
Let $A$
and $B$ be integral domains with $B$ a finite flat $A$-algebra, and let $G$ be a finite group
acting faithfully on $B$ by $A$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of $B$ fixed by
$G$ is the image of an element of $A$. Let $p$ be a prime of $A$ and $P$ a prime of $B$ lying
over $p$, with $B/P$ finite and $B$ unramified over $A$ at $P$ (the localization $B_P$ is
formally unramified over $A$). Let $\mathrm{Frob}_P \in G$ be the chosen arithmetic Frobenius
element at $P$, an element $\sigma \in G$ with $\sigma(x) \equiv x^q \pmod P$ for all
$x \in B$, where $q$ is the number of elements of $A/p$. Then every element of the stabilizer of
$P$ in $G$ (the decomposition group of $P$) equals $\mathrm{Frob}_P^n$ for some natural
number $n$.

articles.title: Trivial decomposition group and the number of primes above
articles.statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative
algebra over a commutative ring $A$, and let a finite group $G$ act on $B$ by $A$-algebra
automorphisms such that every element of $B$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an element of $A$. Let
$p$ be an ideal of $A$ and $P$ a prime of $B$ lying over $p$. Then the stabilizer of $P$ in $G$
(the decomposition group of $P$) is trivial if and only if the number of primes of $B$ lying
over $p$ equals the order of $G$.

articles.title: Frobenius elements coincide when inertia is trivial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings
with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let a group $G$ act on $S$ by $R$-algebra automorphisms, and let $Q$ be
an ideal of $S$. Write $P$ for the preimage of $Q$ in $R$ and $q$ for the number of elements of
$R/P$ (with $q = 0$ when $R/P$ is infinite). Call $\sigma \in G$ an arithmetic Frobenius element at
$Q$ if $\sigma x - x^q \in Q$ for all $x \in S$, and call the inertia subgroup of $Q$ the set of
$\tau \in G$ with $\tau x - x \in Q$ for all $x \in S$. If $\sigma, \sigma' \in G$ are arithmetic
Frobenius elements at $Q$ and the inertia subgroup of $Q$ is trivial, then $\sigma = \sigma'$.

articles.title: Existence and uniqueness of the Frobenius element under trivial inertia
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$
be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let a finite group $G$ act on $S$ by
$R$-algebra automorphisms such that every element of $S$ fixed by $G$ is the image of an element
of $R$. Let $Q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ with $S/Q$ finite, write $P$ for the preimage of $Q$ in
$R$ and $q$ for the number of elements of $R/P$. Call $\sigma \in G$ an arithmetic Frobenius
element at $Q$ if $\sigma x - x^q \in Q$ for all $x \in S$. If the inertia subgroup of $Q$, the set
of $\tau \in G$ with $\tau x - x \in Q$ for all $x \in S$, is trivial, then there is exactly one
arithmetic Frobenius element at $Q$ in $G$.

articles.title: Restricting a Frobenius element to an intermediate field
articles.statement:
Let $K \subseteq L \subseteq M$
be a tower of number fields with $L/K$ and $M/K$ Galois, and let $\mathcal{O}_K$,
$\mathcal{O}_L$ and $\mathcal{O}_M$ be their rings of integers. Let $Q_L$ be a prime of
$\mathcal{O}_L$ at which $\mathcal{O}_L$ is unramified over $\mathcal{O}_K$, let $Q_M$ be a
prime of $\mathcal{O}_M$ lying over $Q_L$ with $\mathcal{O}_M/Q_M$ finite, and let $q$ be the
number of elements of $\mathcal{O}_K/\mathfrak{p}$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is the prime of
$\mathcal{O}_K$ below $Q_M$ (equivalently, below $Q_L$). If $\sigma_M \in \mathrm{Gal}(M/K)$
satisfies $\sigma_M(x) \equiv x^q \pmod{Q_M}$ for all $x \in \mathcal{O}_M$ and
$\sigma_L \in \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ satisfies $\sigma_L(y) \equiv y^q \pmod{Q_L}$ for all
$y \in \mathcal{O}_L$, then the restriction of $\sigma_M$ to $L$ equals $\sigma_L$.

## Sources

- ATLAS Proposition 7.13, generalized from the chosen Frobenius elements at chosen primes to arbitrary Frobenius elements at explicit primes.

articles.title: Lifts of residue generators generate unramified extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields
$\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an
$A$-module and whose structure map is a local homomorphism. Suppose $\kappa_B / \kappa_A$ is
separable and the ideal $\mathfrak m_A B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$ equals
$\mathfrak m_B$. If $\beta \in B$ has residue $\bar\beta \in \kappa_B$ with
$\kappa_A[\bar\beta] = \kappa_B$, then $A[\beta] = B$.

articles.title: Étale finite local algebras are generated by one element with separable reduction
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be local rings and let $S$ be an $R$-algebra whose structure map $R \to S$ is
injective, which is finitely generated and flat as an $R$-module and finitely presented as an
$R$-algebra. Let $k$ be the residue field of $R$. Then $S$ is étale over $R$ if and only if
there is an element $x \in S$ with $R[x] = S$ such that the image in $k[X]$ of the minimal
polynomial of $x$ over $R$ (a monic polynomial in $R[X]$ of least degree with root $x$) is
separable.

articles.title: Étale criterion for extensions of discrete valuation rings
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with residue fields $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that
is finitely generated as an $A$-module and whose structure map is a local homomorphism. If
$\kappa_B / \kappa_A$ is separable and the rank of $B$ as an $A$-module equals the degree
$[\kappa_B : \kappa_A]$, then $B$ is étale over $A$.

articles.title: Monogenicity of extensions with separable residue field extension
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with residue fields $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $A$-module and whose structure map is a local
homomorphism. If $\kappa_B / \kappa_A$ is separable, then there is $\alpha \in B$ with
$A[\alpha] = B$.

No unramifiedness is assumed: in the ramified case a lift of a generator of $\kappa_B$ over
$\kappa_A$ is perturbed so that the lifted minimal polynomial takes a uniformizer as value.

articles.title: Monogenic generator with a uniformizing residue polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields
$\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an
$A$-module and whose structure map is a local homomorphism. If $\kappa_B / \kappa_A$ is
separable, then there are $\alpha \in B$ and a polynomial $F \in A[X]$ such that, writing
$\bar\alpha$ for the residue of $\alpha$ in $\kappa_B$: $A[\alpha] = B$;
$\kappa_A[\bar\alpha] = \kappa_B$; $F$ is monic; the reduction of $F$ modulo $\mathfrak m_A$ is
the minimal polynomial of $\bar\alpha$ over $\kappa_A$; $F'(\alpha)$ is a unit of $B$; and
$\mathfrak m_B$ is the principal ideal generated by $F(\alpha)$.

In general $F$ is not the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $A$: $F(\alpha)$ is a nonzero
uniformizer, whereas the minimal polynomial vanishes at $\alpha$.

articles.title: Algebras generated by a root with invertible derivative are formally unramified
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings, let $S$ be an $R$-algebra, and let $x \in S$ generate $S$
as an $R$-algebra, that is $R[x] = S$. If some polynomial $P \in R[X]$ satisfies $P(x) = 0$ and
$P'(x)$ is a unit of $S$, then $S$ is formally unramified over $R$.

articles.title: Characterization of unramified extensions of a complete DVR
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings, with $A$ complete with respect to its maximal ideal, and let $B$
be an $A$-algebra via a local homomorphism $A \to B$, such that $B$ is finitely generated
and torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let $k_A$ and $k_B$ be the residue fields of $A$ and $B$.
Then the following are equivalent: (a) $k_B$ is separable over $k_A$ and the rank of $B$
as an $A$-module equals $[k_B : k_A]$; (b) there is $\alpha \in B$ with $B = A[\alpha]$ such
that the reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $A$ of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$
over $A$ is separable over $k_A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 10.15.

articles.title: Adjoining a root of unity of order coprime to the residue characteristic is unramified
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings, with $A$ complete with respect to its maximal
ideal, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra via a local homomorphism $A \to B$, such that $B$ is
finitely generated and torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let $k_A$ and $k_B$ be the residue fields
of $A$ and $B$. Let $n$ be a natural number coprime to the characteristic of $k_A$, and let
$\zeta \in B$ be a primitive $n$-th root of unity with $B = A[\zeta]$. Then $k_B$ is separable
over $k_A$ and the rank of $B$ as an $A$-module equals $[k_B : k_A]$.

Coprimality is meant literally, with $\gcd(n, 0) = n$, so when $k_A$ has characteristic $0$
the hypothesis forces $n = 1$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, the helper `cor_10_16_of_adjoin` for Corollary 10.16; the generation $B = A[\zeta]$ is assumed here rather than proved from the integral-closure setup.

articles.title: Additive valuations scale by the ramification index
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is torsion-free as an $A$-module and whose
structure map $\varphi \colon A \to B$ is a local homomorphism. Let $v_A$ and $v_B$ be the
normalized additive valuations of $A$ and $B$, with values in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, and
let $e$ be the ramification index of the maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$. Then
$v_B(\varphi(x)) = e \cdot v_A(x)$ for every $x \in A$.

articles.title: Images of the base maximal ideal lie in the ramification power
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$, and let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra that is torsion-free as an $A$-module and whose structure map is a local
homomorphism. Let $e$ be the ramification index of $\mathfrak m_B$ over $A$. Then for every
$x \in \mathfrak m_A$, the image of $x$ in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak m_B^e$.

articles.title: Multiplicity of the maximal ideal equals the additive valuation
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete
valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and normalized additive valuation
$v \colon R \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every $x \in R$, the multiplicity of
$\mathfrak{m}$ in the principal ideal $(x)$, that is, the supremum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$
of the $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\mathfrak{m}^n$ divides $(x)$ as ideals, equals $v(x)$.

articles.title: Bounds on the inertia degree
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be Dedekind domains, with $S$ an $R$-algebra
that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $R$-module, and let $n$ be the rank of $S$ as an
$R$-module. If $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal of $R$ and $\mathfrak{q}$ is a prime ideal of $S$
lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, then the inertia degree $f_{\mathfrak{q}}$ of $\mathfrak{q}$ over
$\mathfrak{p}$ satisfies $1 \le f_{\mathfrak{q}} \le n$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 5.36 (the $f_{\mathfrak{q}}$ part).

articles.title: Natural numbers that are units in a local ring
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative local ring and
let $p$ be the characteristic of its residue field. For every natural number $n$, the image of
$n$ in $R$ is a unit if and only if $p$ does not divide $n$.

articles.title: The extended maximal ideal is a power of the maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$, and let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra that is torsion-free as an $A$-module and whose structure map is a local
homomorphism. Let $e$ be the ramification index of $\mathfrak m_B$ over $A$. Then the ideal
$\mathfrak m_A B$ of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$ equals $\mathfrak m_B^e$.

articles.title: Bounds on the number of primes above a prime
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be Dedekind domains, with $S$
an $R$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $R$-module, and let $n$ be the
rank of $S$ as an $R$-module. If $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal of $R$, then the number
$g_{\mathfrak{p}}$ of prime ideals of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ satisfies
$1 \le g_{\mathfrak{p}} \le n$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 5.36 (the $g_{\mathfrak{p}}$ part).

articles.title: Bounds on the ramification index
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be Dedekind domains, with $S$ an
$R$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $R$-module, and let $n$ be the rank
of $S$ as an $R$-module. If $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal of $R$ and $\mathfrak{q}$ is a prime
ideal of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, then the ramification index $e_{\mathfrak{q}}$ of
$\mathfrak{q}$ over $\mathfrak{p}$ satisfies $1 \le e_{\mathfrak{q}} \le n$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 5.36 (the $e_{\mathfrak{q}}$ part).

articles.title: Bounds on ramification, inertia and splitting, fraction-field form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be
Dedekind domains, with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an
$R$-module. Let $K$ be the fraction field of $R$ and $L$ the fraction field of $S$, with $L$ a
$K$-algebra compatible with the maps $R \to K \to L$ and $R \to S \to L$, and let $n = [L : K]$.
If $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal of $R$ and $\mathfrak{q}$ is a prime ideal of $S$ lying over
$\mathfrak{p}$, then the ramification index $e_{\mathfrak{q}}$ and the inertia degree
$f_{\mathfrak{q}}$ of $\mathfrak{q}$ over $\mathfrak{p}$ and the number $g_{\mathfrak{p}}$ of prime
ideals of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ all lie in the interval $[1, n]$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 5.36.

articles.title: Bounds on ramification, inertia and splitting
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be Dedekind domains, with
$S$ an $R$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $R$-module, and let $n$ be the
rank of $S$ as an $R$-module. If $\mathfrak{p}$ is a maximal ideal of $R$ and $\mathfrak{q}$ is a
prime ideal of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, then the ramification index $e_{\mathfrak{q}}$ and
the inertia degree $f_{\mathfrak{q}}$ of $\mathfrak{q}$ over $\mathfrak{p}$ and the number
$g_{\mathfrak{p}}$ of prime ideals of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$ all lie in the interval
$[1, n]$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 5.36.

articles.title: Relative norm is the base prime to the inertia degree, separable case
articles.statement:
Theorem 6.10 of ATLAS `NumberTheoryI`, in the separable (rather than Galois
or perfect-field) form: the relative norm of a maximal ideal lying over a maximal
ideal is the base prime raised to the inertia degree.

articles.title: Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$ and no nontrivial $p$-th roots of unity, cyclotomic extensions of order divisible by $p$ ramify
articles.statement:
**Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$ and no nontrivial $p$-th roots of unity,
cyclotomic extensions of order divisible by $p$ ramify.** Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring,
complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, with fraction field $K$ and finite
residue field of characteristic a prime $p$, and suppose $\mathfrak m_A = (p)$. Suppose $1$ is the
only $p$-th root of unity in $K$. Let $m > 0$ be divisible by $p$, let $L$ be an $m$-th cyclotomic
extension of $K$ that is finite over $K$, and let $B$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction
field $L$ and an $A$-algebra structure such that the maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$
agree. Then the ramification index of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ of $B$ over
$\mathfrak m_A$ (the largest $n$ with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$) is not $1$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Section 10.2, Corollary 10.18, a special case of the ramified implication: the source does not assume $\mathfrak m_A = (p)$, and the converse is not proved.

articles.title: Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$ and no primitive $p$-th root of unity, an index-one extension has no nontrivial $p$-th roots of unity
articles.statement:
**Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$ and no primitive $p$-th root of unity, an
index-one extension has no nontrivial $p$-th roots of unity.** Let $A$ be a discrete valuation
ring, complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, with fraction field $K$ and
finite residue field of characteristic a prime $p$, and suppose $\mathfrak m_A = (p)$. Let $L$ be a
finite extension of $K$, and let $B$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and an
$A$-algebra structure such that the maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$ agree. Suppose the
ramification index of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_A$ (the largest
$n$ with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$) is $1$. If $K$ contains no primitive $p$-th
root of unity, then every $\eta \in L$ with $\eta^p = 1$ equals $1$.

articles.title: No primitive p-th root in an unramified DVR extension
articles.statement:
For a complete DVR base whose maximal ideal is generated by `p`, a
primitive `p`-th root cannot appear in an index-one DVR extension: if the residue characteristic is `p`,
`(p)` is the maximal ideal, the ramification index is `1`, and the base field
has no primitive `p`-th root, then neither does the extension.

The proof is the valuation argument: a primitive root `b ∈ B` reduces to `1`
in the residue field (characteristic `p`), so each factor `1 - b ^ (k + 1)`
lies in the maximal ideal, while their product is exactly `p`; hence
`p ∈ 𝔪_B ^ (p - 1)`, which forces `p ∈ 𝔪_B ^ 2`, contradicting
ramification index `1` (for `p = 2` the argument is replaced by the
observation that `-1` would be a primitive square root in the base field).

articles.title: Without primitive $p$-th roots of unity, every $p$-th root of unity is trivial
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime and let $L$ be a field containing no primitive $p$-th root of unity. Then every $\eta \in L$
with $\eta^p = 1$ equals $1$.

The order of $\eta$ divides the prime $p$, so it is $1$ or $p$, and $p$ is excluded.

articles.title: Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$, the $p$-th roots of unity in an index-one extension come from the base
articles.statement:
**Over a complete base with maximal ideal $(p)$, the $p$-th roots of unity in an index-one
extension come from the base.** Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring, complete with respect to its
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, with fraction field $K$ and finite residue field of characteristic a
prime $p$, and suppose $\mathfrak m_A = (p)$. Let $L$ be a finite extension of $K$, and let $B$ be
a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and an $A$-algebra structure such that the maps
$A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$ agree. Suppose the ramification index of the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m_B$ of $B$ over $\mathfrak m_A$ (the largest $n$ with
$\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$) is $1$. Then every $\eta \in L$ with $\eta^p = 1$ is
the image of an element of $K$.

articles.title: Residue separability, unfolded
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is
residue separable over $R$ if and only if the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the
residue field $\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism
$R_p \to S_q$ of localizations.

articles.title: Unramified primes are residue separable
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is
unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is
residue separable over $R$.

articles.title: Residue separability at a prime
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is
residue separable over $R$ when the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the residue field
$\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism $R_p \to S_q$
of localizations.

articles.title: Tame primes are residue separable
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then $q$ is
residue separable over $R$.

articles.title: Tameness in residue characteristic zero
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra that is finite as an $R$-module, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ whose residue
field $\kappa(q)$ has characteristic $0$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$
is residue separable over $R$.

articles.title: Characterization of tame ramification
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only
if $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does
not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

articles.title: Criterion for tame ramification
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the
characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over
$R$, then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$.

articles.title: Unramified primes are tamely ramified
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an
$R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is
unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is
tamely ramified over $R$.

articles.title: Tamely ramified prime
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and
let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *tamely ramified* over $R$ when $q$ is residue
separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the
ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

articles.title: Wild ramification under residue separability
articles.statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$
an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ that is residue separable over $R$. Then $q$ is
wildly ramified over $R$ if and only if the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ divides
the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

articles.title: Wild ramification is the failure of tame ramification
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring,
$S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$
if and only if $q$ is not tamely ramified over $R$.

articles.title: Divisibility of the ramification index forces wild ramification
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue field
$\kappa(q)$. If the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ divides the ramification index of $q$ over $R$,
then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.

No separability hypothesis on the residue field extension is needed.

articles.title: An inseparable residue field extension forces wild ramification
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a
commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra, $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ and $p$ the preimage
of $q$ in $R$. If the residue field extension $\kappa(p) \to \kappa(q)$ is not separable, then
$q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.

articles.title: Wildly ramified prime
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and
$q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *wildly ramified* over $R$ if it is not tamely ramified
over $R$.

articles.title: The residue characteristic of a tame prime does not divide its ramification index
articles.statement:
Let
$R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue
field $\kappa(q)$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ does
not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

articles.title: Different ideal of a tamely ramified extension of DVRs
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak{m}_A$ and $\mathfrak{m}_B$, and let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra that is finite and torsion-free as an $A$-module, such that the extension of
fraction fields and the extension of residue fields are both separable. Let $e$ be a natural
number whose image in $B$ is a unit, and suppose that the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak{m}_A$ equals $\mathfrak{m}_B^e$. Then the different ideal of $B$ over $A$ equals
$\mathfrak{m}_B^{e-1}$.

Without the tameness hypothesis that $e$ is a unit in $B$, this equality fails in general.

articles.title: Surjectivity of the transition maps between maximal-ideal-power quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and
$B$ be discrete valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$
be an $A$-algebra, write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak m_A$, and for each $m$ let $Q_m = B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$. For every
natural number $n$, the transition homomorphism $Q_{n+1} \to Q_n$ that sends the class of each
$b \in B$ to its class in $Q_n$ is surjective.

articles.title: The transition map on residue classes
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings with
maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, write
$\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$, and for each $m$
let $Q_m = B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$. For every natural number $n$ and every
$b \in B$, the transition homomorphism $Q_{n+1} \to Q_n$ maps the class of $b$ in $Q_{n+1}$ to
the class of $b$ in $Q_n$.

articles.title: Transition map between maximal-ideal-power quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete
valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ and let
$\kappa_A = A/\mathfrak m_A$ be the residue field of $A$. Let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, write
$\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$, and for each $m$
let $Q_m = B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$, a $\kappa_A$-algebra in which the class of
$r \in A$ acts as multiplication by the class of its image in $B$. For a natural number $n$,
this is the $\kappa_A$-algebra homomorphism $Q_{n+1} \to Q_n$ sending the class of each
$b \in B$ to its class in $Q_n$; it is well defined because
$\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^{n+1} \subseteq \mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n$.

articles.title: Graded pieces of a DVR are one-dimensional
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$. For every
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, the graded piece $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ is a vector space of
dimension one over $\kappa$.

articles.title: Tame extensions have surjective integral trace
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation
rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields $\kappa_A$,
$\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an
$A$-module, with $\kappa_B / \kappa_A$ separable. Let $e$ be a natural number that is a unit
in $B$ and such that the ideal $\mathfrak m_A B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$
equals $\mathfrak m_B^e$. Then the integral trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{B/A} \colon B \to A$
(the trace of the extension of fraction fields, restricted to $B$) is surjective.

Since $A \to B$ is local, $e$ is a unit in $B$ if and only if it is a unit in $A$.

articles.title: Graded pieces of the maximal-ideal filtration
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th graded piece is the $R$-module
$\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$, realized as the quotient of the ideal $\mathfrak{m}^i$,
viewed as an $R$-module, by its submodule $\mathfrak{m} \cdot \mathfrak{m}^i$.

articles.title: Collapse of the quotient-defining ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings with
maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, and write
$\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$. For every
natural number $n$, if $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$, then
$\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n = \mathfrak m_B^n$.

articles.title: The quotient-defining ideals decrease
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings with
maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, and write
$\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$. For every
natural number $n$, the ideal $\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ is contained in
$\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n$.

articles.title: The residue-field isomorphism intertwines multiplication
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation
ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$, let
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $e : \kappa \to \mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ be the
$\kappa$-linear isomorphism of the residue field with the graded piece. Let $K$ be a field, with
a $K$-algebra structure on $\kappa$ and a $K$-module structure on
$\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ such that $(c b) x = c (b x)$ for all $c \in K$,
$b \in \kappa$ and $x \in \mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$. Then for every $a \in \kappa$,
writing $\mu_a : \kappa \to \kappa$ for multiplication by $a$, the $K$-linear map
$e \circ \mu_a \circ e^{-1}$ equals multiplication by $a$ on $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$,
viewed as a $K$-linear map.

articles.title: Graded pieces as kernels of the transition maps
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation
rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields
$\kappa_A = A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\kappa_B = B/\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra whose
algebra map $A \to B$ is a local homomorphism, so that it induces a field homomorphism
$\kappa_A \to \kappa_B$, and write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image
of $\mathfrak m_A$. For each $m$ let $Q_m = B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$, a
$\kappa_A$-algebra in which the class of $r \in A$ acts as multiplication by the class of its
image in $B$. Let $n$ be a natural number with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$,
and suppose the $\kappa_B$-vector space $\mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ carries a
$\kappa_A$-module structure such that $(\bar a c) \cdot x = a \cdot (c \cdot x)$ for all
$a \in \kappa_A$, $c \in \kappa_B$ and $x \in \mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$, where $\bar a$
is the image of $a$ in $\kappa_B$. This is the $\kappa_A$-linear isomorphism from
$\mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ onto the kernel of the $\kappa_A$-algebra homomorphism
$Q_{n+1} \to Q_n$ that sends the class of each $b \in B$ to its class in $Q_n$; it sends the
class of each $z \in \mathfrak m_B^n$ to the class of $z$ in $Q_{n+1}$.

articles.title: The kernel identification on representatives
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation
rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields
$\kappa_A = A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\kappa_B = B/\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra whose
algebra map $A \to B$ is a local homomorphism, so that it induces a field homomorphism
$\kappa_A \to \kappa_B$, and write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image
of $\mathfrak m_A$. For each $m$ let $Q_m = B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$, a
$\kappa_A$-algebra in which the class of $r \in A$ acts as multiplication by the class of its
image in $B$. Let $n$ be a natural number with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$,
and suppose the $\kappa_B$-vector space $\mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ carries a
$\kappa_A$-module structure such that $(\bar a c) \cdot x = a \cdot (c \cdot x)$ for all
$a \in \kappa_A$, $c \in \kappa_B$ and $x \in \mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$, where $\bar a$
is the image of $a$ in $\kappa_B$. Let $\pi \colon Q_{n+1} \to Q_n$ be the $\kappa_A$-algebra
homomorphism sending the class of each $b \in B$ to its class in $Q_n$. Then for every
$z \in \mathfrak m_B^n$, the $\kappa_A$-linear isomorphism from
$\mathfrak m_B^n/\mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ onto $\ker \pi$ sends the class of $z$ to the class of $z$ in
$Q_{n+1}$.

articles.title: Graded pieces of a DVR as copies of the residue field
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation
ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$, and let
$\varpi$ be a generator of $\mathfrak{m}$ chosen once and for all. For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the
map $\kappa \to \mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ sending the class of $r \in R$ to the class
of $r \varpi^i$ is a $\kappa$-linear isomorphism.

Here $\kappa$ acts on $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ through $R$, which is well defined
because $\mathfrak{m}$ annihilates the graded piece.

articles.title: Ring isomorphism with the quotient by a power of the maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra, and write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak m_A$. For a natural number $n$ with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$, this
is the ring isomorphism $B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n) \cong B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ sending
the class of each $b \in B$ to the class of $b$; it exists because the two ideals are equal.

articles.title: The power-quotient isomorphism on residue classes
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation
rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an $A$-algebra, and
write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$. For every
natural number $n$ with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$ and every $b \in B$, the ring
isomorphism $B/(\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n) \cong B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ induced by the
equality of these two ideals sends the class of $b$ to the class of $b$.

articles.title: Quotient by the extended maximal ideal plus a maximal-ideal power
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak m_B$, let $B$ be an
$A$-algebra, and write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak m_A$. For a natural number $n$, this is the quotient ring
$B / (\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n)$.

articles.title: Multiplication by a residue class on representatives
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation
ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$. For $x \in R$,
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $y \in \mathfrak{m}^i$, multiplication by the residue class
$\bar{x} \in \kappa$ on $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ sends the class of $y$ to the class
of $x y$.

articles.title: Multiplication by a residue class on a graded piece
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$. For $a \in \kappa$
and $i \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the $\kappa$-linear endomorphism $x \mapsto a x$ of the graded
piece $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$.

articles.title: Residue of the integral trace
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings with maximal
ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$
be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated and torsion-free as an $A$-module. Let $e$ be a
natural number such that the ideal $\mathfrak m_A B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$
equals $\mathfrak m_B^e$. Then for every $b \in B$, writing $\bar b$ for the residue of $b$ in
$\kappa_B$, the residue in $\kappa_A$ of the integral trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{B/A}(b)$ (the
trace of the extension of fraction fields, restricted to $B$) equals
$e \cdot \operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa_B/\kappa_A}(\bar b)$.

This determines the integral trace only modulo $\mathfrak m_A$.

articles.title: Trace on the maximal-ideal-power quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings
with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields $\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$,
and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra whose structure map is a local homomorphism. Write
$\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$. Let $n$ be a
natural number with $\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^n$, and suppose the $\kappa_A$-algebra
$Q_n = B / (\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^n)$ is finite-dimensional over $\kappa_A$. Then for
every $b \in B$, writing $\bar b$ for the residue of $b$ in $\kappa_B$, the trace over
$\kappa_A$ of multiplication by the class of $b$ on $Q_n$ equals
$n \cdot \operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa_B/\kappa_A}(\bar b)$.

articles.title: One-step trace recurrence for the maximal-ideal-power quotients
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A$, $\mathfrak m_B$ and residue fields
$\kappa_A$, $\kappa_B$, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra whose structure map is a local
homomorphism. Write $\mathfrak m_A B$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of
$\mathfrak m_A$, and for each $m$ let $Q_m = B / (\mathfrak m_A B + \mathfrak m_B^m)$, a
$\kappa_A$-algebra. Let $n$ be a natural number with
$\mathfrak m_A B \subseteq \mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$, suppose $Q_{n+1}$ is finite-dimensional over
$\kappa_A$, and equip the graded piece $\mathfrak m_B^n / \mathfrak m_B^{n+1}$ with a
$\kappa_A$-module structure compatible with its $\kappa_B$-module structure through
$\kappa_A \to \kappa_B$. Then for every $b \in B$, writing $\bar b$ for the residue of $b$ in
$\kappa_B$, the trace over $\kappa_A$ of multiplication by the class of $b$ on $Q_{n+1}$ equals
$\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa_B/\kappa_A}(\bar b)$ plus the trace over $\kappa_A$ of multiplication
by the class of $b$ on $Q_n$.

articles.title: Trace of multiplication on a graded piece
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and residue field $\kappa = R/\mathfrak{m}$, let $i \in \mathbb{N}$,
and let $K$ be a field, with a $K$-algebra structure on $\kappa$ and a $K$-module structure on
$\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ such that $(c b) x = c (b x)$ for all $c \in K$,
$b \in \kappa$ and $x \in \mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$. Then for every $a \in \kappa$, the
trace of multiplication by $a$ on $\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$, as a $K$-linear map,
equals the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa/K}(a)$.

Each trace is taken to be $0$ when the corresponding space is not finite-dimensional over $K$.

articles.title: The constant coefficient lies in the ideal generated by the adjoined root
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
commutative ring, let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in
$A[X]/(f)$. Then the image in $A[X]/(f)$ of the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$ lies in the
principal ideal $(\alpha)$.

articles.title: Totally ramified extensions are generated by an Eisenstein uniformizer
articles.statement:
Let $A \subseteq B$
be an extension of discrete valuation rings with $B$ finite over $A$ and the inclusion a local
homomorphism, and let $K \subseteq L$ be their fraction fields, with $L$ finite over $K$ and the
maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$ agreeing. If the ramification index of the maximal ideal of
$B$ over $A$ equals $[L : K]$, then every uniformizer $\pi$ of $B$ satisfies $B = A[\pi]$, and the
minimal polynomial of $\pi$ over $A$ is Eisenstein at the maximal ideal of $A$.

articles.title: The adjoined root of an Eisenstein polynomial over a DVR is irreducible
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial
of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image
of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha$ is an irreducible element of $A[X]/(f)$.

articles.title: Adjoining a root of an Eisenstein polynomial to a DVR gives a DVR
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of
positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $A[X]/(f)$ is a discrete
valuation ring.

articles.title: The maximal ideal of an Eisenstein extension of a DVR is generated by the root
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be
a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial
of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image
of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. If $A[X]/(f)$ is a local ring, then its maximal ideal is the principal ideal
$(\alpha)$.

articles.title: An Eisenstein extension of a DVR is local
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree that is
Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $A[X]/(f)$ is a local ring.

articles.title: The adjoined root of an Eisenstein polynomial generates a maximal ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial
of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image
of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the principal ideal $(\alpha)$ of $A[X]/(f)$ is a maximal ideal.

articles.title: The maximal ideal of a DVR maps into the ideal of an Eisenstein root
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial of
positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of
$X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the ideal of $A[X]/(f)$ generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ is
contained in the principal ideal $(\alpha)$.

articles.title: The constant term of an Eisenstein polynomial generates the maximal ideal of a DVR
articles.statement:
Let
$A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a
polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then
$\mathfrak m$ is the principal ideal generated by the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$.

articles.title: Eisenstein criterion for total ramification of discrete valuation rings
articles.statement:
Let $A \subseteq B$
be an extension of discrete valuation rings with $B$ finite over $A$ and the inclusion a local
homomorphism, and let $K \subseteq L$ be their fraction fields, with $L$ finite over $K$ and the
maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$ agreeing. For a uniformizer $\pi$ of $B$, the ramification
index of the maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$ equals $[L : K]$ if and only if $B = A[\pi]$ and the
minimal polynomial of $\pi$ over $A$ is Eisenstein at the maximal ideal of $A$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Theorem 11.5 (Sutherland, MIT 18.785, Lecture 11).

articles.title: A generating uniformizer gives total ramification
articles.statement:
Let $A \subseteq B$ be an extension of
discrete valuation rings with $B$ finite over $A$ and the inclusion a local homomorphism, and let
$K \subseteq L$ be their fraction fields, with the maps $A \to B \to L$ and $A \to K \to L$
agreeing. If a uniformizer $\pi$ of $B$ satisfies $B = A[\pi]$, then the ramification index of the
maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$ equals $[L : K]$.

The proof shows that the inertia degree $f$ of the maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$ is $1$ and applies
the identity $[L : K] = ef$, where $e$ is the ramification index.

articles.title: An Eisenstein generating uniformizer gives total ramification
articles.statement:
Let $A \subseteq B$ be an
extension of discrete valuation rings with $B$ finite over $A$ and the inclusion a local
homomorphism, and let $K \subseteq L$ be their fraction fields, with the maps $A \to B \to L$ and
$A \to K \to L$ agreeing. If a uniformizer $\pi$ of $B$ satisfies $B = A[\pi]$ and its minimal
polynomial over $A$ is Eisenstein at the maximal ideal of $A$, then the ramification index of the
maximal ideal of $B$ over $A$ equals $[L : K]$.

The Eisenstein hypothesis is not used: a generating uniformizer already suffices.

articles.title: Every maximal ideal of an Eisenstein extension of a DVR contains the root
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a
discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial
that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in
$A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha$ lies in every maximal ideal of $A[X]/(f)$.

articles.title: The adjoined root of an Eisenstein polynomial is nonzero
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local integral
domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $f \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial of positive degree
that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in
$A[X]/(f)$. Then $\alpha \neq 0$.

articles.title: Lifting residue-field isomorphisms between Henselian étale DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$,
$C$ be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure maps are local
homomorphisms, both étale over $A$ and both Henselian local rings. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the
residue field of a local ring $R$. Then every $\kappa(A)$-algebra isomorphism
$e \colon \kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ lifts to an $A$-algebra isomorphism $e' \colon B \to C$: the
map that $e'$ induces on residue fields is $e$, and the map that $e'^{-1}$ induces is $e^{-1}$.

articles.title: Algebra maps from an étale DVR extension into a Henselian one match residue-field maps
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure
maps are local homomorphisms, $B$ étale over $A$, and $C$ a Henselian local ring. Write
$\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Then sending an $A$-algebra homomorphism
$B \to C$ to the $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism $\kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ it induces is a
bijection.

articles.title: Lifting residue-field isomorphisms between complete étale DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$
be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure maps are local
homomorphisms, both étale over $A$, and both complete and separated for their maximal-ideal-adic
topologies. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Then every
$\kappa(A)$-algebra isomorphism $e \colon \kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ lifts to an $A$-algebra
isomorphism $e' \colon B \to C$: the map that $e'$ induces on residue fields is $e$, and the map
that $e'^{-1}$ induces is $e^{-1}$.

articles.title: Algebra maps from an étale DVR extension into a complete one match residue-field maps
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure
maps are local homomorphisms, $B$ étale over $A$, and $C$ complete and separated for its
maximal-ideal-adic topology. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Then
sending an $A$-algebra homomorphism $B \to C$ to the $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism
$\kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ it induces is a bijection.

articles.title: Lifting residue-field images to roots of a minimal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings with $B$ a finite étale $A$-algebra whose structure map is local, and
let $C$ be a Henselian local ring that is an $A$-algebra whose structure map is local. Write
$k_A$, $k_B$, $k_C$ for the residue fields. Let $\beta \in B$ generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra,
and let $\bar\beta \in k_B$ be its residue class. Then for every $k_A$-algebra homomorphism
$f : k_B \to k_C$ there is $\gamma \in C$ that is a root of the minimal polynomial of $\beta$
over $A$ and whose residue class in $k_C$ is $f(\bar\beta)$.

articles.title: Lifting residue-field homomorphisms of finite étale DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be
discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ finite $A$-algebras whose structure maps are local,
$B$ étale over $A$ and $C$ Henselian. Write $k_A$, $k_B$, $k_C$ for the residue fields. Then
every $k_A$-algebra homomorphism $k_B \to k_C$ is induced by an $A$-algebra homomorphism: the
map sending an $A$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi : B \to C$ to the induced homomorphism of
residue fields $k_B \to k_C$, $\bar b \mapsto \overline{\varphi(b)}$, is surjective.

articles.title: Monic lifts of irreducible residue polynomials give DVRs
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation
ring with residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial whose reduction
$\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$ is irreducible. If $A[X]/(g)$ is an integral
domain and a local ring, then $A[X]/(g)$ is a discrete valuation ring.

articles.title: Local base map for polynomials with irreducible reduction
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with
residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a polynomial whose reduction $\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo
the maximal ideal of $A$ is irreducible. If $A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, then the canonical map
$A \to A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring homomorphism: an element of $A$ whose image in $A[X]/(g)$ is a
unit is itself a unit.

articles.title: Monic polynomials with irreducible reduction give local rings
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring
with residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial whose reduction
$\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$ is irreducible. Then $A[X]/(g)$ is a local
ring.

articles.title: The extended maximal ideal is maximal for irreducible reduction
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a polynomial whose
reduction $\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is irreducible. Then the ideal of $A[X]/(g)$
generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ under the canonical map $A \to A[X]/(g)$ is maximal.

articles.title: Reducing $R(X)/(g)$ modulo the maximal ideal of $R$
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$, let $g \in R[X]$, and let $\bar g \in k[X]$ be a
polynomial equal to the reduction of $g$ modulo $\mathfrak m$. This is the canonical ring
isomorphism from the quotient of $R[X]/(g)$ by the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$
onto $k[X]/(\bar g)$; it sends the class of the image of $p \in R[X]$ to the class of the
reduction $\bar p \in k[X]$.

articles.title: Finite separable residue extensions lift to finite DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring with residue field $k$, and let $L$ be a finite separable field extension of $k$.
Then there is a discrete valuation ring $B$ with an $A$-algebra structure such that $B$ is
finitely generated as an $A$-module and the structure map $A \to B$ is a local homomorphism,
together with an isomorphism of $k$-algebras between the residue field of $B$ (a $k$-algebra
via $A \to B$) and $L$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI N211, Theorem 10.13, essential-surjectivity object-construction stage only (a prerequisite, not the full N211 target): completeness and Henselianity of $A$ are not assumed, and neither full faithfulness nor the categorical equivalence is proved.

articles.title: Monic lifts of irreducible residue polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with
residue field $k$, and let $\bar g \in k[X]$ be monic and irreducible. Then there is a monic
polynomial $g \in A[X]$ whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $A$ is $\bar g$, such that
$A[X]/(g)$ is an integral domain and is finitely generated as an $A$-module.

articles.title: The maximal ideal of $A(X)/(g)$ is extended from $A$
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a polynomial whose reduction
$\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is irreducible. If $A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, then its
maximal ideal is the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ under the canonical map
$A \to A[X]/(g)$.

articles.title: The residue-field algebra isomorphism on polynomial classes
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$, let $g \in A[X]$ be a polynomial such that
$A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, the canonical map $A \to A[X]/(g)$ is a local homomorphism, and the
reduction $\bar g \in k[X]$ of $g$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is irreducible. Then for every
$p \in A[X]$, the canonical $k$-algebra isomorphism from the residue field of $A[X]/(g)$
onto $k[X]/(\bar g)$ sends the residue class of the image of $p$ in $A[X]/(g)$ to the class
of the reduction $\bar p \in k[X]$ of $p$.

articles.title: The residue field of $A(X)/(g)$ as a $k$-algebra
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a polynomial such that
$A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, the canonical map $A \to A[X]/(g)$ is a local homomorphism, and the
reduction $\bar g \in k[X]$ of $g$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ is irreducible. This is the isomorphism of
$k$-algebras from the residue field of $A[X]/(g)$ (a $k$-algebra via $A \to A[X]/(g)$) onto
$k[X]/(\bar g)$ that sends the residue class of the image of each $p \in A[X]$ to the class of its
reduction $\bar p \in k[X]$.
