articles.title: Residue field of $A(X)/(g)$ on representatives
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with residue field
$\kappa(A)$, let $g \in A[X]$ be such that $A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, and let
$\bar g \in \kappa(A)[X]$ be the reduction of $g$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$, assumed
irreducible. Then for every $p \in A[X]$, the ring isomorphism from the residue field of
$A[X]/(g)$ onto $\kappa(A)[X]/(\bar g)$ sends the residue class of the image of $p$ in $A[X]/(g)$
to the class of $\bar p$, the reduction of the coefficients of $p$ modulo the maximal ideal of
$A$.

articles.title: Residue field of $A(X)/(g)$
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa(A)$, let
$g \in A[X]$ be such that $A[X]/(g)$ is a local ring, and let $\bar g \in \kappa(A)[X]$ be the
reduction of $g$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$, assumed irreducible. This is the ring
isomorphism from the residue field of $A[X]/(g)$ onto $\kappa(A)[X]/(\bar g)$ that sends the residue
class of the image of each $p \in A[X]$ to the class of $\bar p$, the reduction of the coefficients
of $p$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$.

articles.title: Algebra maps from a DVR into a finite local DVR extension are local
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$
be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ algebras over $A$, where $C$ is finite as an
$A$-module and the structure map $A \to C$ is a local homomorphism. Then every $A$-algebra
homomorphism $B \to C$ is a local homomorphism.

articles.title: Residue-field maps determine algebra maps out of a formally unramified DVR extension
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be discrete valuation rings, with $B$ and $C$ algebras over $A$ whose structure
maps are local homomorphisms, where $C$ is finite as an $A$-module and $B$ is formally unramified
over $A$. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Then two $A$-algebra
homomorphisms $B \to C$ that induce the same $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism
$\kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ are equal.

articles.title: Induced map on residue fields of DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be discrete valuation
rings, with $B$ and $C$ algebras over $A$ whose structure maps are local homomorphisms, where $C$
is finite as an $A$-module. Write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. An
$A$-algebra homomorphism $f \colon B \to C$ induces the $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism
$\kappa(B) \to \kappa(C)$ that sends the residue class of $b \in B$ to the residue class of
$f(b)$.

articles.title: Partial residue-field equivalence for complete finite DVR extensions
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring, and write $\kappa(R)$ for the residue field of a local ring $R$. Let $B_1$ and $B_2$
be discrete valuation rings that are finite $A$-algebras with local structure maps, complete and
separated for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies, such that for $i = 1, 2$ the field
$\kappa(B_i)$ is separable over $\kappa(A)$ and $\operatorname{rank}_A B_i$ equals
$\dim_{\kappa(A)} \kappa(B_i)$. Then the following three statements hold.
(i) Sending an $A$-algebra homomorphism $B_1 \to B_2$ to the $\kappa(A)$-algebra homomorphism
$\kappa(B_1) \to \kappa(B_2)$ it induces is a bijection.
(ii) For every finite separable field extension $L$ of $\kappa(A)$ there is a discrete valuation
ring $B$ that is a finite $A$-algebra with local structure map and whose residue field
$\kappa(B)$ is isomorphic to $L$ as a $\kappa(A)$-algebra; no unramifiedness of $B$ is claimed.
(iii) Every $\kappa(A)$-algebra isomorphism $e \colon \kappa(B_1) \to \kappa(B_2)$ lifts to an
$A$-algebra isomorphism $e' \colon B_1 \to B_2$: the map that $e'$ induces on residue fields is
$e$, and the map that $e'^{-1}$ induces is $e^{-1}$.

articles.title: Hilbert's syzygy theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $M$ be a
finitely generated module over the polynomial ring $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ in $n$ variables. Then
$M$ has projective dimension at most $n$ in the category of $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$-modules.

## Sources

- D. Hilbert, Math. Ann. 36 (1890) 473–534 finite free resolution length ≤n; Lang, Algebra; Lean states field case `k[X₁, …, Xₙ]` with `HasProjectiveDimensionLE n` and n=0 field case.

articles.title: Base change of a homogeneous element along zero evaluation
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field,
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $F$ be a multigraded free $R$-module with basis
$(b_j)_{j \in \iota}$, where each $b_j$ is homogeneous of degree $d_j \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.
Make $K$ an $R$-algebra through the zero evaluation $R \to K$, which sends every
variable to $0$. If $x \in F$ is homogeneous of degree $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, then
$1 \otimes x \in K \otimes_R F$ lies in the $K$-linear span of the vectors $1 \otimes b_j$
with $d_j = \alpha$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 862–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>, which split a graded free resolution and take the degree-`α` component after tensoring with `K`.

articles.title: Multidegree decomposition of the base-changed resolution
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained
from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation $R \to K$ at $x = 0$, and for
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ call the $K$-span of the vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree
$\alpha$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$. For every $i \ge 0$, this is the
decomposition of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$ as the internal direct sum of its degree-$\alpha$ pieces
over $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.

## Sources

- Braun-Davis, JIS 23 (2020), lines 856-867. See https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex

articles.title: Finite bases give finite-dimensional multidegree pieces
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained
from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation $R \to K$ at $x = 0$. If $\iota_i$ is finite,
then for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$, the
$K$-span of the vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree $\alpha$, is finite-dimensional
over $K$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 862–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>.

articles.title: The base-changed differential preserves multidegree
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained
from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation $R \to K$ at $x = 0$, and for
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ call the $K$-span of the vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree
$\alpha$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$. Then for every $i \ge 0$ and every
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the differential $(K \otimes_R F)_{i+1} \to (K \otimes_R F)_i$ maps
the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_{i+1}$ into the degree-$\alpha$ piece of
$(K \otimes_R F)_i$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 862–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>.

articles.title: Multidegree component complex of the base-changed resolution
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained
from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation $R \to K$ at $x = 0$, and for
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ call the $K$-span of the vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree
$\alpha$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$. The degree-$\alpha$ complex is the
chain complex of $K$-vector spaces whose term in homological degree $i$ is the degree-$\alpha$
piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$ and whose differentials are the restrictions of the differentials
of $K \otimes_R F$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 864–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>.

articles.title: Inclusion of a multidegree component complex
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained
from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation $R \to K$ at $x = 0$, and for
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ call the $K$-span of the vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree
$\alpha$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$. The inclusion of the degree-$\alpha$
complex is the chain map from the degree-$\alpha$ complex of $K \otimes_R F$ to $K \otimes_R F$
whose component in each homological degree $i$ is the inclusion of the degree-$\alpha$ piece of
$(K \otimes_R F)_i$ into $(K \otimes_R F)_i$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 864–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>.

articles.title: Injectivity of the base-changed degree inclusion
articles.statement:
Each component of the degree inclusion is injective. Source:
Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of
Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 864–867,
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex`.

articles.title: Existence of multigraded base-change data
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, and let $F$ be a
multigraded free resolution of $M$ whose term $F_i$ has the homogeneous basis
$(e_j)_{j \in \iota_i}$, where every index set $\iota_i$ is finite. Write $K \otimes_R F$ for the
chain complex of $K$-vector spaces obtained from $F$ by extending scalars along the evaluation
$R \to K$ at $x = 0$, and for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ call the $K$-span of the vectors
$1 \otimes e_j$ with $e_j$ of degree $\alpha$ the degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$.
Then multigraded base-change data for $F$ exist: each $(K \otimes_R F)_i$ is the direct sum of
its degree-$\alpha$ pieces over $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the differentials of $K \otimes_R F$
preserve these pieces, and for every $\alpha$ there is a chain complex $C^\alpha$ of $K$-vector
spaces with finite-dimensional homology in every degree, together with a chain map
$C^\alpha \to K \otimes_R F$ that is injective in each homological degree $i$ with image the
degree-$\alpha$ piece of $(K \otimes_R F)_i$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), lines 862–867, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>.

articles.title: Range of the base-changed degree inclusion
articles.statement:
Each component of the degree inclusion has range exactly the
degree piece `baseChangedDegreePiece`. Source: Benjamin Braun and
Brian Davis, "Antichain Simplices," Journal of Integer Sequences 23
(2020), lines 864–867,
`https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex`.

articles.title: Existence of finite multigraded free resolutions
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be a multigraded $R$-module that is finitely generated over
$R$. Then there are a projective resolution $P_\bullet \to M$ over $R$, index types $\iota_i$ for
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, a multigraded free resolution structure on $P_\bullet$ for the given grading
of $M$ in which $P_i$ has basis indexed by $\iota_i$, and a number $b \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
every $\iota_i$ is finite and $\iota_i$ is empty for every $i > b$.

The proof uses stagewise minimal homogeneous free covers, the determinant trick,
dimension shifting, and Hilbert's syzygy theorem.

## Sources

- Hoffman–Wang, https://export.arxiv.org/e-print/math/0601101v1 lines 592-612 (finite free graded resolution). The Braun–Davis JIS passage https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex lines 856-876 supplies the motivating Hilbert-syzygy / Poincaré-series context only. No `≤ n` bound is claimed here.

articles.title: Finite homogeneous generating sets
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$,
and let $M$ be a multigraded polynomial module over $R$, with degree-$\alpha$ components
$M_\alpha$ for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, that is finitely generated as an $R$-module. Then
there is a finite set $s \subseteq M$ of homogeneous elements, each lying in $M_\alpha$ for some
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, that generates $M$ as an $R$-module.

## Sources

- Braun-Davis, JIS 23 (2020), span 856-877; see https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex

articles.title: Betti numbers agree across comparable resolutions
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with two
multigraded free resolutions, each equipped with multigraded base change data, whose
degree-$\alpha$ component complexes are $C^\alpha$ and $D^\alpha$ for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.
If the two are related by a multigraded resolution comparison, that is, for every $\alpha$
a chain-homotopy equivalence between $C^\alpha$ and $D^\alpha$, then the multigraded Betti
numbers defined by the two base change data agree in every multidegree
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ and every homological index $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, “Antichain Simplices,” Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>, exact lines 866--874. This is conditional only: it assumes the comparison and claims no existence, uniqueness, minimality, finite support, Poincaré polynomiality or rationality, or Hilbert syzygy.

articles.title: Multigraded resolution comparison
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$,
and let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with two multigraded free resolutions,
each equipped with multigraded base change data, whose degree-$\alpha$ component complexes
are $C^\alpha$ and $D^\alpha$ for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. A comparison between the two
base change data is a choice, for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, of a chain-homotopy
equivalence between $C^\alpha$ and $D^\alpha$.

A homotopy equivalence, rather than a bare quasi-isomorphism, is the comparison-theorem
input: it induces an isomorphism on homology. Existence and uniqueness of such a
comparison are not claimed here.

articles.title: Betti numbers do not depend on the choice of base change data
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field,
let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with a fixed
multigraded free resolution $P_\bullet \to M$. Any two choices of multigraded base change
data for $P_\bullet$ define the same multigraded Betti numbers, in every multidegree
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ and every homological index $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, “Antichain Simplices,” Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>, exact lines 866--874. This covers only the fixed-resolution coherence step; independence across resolutions, finite support, Poincaré polynomiality, and Hilbert syzygy are deliberately not claimed here.

articles.title: Base change of a resolution to the residue field
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Given a projective resolution
$P_\bullet \to M$ over $R$, its base change is the chain complex of $K$-vector spaces
$K \otimes_R P_\bullet$, indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ with differentials lowering the index,
obtained by extending scalars termwise along the augmentation $R \to K$ that sends every
variable to $0$: its $i$th term is $K \otimes_R P_i$ and its differentials are the maps
$\mathrm{id}_K \otimes d$ for the differentials $d$ of $P_\bullet$.

articles.title: Degree pieces of the base-changed resolution
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with a
multigraded free resolution $P_\bullet \to M$, in which each $P_i$ has an $R$-basis
$(e_j)_{j \in J_i}$ with $e_j$ homogeneous of degree $\deg e_j \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. For
$i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the degree-$\alpha$ piece of the $i$th
term $K \otimes_R P_i$ of the base-changed complex is the $K$-subspace spanned by the
vectors $1 \otimes e_j$ with $j \in J_i$ and $\deg e_j = \alpha$.

articles.title: Multigraded base change data
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$,
and let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with a multigraded free resolution
$P_\bullet \to M$. Write $K \otimes_R P_\bullet$ for its base change along the
augmentation $R \to K$ and $(K \otimes_R P_i)_\beta$ for the degree-$\beta$ piece of its
$i$th term. Multigraded base change data for $P_\bullet$ consist of: for each
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, a decomposition of $K \otimes_R P_i$ as the internal direct sum of the
pieces $(K \otimes_R P_i)_\beta$ over $\beta \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, such that for all $i$ and
$\beta$ the differential $K \otimes_R P_{i+1} \to K \otimes_R P_i$ maps
$(K \otimes_R P_{i+1})_\beta$ into $(K \otimes_R P_i)_\beta$; and, for each
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, an $\mathbb{N}$-indexed chain complex $C^\alpha$ of
$K$-vector spaces with a chain map $C^\alpha \to K \otimes_R P_\bullet$ whose $i$th
component is injective with image $(K \otimes_R P_i)_\alpha$ for every $i$, such that
every homology $H_i(C^\alpha)$ exists and is finite-dimensional over $K$.

articles.title: Multigraded Betti number
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and
let $M$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^n$-graded $R$-module with a multigraded free resolution
$P_\bullet \to M$. Fix multigraded base change data for $P_\bullet$; for each
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ they supply a chain complex $C^\alpha$ of $K$-vector spaces
embedded in the base-changed complex $K \otimes_R P_\bullet$ with image its degree-$\alpha$
pieces. For $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ and $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the multigraded Betti number
of $M$ in multidegree $\alpha$ and homological index $i$, with respect to these data, is
the dimension over $K$ of the homology $H_i(C^\alpha)$.

articles.title: Augmentation of the polynomial ring
articles.statement:
For a field $K$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the
augmentation $K[x_1, \dots, x_n] \to K$ is the ring homomorphism sending each polynomial
$p$ to its value $p(0, \dots, 0)$: it is the identity on constants and sends every
variable to $0$.

articles.title: Degree-zero homomorphisms of multigraded modules
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ and $N$ be multigraded $R$-modules with homogeneous pieces
$M_\alpha$ and $N_\alpha$ for $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. An $R$-linear map $f : M \to N$ is
degree-zero when $f(M_\alpha) \subseteq N_\alpha$ for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.

articles.title: Multigraded free module
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let
$\iota$ be an index type. A multigraded free module structure on an $R$-module $F$ consists of a
multigraded $R$-module structure on $F$, with homogeneous pieces $F_\alpha$ for
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, together with an $R$-basis $(b_j)_{j \in \iota}$ of $F$ and a degree
$d_j \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ for each $j \in \iota$ such that $b_j \in F_{d_j}$ for every
$j \in \iota$.

articles.title: Multigraded free resolution
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be
a multigraded $R$-module, let $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to M$ be a projective resolution of $M$
over $R$, and for each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\iota_i$ be an index type. A multigraded free
resolution structure on this resolution consists of a multigraded free module structure on each
$P_i$ with basis indexed by $\iota_i$, such that every differential $P_{i+1} \to P_i$ and the
augmentation $P_0 \to M$ are degree-zero for these gradings and the given grading of $M$.

Each $P_i$ is regarded as a $K$-vector space by restricting scalars along $K \to R$.

articles.title: Coefficients of the multigraded Poincaré polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ be base-change data
for a multigraded free resolution $F_\bullet$ of $M$ in which $F_i$ has a homogeneous basis
indexed by a finite set $\iota_i$, with $\iota_i$ empty for every $i > b$ for a fixed
$b \in \mathbb{N}$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the coefficient
at $(i, \alpha)$ of the multigraded Poincaré polynomial of $D$ is the multigraded Betti number
$\beta_{i,\alpha}(D)$ of $D$ in homological degree $i$ and multidegree $\alpha$.

articles.title: Multigraded Poincaré polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let
$M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ be base-change data for a multigraded free
resolution $F_\bullet$ of $M$ in which $F_i$ has a homogeneous basis indexed by a finite set
$\iota_i$, with $\iota_i$ empty for every $i > b$ for a fixed $b \in \mathbb{N}$. The
multigraded Poincaré polynomial of $D$ is the element of the monoid algebra
$\mathbb{N}[\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{Z}^n]$ whose coefficient at $(i, \alpha)$ is the
multigraded Betti number $\beta_{i,\alpha}(D)$ of $D$ in homological degree $i$ and multidegree
$\alpha$; the hypotheses on the $\iota_i$ make these coefficients finitely supported.

articles.title: Multigraded Poincaré coefficients are Betti numbers
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ be base-change data
for a multigraded free resolution of $M$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and
$\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the multigraded Poincaré coefficient family of $D$ takes the value
$\beta_{i,\alpha}(D)$ at $(i, \alpha)$, where $\beta_{i,\alpha}(D)$ is the multigraded Betti
number of $D$ in homological degree $i$ and multidegree $\alpha$.

articles.title: Resolution comparisons preserve multigraded Poincaré coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field,
let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ and $D'$ be
base-change data for two multigraded free resolutions of $M$. Given a multigraded resolution
comparison between $D$ and $D'$, that is, for every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ a chain-homotopy
equivalence between the degree-$\alpha$ component complexes of $D$ and $D'$, the multigraded
Poincaré coefficient families of $D$ and $D'$ are equal.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, “Antichain Simplices,” Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>, exact lines 870--874. This is conditional only: it assumes the comparison and claims no existence, unconditional independence, finite support, polynomiality, rationality, or convergence.

articles.title: Multigraded Poincaré coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let
$M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ be base-change data for a multigraded free
resolution of $M$. The multigraded Poincaré coefficient family of $D$ is the function
$\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{Z}^n \to \mathbb{N}$ sending $(i, \alpha)$ to the multigraded Betti
number $\beta_{i,\alpha}(D)$ of $D$ in homological degree $i$ and multidegree $\alpha$.

A plain function records every coefficient without asserting finite
support, convergence, polynomiality, or rationality.

articles.title: Finite support of the multigraded Poincaré coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let
$R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, let $M$ be a multigraded $R$-module, and let $D$ be base-change data
for a multigraded free resolution $F_\bullet$ of $M$ in which $F_i$ has a homogeneous basis
indexed by $\iota_i$. Suppose every $\iota_i$ is finite and, for some $b \in \mathbb{N}$,
$\iota_i$ is empty for every $i > b$. Then the multigraded Poincaré coefficient family of $D$ is
nonzero at only finitely many $(i, \alpha) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{Z}^n$.

## Sources

- Benjamin Braun and Brian Davis, “Antichain Simplices,” Journal of Integer Sequences 23 (2020), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL23/Braun/braun4.tex>, exact line 876. This is the conditional finite-resolution bridge behind that line, not the full Hilbert syzygy existence theorem: it assumes the finite terminating resolution and derives finite coefficient support, without assuming finite support, eventual Betti vanishing, or a polynomial realization, and without constructing the resolution.

articles.title: Multigraded modules over a polynomial ring
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $n \in \mathbb{N}$
and $R = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and let $M$ be an $R$-module that is also a $K$-vector
space. A $\mathbb{Z}^n$-grading of $M$ compatible with monomial multiplication consists of
$K$-subspaces $M_\alpha \subseteq M$, one for each $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, such that $M$
is the direct sum of the $M_\alpha$, the action of each $k \in K$ on $M$ agrees with
multiplication by the constant polynomial $k \in R$, and for every $a \in \mathbb{N}^n$,
every $c \in K$ and every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, multiplication by the monomial
$c x^a = c x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_n^{a_n}$ maps $M_\alpha$ into $M_{\alpha + a}$, where $a$ is
viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Z}^n$.

articles.title: Exponent vectors as integer vectors
articles.statement:
For an exponent vector
$a = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{N}^n$ of a monomial, this is the vector
$(a_1, \dots, a_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ obtained by viewing each entry $a_i$ as an integer.

articles.title: Power series over a DVR modulo $X - \varpi$ form a complete DVR
articles.statement:
Modulo `X - ϖ`, a power series ring over a discrete valuation ring is a
discrete valuation ring, adically complete at its maximal ideal, with
uniformizer the image of `ϖ`.

articles.title: Power series over a DVR modulo $X - \varpi^e$ form a DVR
articles.statement:
Modulo `X - ϖ ^ e`, a power series ring over a discrete valuation ring is a
discrete valuation ring, with uniformizer the image of `ϖ`.

articles.title: Power series over a DVR modulo $X - \varpi^e$ form a local PID
articles.statement:
Modulo `X - ϖ ^ e`, a power series ring over a discrete valuation ring
is a principal ideal ring and a local ring, and the image of `ϖ` is
irreducible.

articles.title: Valuation subring at a height-one prime of a normal domain
articles.statement:
At a height-one prime of a Noetherian integrally closed domain, there
is a principal ideal valuation subring of the fraction field whose
membership is the usual numerator-denominator criterion.

articles.title: Localization at a height-one prime is a DVR
articles.statement:
In a Noetherian integrally closed domain, the localization at a
height-one prime ideal is a discrete valuation ring.

articles.title: Maximal ideals contract to the maximal ideal of a complete base
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
commutative rings with $B$ an $A$-algebra that is integral over $A$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be a
maximal ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $\mathfrak p$-adically complete. Then every maximal ideal
$Q$ of $B$ has preimage $\mathfrak p$ under the structure map $A \to B$.

articles.title: Finitely many DVR points with trivial common kernel
articles.statement:
A finite torsion-free local reduced algebra over an adically complete DVR
with finite residue field and characteristic zero admits finitely many
adically complete DVR points whose kernels intersect to `⊥`, with a common
denominator clearing all denominators.

articles.title: Exactly one prime lies over the maximal ideal of a complete DVR
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, $K$ its fraction
field, $L$ a finite separable extension of $K$, and $B$ the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. Then
there is exactly one prime ideal of $B$ whose preimage under $A \to B$ is $\mathfrak m$.

articles.title: Integral closure of a complete DVR in a separable extension
articles.statement:
The integral closure of a complete discrete valuation ring in a finite
separable extension of its fraction field is finite over the base, is a
discrete valuation ring, and is complete for its maximal ideal.

articles.title: Valuation rings dominating a complete DVR are integral closures
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal, $K$ its fraction field, and
$L$ a finite separable extension of $K$. Let $v$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in a linearly
ordered commutative group with zero, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_v = \{x \in L : v(x) \le 1\}$.
Suppose $\mathcal O_v$ is an $A$-algebra such that the composite $A \to \mathcal O_v \subseteq L$
is the structure map $A \to L$, and $A \to \mathcal O_v$ is a local homomorphism. Then
$\mathcal O_v$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $L$.

articles.title: Completeness passes to finite extensions of discrete valuation rings
articles.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be
discrete valuation rings, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an
$A$-module and whose structure map $A \to B$ is injective. If $A$ is complete and Hausdorff for
the adic topology of its maximal ideal, then $B$ is complete and Hausdorff for the adic topology
of its maximal ideal.

## Sources

- generalizes `integral_closure_isAdicComplete` (atlas-lean v1) from the integral closure to any finite faithful extension of DVRs.

articles.title: The integral closure of a complete DVR is complete
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring
that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal, $K$ its fraction field, $L$ a finite separable
extension of $K$, and $B$ the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. If $B$ is local (as it always is
here), then $B$ is complete with respect to its maximal ideal.

## Sources

- ATLAS `integral_closure_isAdicComplete`, obtained here from the general completeness theorem for finite local extensions.

articles.title: The integral closure of a complete DVR is a DVR
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring
that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal, $K$ its fraction field and $L$ a finite
separable extension of $K$. Then the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ is a discrete valuation
ring.

articles.title: The integral closure of a complete DVR is local
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring
that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal, $K$ its fraction field and $L$ a finite
separable extension of $K$. Then the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ is a local ring.

articles.title: Domains integral over a complete local domain are local
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an integral domain
and $\mathfrak p$ a maximal ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $\mathfrak p$-adically complete. If $B$
is an integral domain and an $A$-algebra that is integral over $A$, then $B$ is a local ring.

articles.title: Valuation rings dominating a complete DVR are finite over it
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete
valuation ring that is complete with respect to its maximal ideal, $K$ its fraction field, and
$L$ a finite separable extension of $K$. Let $v$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in a linearly
ordered commutative group with zero, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_v = \{x \in L : v(x) \le 1\}$.
Suppose $\mathcal O_v$ is an $A$-algebra such that the composite $A \to \mathcal O_v \subseteq L$
is the structure map $A \to L$, and $A \to \mathcal O_v$ is a local homomorphism. Then
$\mathcal O_v$ is a finitely generated $A$-module.

articles.title: Finite domains over adically complete local rings are local
articles.statement:
A finite algebra over an adically complete Noetherian local ring that is
a domain is itself local.

articles.title: Nearby roots share the derivative valuation
articles.statement: A root sufficiently close to the approximation has the same derivative valuation.

articles.title: Elements of the maximal ideal have positive valuation
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation
ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and normalized additive valuation
$v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. If $d \in A$ is nonzero and $q \in \mathfrak{m}$, then
$v(d) < v(d) + v(q)$.

Since $v(dq) = v(d) + v(q)$, multiplying a nonzero element by an element of the maximal ideal
strictly increases its valuation.

articles.title: Polynomials do not decrease the valuation of differences
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation
ring with normalized additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every
polynomial $p \in A[X]$ and all $a, a_0 \in A$, we have $v(a - a_0) \le v(p(a) - p(a_0))$.

articles.title: Uniqueness of roots near a point
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with normalized
additive valuation $v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative
$f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$. If $a, a' \in A$ are roots of $f$ with $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a - a_0)$ and
$v(f'(a_0)) < v(a' - a_0)$, then $a = a'$.

articles.title: Sections of étale algebras over Henselian local rings
articles.statement:
Over a Henselian local ring, an étale algebra has a section lifting any
residue-field point.

articles.title: Hensel's lemma with a derivative bound
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal
ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ that is complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic topology, and let
$v \colon A \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ be its normalized additive valuation. Let $f \in A[X]$
have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$ satisfy $2 v(f'(a_0)) < v(f(a_0))$. Then $f$ has a root
$a \in A$ such that $a - a_0 \in \mathfrak{m}$, $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a - a_0)$,
$v(f(a_0)) \le v(a - a_0) + 2 v(f'(a_0))$ and $v(f'(a)) = v(f'(a_0))$. Moreover, every root
$a' \in A$ of $f$ with $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a' - a_0)$ equals $a$.

## Sources

- ATLAS Hensel endpoint; the published statement dropped the condition $v(f'(a_0)) < v(a - a_0)$ on the root, which is kept here so that uniqueness applies to it.

articles.title: Hensel's lemma for complete discrete valuation rings
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ that is complete and Hausdorff for the $\mathfrak{m}$-adic
topology. Let $f \in A[X]$ have derivative $f'$, and let $a_0 \in A$ satisfy
$f(a_0) \in \mathfrak{m}$ with $f'(a_0)$ a unit of $A$. Then $f$ has a root $a \in A$ with
$a - a_0 \in \mathfrak{m}$.

articles.title: Hensel lifting of monic coprime factorizations, with degrees
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
ring and $I$ an ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete and $A/I$ is not the zero
ring, and let $f \in A[X]$ be monic. Suppose the reduction of $f$ modulo $I$ equals
$\bar g \bar h$, where $\bar g, \bar h \in (A/I)[X]$ are monic and coprime (that is,
$a \bar g + b \bar h = 1$ for some $a, b \in (A/I)[X]$). Then there exist monic $g, h \in A[X]$
with $f = gh$ whose reductions modulo $I$ are $\bar g$ and $\bar h$ respectively, and such that
$\deg g = \deg \bar g$ and $\deg h = \deg \bar h$.

articles.title: Hensel lifting of monic coprime factorizations
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I$ an
ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete, and let $f \in A[X]$ be monic. Suppose the
reduction of $f$ modulo $I$ equals $\bar g \bar h$, where $\bar g, \bar h \in (A/I)[X]$ are monic
and coprime (that is, $a \bar g + b \bar h = 1$ for some $a, b \in (A/I)[X]$). Then there exist
monic $g, h \in A[X]$ with $f = gh$ whose reductions modulo $I$ are $\bar g$ and $\bar h$
respectively.

The proof packages the residue factorization via the universal coprime factorization ring, lifts
its structure map through $I$-adic completeness, and evaluates the universal factors over $A$.

articles.title: Hensel lifting of coprime monic factors over a complete ring
articles.statement:
Coprime monic factors lift over a ring complete at the kernel of a
surjective homomorphism. The lifts are coprime, and the first is the unique
monic divisor of the original polynomial with its specified reduction.

articles.title: Unique lift of a monic factor through a nilpotent-kernel surjection
articles.statement:
A monic factor of a coprime factorization lifts uniquely through a
surjective homomorphism with nilpotent kernel. The original polynomial
and the complementary reduced factor are not required to be monic.

articles.title: Valuation subrings of algebraically closed fields are Henselian
articles.statement: A valuation subring of an algebraically closed field is Henselian.

articles.title: Local homomorphisms reflect coprimality with a monic polynomial
articles.statement:
A local ring homomorphism reflects coprimality of polynomials when the
first polynomial is monic. Neither ring needs to be local.

articles.title: Complete local rings are Henselian
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal
$\mathfrak m$. If $R$ is Hausdorff and complete for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology, then $R$
is a Henselian local ring.

articles.title: Valuation rings of one-variable function fields are PIDs
articles.statement:
A valuation subring of a function field in one variable over `K`,
containing `K` and different from the whole field, is a principal ideal
ring.

articles.title: Valuation subrings of finite extensions of dimension-one domains are DVRs
articles.statement:
A valuation subring of a finite extension of the fraction field of a
Noetherian domain of Krull dimension at most one, containing the base ring
and different from the whole field, is a discrete valuation ring.

articles.title: Krull–Akizuki theorem
articles.statement:
The Krull–Akizuki theorem: a subalgebra of a finite extension of the
fraction field of a Noetherian domain of Krull dimension at most one is
Noetherian of Krull dimension at most one, and every nonzero quotient has
finite length over the base.

articles.title: Residue fields in algebraic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ are algebraic
articles.statement:
The residue field of a valuation subring of an algebraic extension of
`ℚ` is algebraic over `𝔽_p`.

articles.title: Monic polynomials have roots in valuation subrings of closed fields
articles.statement:
A monic polynomial over a valuation subring of an algebraically closed
field, of nonzero degree, has a root in the subring: take a root in the field,
it is integral over the subring, and valuation subrings are integrally closed.

articles.title: Residue field of a valuation subring of a closed field is closed
articles.statement:
The residue field of a valuation subring of an algebraically closed field
is algebraically closed: lift a monic irreducible polynomial to the valuation
subring, take a root there, and reduce it back.

articles.title: Roots of unity under the residue map of a valuation subring
articles.statement:
The residue map is injective on `m`-th roots of unity, and every `m`-th
root of unity in the residue field lifts, when `m` is nonzero in the
residue field.
